1.112.s:
sanātana uvāca
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi tṛtīyāyā vratāni te /
yāni samyagvidhāyāśu nārī saubhāgyamāpnuyāt //
1.112.d:
सनातन उवाच
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि तृतीयाया व्रतानि ते ।
यानि सम्यग्विधायाशु नारी सौभाग्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.112.m: Sanātana said: / Listen, O Nārada! I shall declare to you the vows of the third lunar day, / by properly observing which a woman quickly attains marital felicity.

1.112.s:
caitraśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ gaurīṃ kṛtvā sabhartṛkām /
sauvarṇā rājatīṃ vāpi tāmnīṃ vā mṛṇyayīṃ dvija //
1.112.d:
चैत्रशुक्लतृतीयायां गौरीं कृत्वा सभर्तृकाम् ।
सौवर्णा राजतीं वापि ताम्नीं वा मृण्ययीं द्विज ॥
1.112.m: On the third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, having made [an image of] Gaurī with her husband, / [whether] of gold, silver, copper, or clay, O twice-born one,

1.112.s:
abhyarcya gandhapuṣpādyairvastrairābharaṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ /
dūrvākāṇḍaiśca vidhivatsopavāsā tu kanyakā //
1.112.d:
अभ्यर्च्य गन्धपुष्पाद्यैर्वस्त्रैराभरणैः शुभैः ।
दूर्वाकाण्डैश्च विधिवत्सोपवासा तु कन्यका ॥
1.112.m: having worshipped her according to rule with perfumes, flowers, and the like, with auspicious garments and ornaments, / and with stalks of dūrvā grass, an unmarried girl who fasts,

1.112.s:
varārthinī ca saubhāgyaputrabhartrarthinī tathā /
dvijabhāryā bhartṛmatīḥ kanyakāṃ vā sulakṣaṇāḥ //
1.112.d:
वरार्थिनी च सौभाग्यपुत्रभर्त्रर्थिनी तथा ।
द्विजभार्या भर्तृमतीः कन्यकां वा सुलक्षणाः ॥
1.112.m: or one seeking a husband, or likewise one desiring marital felicity, sons, and a husband, / having pleased the wives of brāhmaṇas who have living husbands, or well-omened unmarried girls,

1.112.s:
siṃdūrāñjanavastrādyaiḥ pratoṣya prītamānasā /
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kuryādvratasaṃpūrtikāmyayā //
1.112.d:
सिंदूराञ्जनवस्त्राद्यैः प्रतोष्य प्रीतमानसा ।
रात्रौ जागरणं कुर्याद्व्रतसंपूर्तिकाम्यया ॥
1.112.m: with vermilion, collyrium, garments, and other [gifts], with a delighted mind, / should keep vigil at night, desiring the completion of the vow.

1.112.s:
tatastāṃ pratimāṃ vipra gurave pratipādayet /
dhātujāṃ mṛnmayīṃ vā tu nikṣipecca jalāśaye //
1.112.d:
ततस्तां प्रतिमां विप्र गुरवे प्रतिपादयेत् ।
धातुजां मृन्मयीं वा तु निक्षिपेच्च जलाशये ॥
1.112.m: Then, O vipra, she should give that image to her guru, / or if it is made of metal or clay, cast it into a reservoir of water.

1.112.s:
evaṃ dvādaśavarṣāṇi kṛtvā gaurīvrataṃ śubham /
dhenudvādaśasaṃkalpaṃ dadyādutsargasiddhaye //
1.112.d:
एवं द्वादशवर्षाणि कृत्वा गौरीव्रतं शुभम् ।
धेनुद्वादशसंकल्पं दद्यादुत्सर्गसिद्धये ॥
1.112.m: Having thus observed the auspicious vow of Gaurī for twelve years, / she should make a resolve to donate twelve cows for the accomplishment of its completion.

1.112.s:
kimatra bahunoktena gaurī saubhāgyadāyinī /
strīṇāṃ yathā tathā nānyā vidyate bhuvanatraye //
1.112.d:
किमत्र बहुनोक्तेन गौरी सौभाग्यदायिनी ।
स्त्रीणां यथा तथा नान्या विद्यते भुवनत्रये ॥
1.112.m: What is the use of speaking much on this? Gaurī bestows marital felicity; / for women, there is none other like her in the three worlds.

1.112.s:
dhanaṃ putrānpatiṃ vidyāmājñāsiddhiṃ yaśaḥ sukham /
labhate sarvameveṣṭaṃ gaurīmabhyarcya bhaktitaḥ //
1.112.d:
धनं पुत्रान्पतिं विद्यामाज्ञासिद्धिं यशः सुखम् ।
लभते सर्वमेवेष्टं गौरीमभ्यर्च्य भक्तितः ॥
1.112.m: Wealth, sons, a husband, learning, success of command, renown, happiness— / by worshipping Gaurī with devotion, she obtains every desired thing.

1.112.s:
rādhaśuklatṛtīyā yā sākṣayā parikīrtitā /
tithistrotāyugādyā sā kṛtasyākṣayakāriṇī //
1.112.d:
राधशुक्लतृतीया या साक्षया परिकीर्तिता ।
तिथिस्त्रोतायुगाद्या सा कृतस्याक्षयकारिणी ॥
1.112.m: The third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Rādha (Vaiśākha) is proclaimed as Akṣayā (Imperishable); / that lunar day, the beginning of the Tretā age, renders imperishable whatever is performed.

1.112.s:
dve śukle dve tathā kṛṣṇe yugādī kavayo viduḥ /
śukle pūrvāhnike grāhye kṛṣṇe caiva tapastatha //
1.112.d:
द्वे शुक्ले द्वे तथा कृष्णे युगादी कवयो विदुः ।
शुक्ले पूर्वाह्निके ग्राह्ये कृष्णे चैव तपस्तथ ॥
1.112.m: Two in the bright fortnight and likewise two in the dark fortnight are known by the wise as age-beginnings (yugādis); / in the bright fortnight they are to be taken in the forenoon, and in the dark fortnight likewise [...].

1.112.s:
dvāparaṃ hi kalirbhādre pravṛttāni yugāni vai /
tatra rādhatṛtīyāyāṃ śrīsametaṃ jagadgurum //
1.112.d:
द्वापरं हि कलिर्भाद्रे प्रवृत्तानि युगानि वै ।
तत्र राधतृतीयायां श्रीसमेतं जगद्गुरुम् ॥
1.112.m: The Dvāpara and the Kali ages indeed commenced in the month of Bhādra; / there, on the third lunar day of Rādha, having worshipped the teacher of the world,

1.112.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ samabhyarcetpuṣpadhūpavilepanaiḥ /
yadvā gaṅgāṃbhasi snāto mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ //
1.112.d:
नारायणं समभ्यर्चेत्पुष्पधूपविलेपनैः ।
यद्वा गङ्गांभसि स्नातो मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ॥
1.112.m: Nārāyaṇa accompanied by Śrī, with flowers, incense, and ointments, / or having bathed in the waters of the Gaṅgā, a person is freed from all sins.

1.112.s:
akṣatnaiḥ pūjayedviṣṇuṃ snāyādapyakṣatairnaraḥ /
saktūnsaṃbhojayedviprānsvayamabhyavaharecca tān //
1.112.d:
अक्षत्नैः पूजयेद्विष्णुं स्नायादप्यक्षतैर्नरः ।
सक्तून्संभोजयेद्विप्रान्स्वयमभ्यवहरेच्च तान् ॥
1.112.m: A man should worship Viṣṇu with unbroken grains of rice and bathe with unbroken grains of rice; / he should feed the vipras with roasted barley flour and consume it himself.

1.112.s:
evaṃ kṛtavidhirvipra naro viṣṇuparāyaṇaḥ /
viṣṇulokamavāpnoti sarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ //
1.112.d:
एवं कृतविधिर्विप्र नरो विष्णुपरायणः ।
विष्णुलोकमवाप्नोति सर्वदेवनमस्कृतः ॥
1.112.m: The man who has thus performed the ritual, O vipra, devoted to Viṣṇu, / goes to the world of Viṣṇu, bowed to by all the gods.

1.112.s:
atha jyeṣṭhatṛtīyā tu śuklā raṃbheti nāmataḥ /
tasyāṃ sabhāryaṃ vidhivatpūjayedvāhmaṇottamam //
1.112.d:
अथ ज्येष्ठतृतीया तु शुक्ला रंभेति नामतः ।
तस्यां सभार्यं विधिवत्पूजयेद्वाह्मणोत्तमम् ॥
1.112.m: Now, the third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha is named Rambhā; / on it, one should worship an excellent brāhmaṇa along with his wife according to rule,

1.112.s:
gandhapuṣpāṃśukādyaistu nārī saubhāgyakāmyayā /
raṃbhāvratamidaṃ vipra vidhivatsamupāśritam //
1.112.d:
गन्धपुष्पांशुकाद्यैस्तु नारी सौभाग्यकाम्यया ।
रंभाव्रतमिदं विप्र विधिवत्समुपाश्रितम् ॥
1.112.m: with perfumes, flowers, cloths, and the like, a woman desiring marital felicity; / this Rambhā vow, O vipra, when observed according to rule,

1.112.s:
dadāti vittaṃ putrāṃśca matiṃ dharme śubhāvahām /
athāṣāḍhatṛtīyāyāṃ śuklāyāṃ śuklavāsasā //
1.112.d:
ददाति वित्तं पुत्रांश्च मतिं धर्मे शुभावहाम् ।
अथाषाढतृतीयायां शुक्लायां शुक्लवाससा ॥
1.112.m: bestows wealth, sons, and an auspicious disposition towards righteousness. / Then, on the third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, [dressed] in white garments,

1.112.s:
keśavaṃ tu salakṣmīkaṃ sastrīke tu dvijer'cayet /
bhojanaiḥ surabhīdānairvastraiścāpi vibhūṣaṇaiḥ //
1.112.d:
केशवं तु सलक्ष्मीकं सस्त्रीके तु द्विजेर्ऽचयेत् ।
भोजनैः सुरभीदानैर्वस्त्रैश्चापि विभूषणैः ॥
1.112.m: she should worship Keśava along with Lakṣmī, and a brāhmaṇa couple, / with meals, gifts of cows, garments, and ornaments,

1.112.s:
priyervākyairbhṛśaṃ prītā nārī saubhāgyavāñchayā /
samupāsya vrataṃ caitaddhanadhānyasamanvitā //
1.112.d:
प्रियेर्वाक्यैर्भृशं प्रीता नारी सौभाग्यवाञ्छया ।
समुपास्य व्रतं चैतद्धनधान्यसमन्विता ॥
1.112.m: greatly pleased, with affectionate words. A woman desiring marital felicity, / having observed this vow, endowed with wealth and grain,

1.112.s:
devadevaprasādena viṣṇulokamavāpnuyāt /
nabhaḥ śuklatṛtīyāyāṃ svarṇagaurīvrataṃ caret //
1.112.d:
देवदेवप्रसादेन विष्णुलोकमवाप्नुयात् ।
नभः शुक्लतृतीयायां स्वर्णगौरीव्रतं चरेत् ॥
1.112.m: by the grace of the God of gods, will reach the world of Viṣṇu. / On the third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Nabhas (Śrāvaṇa), she should observe the Svarṇagaurī vow.

1.112.s:
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirbhavānīmabhipūjayet /
putrāndehi dhanaṃ dehi saubhāgyaṃ dehi suvrate //
1.112.d:
उपचारैः षोडशभिर्भवानीमभिपूजयेत् ।
पुत्रान्देहि धनं देहि सौभाग्यं देहि सुव्रते ॥
1.112.m: She should worship Bhavānī with sixteen articles of worship: / 'Grant me sons, grant me wealth, grant me marital felicity, O observant goddess!

1.112.s:
anyāṃśca sarvakāmānme dehi dehi namo 'stu te /
evaṃ saṃprārthya deveśīṃ bhavānīṃ bhavasaṃyutām //
1.112.d:
अन्यांश्च सर्वकामान्मे देहि देहि नमो ऽस्तु ते ।
एवं संप्रार्थ्य देवेशीं भवानीं भवसंयुताम् ॥
1.112.m: And grant me all my other desires, grant them! Salutations to you!' / Having thus prayed to the ruler of the gods, Bhavānī, who is united with Bhava,

1.112.s:
vratasaṃpūrtikāmā tu vāyanaṃ dāpayettathā /
evaṃ ṣoḍaśavarṣāṇi kṛtvā nārī vrataṃ śubham //
1.112.d:
व्रतसंपूर्तिकामा तु वायनं दापयेत्तथा ।
एवं षोडशवर्षाणि कृत्वा नारी व्रतं शुभम् ॥
1.112.m: and desiring the completion of the vow, she should offer the sacred gift (vāyana). / Having thus performed this auspicious vow for sixteen years, a woman,

1.112.s:
udyāpanaṃ caredbhaktyā vittaśāṭhyavivarjitā /
maṇḍape maṇḍale śuddhe gaṇeśādisurārcanam //
1.112.d:
उद्यापनं चरेद्भक्त्या वित्तशाठ्यविवर्जिता ।
मण्डपे मण्डले शुद्धे गणेशादिसुरार्चनम् ॥
1.112.m: free from deceit regarding wealth, should perform the concluding rite with devotion. / Having worshipped Gaṇeśa and the other deities in an altar-pavilion upon a purified diagram,

1.112.s:
kṛtvā tāmramayaṃ pātraṃ kalaśoparivinyaset /
sauvarṇīṃ pratimāṃ tatra bhavānyāḥ pratipūjayet //
1.112.d:
कृत्वा ताम्रमयं पात्रं कलशोपरिविन्यसेत् ।
सौवर्णीं प्रतिमां तत्र भवान्याः प्रतिपूजयेत् ॥
1.112.m: she should place a copper vessel upon a sacred water-pot; / there she should worship a golden image of Bhavānī,

1.112.s:
gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ samyak tato homaṃ samācaret /
veṇupātraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ pakvānnaparipūritaiḥ //
1.112.d:
गन्धपुष्पादिभिः सम्यक् ततो होमं समाचरेत् ।
वेणुपात्रैः षोडशभिः पक्वान्नपरिपूरितैः ॥
1.112.m: duly with perfumes, flowers, and other [offerings], and then perform the fire oblation. / With sixteen bamboo baskets filled with cooked food,

1.112.s:
samarpya devyai naivedyaṃ dvijeṣvetannivedayet /
vāyanaṃ ca tataḥ paścāddadyātsaṃbandhibandhuṣu //
1.112.d:
समर्प्य देव्यै नैवेद्यं द्विजेष्वेतन्निवेदयेत् ।
वायनं च ततः पश्चाद्दद्यात्संबन्धिबन्धुषु ॥
1.112.m: having offered them as food offering to the Goddess, she should present them to the twice-born; / and then afterwards she should give the sacred gift to relatives and kin.

1.112.s:
pratimāṃ gurave dattvā dvijebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ tathā /
pūrṇaṃ labhetphalaṃ nārī vratācaraṇatatparā //
1.112.d:
प्रतिमां गुरवे दत्त्वा द्विजेभ्यो दक्षिणां तथा ।
पूर्णं लभेत्फलं नारी व्रताचरणतत्परा ॥
1.112.m: Having given the image to her guru and likewise priestly fees to the twice-born, / the woman devoted to the observance of the vow attains the full fruit.

1.112.s:
bhādraśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ vrataṃ vai hāritālakam /
kuryādbhaktyā vidhānena pādyārdhyārcana pūrvakam //
1.112.d:
भाद्रशुक्लतृतीयायां व्रतं वै हारितालकम् ।
कुर्याद्भक्त्या विधानेन पाद्यार्ध्यार्चन पूर्वकम् ॥
1.112.m: On the third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Bhādra, she should perform the vow of Hāritālikā / with devotion according to the prescribed rule, beginning with the worship of water for the feet and guest-water.

1.112.s:
tatastu kāñcane pātre rājate cāpi tāmrake /
vaiṇave mṛnmaye vāpi vinyasyānnaṃ sadakṣiṇam //
1.112.d:
ततस्तु काञ्चने पात्रे राजते चापि ताम्रके ।
वैणवे मृन्मये वापि विन्यस्यान्नं सदक्षिणम् ॥
1.112.m: Then, having placed food along with a priestly gift in a golden, / silver, copper, bamboo, or earthen vessel,

1.112.s:
saphalaṃ ca savastraṃ ca dvijāya pratipādayet /
tadante pāraṇaṃ kuryādiṣṭabandhujanaiḥ saha //
1.112.d:
सफलं च सवस्त्रं च द्विजाय प्रतिपादयेत् ।
तदन्ते पारणं कुर्यादिष्टबन्धुजनैः सह ॥
1.112.m: together with fruit and together with cloth, she should offer it to a twice-born one; / at the end of it, she should break her fast together with her cherished relatives.

1.112.s:
evaṃ kṛtavratā nārī bhuktvā bhogānmanoramān /
vratasyāsya prabhāveṇa gaurīsahacarībhavet //
1.112.d:
एवं कृतव्रता नारी भुक्त्वा भोगान्मनोरमान् ।
व्रतस्यास्य प्रभावेण गौरीसहचरीभवेत् ॥
1.112.m: A woman who has observed this vow, having enjoyed delightful pleasures, / becomes a companion of Gaurī by the power of this vow.

1.112.s:
saubhāgyadravyavastrāṇi vaṃśapātrāṇi ṣoḍaśa /
dātavyāni prayatnena brāhmaṇebhyo yathāvidhi //
1.112.d:
सौभाग्यद्रव्यवस्त्राणि वंशपात्राणि षोडश ।
दातव्यानि प्रयत्नेन ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यथाविधि ॥
1.112.m: Articles of marital felicity, garments, and sixteen bamboo vessels / should be diligently given to brāhmaṇas according to rule.

1.112.s:
anyebhyo vipravaryebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ ca prayatnataḥ /
bhūyasīṃ ca tato dadyādviprebhyo devituṣṭaye //
1.112.d:
अन्येभ्यो विप्रवर्येभ्यो दक्षिणां च प्रयत्नतः ।
भूयसीं च ततो दद्याद्विप्रेभ्यो देवितुष्टये ॥
1.112.m: And then, for the satisfaction of the Goddess, she should diligently give a generous priestly fee / to the other eminent vipras.

1.112.s:
evaṃ yā kurute nārī vrataṃ saubhāgyavarddhanam /
sā tu devīprasādena saubhāgyaṃ labhate dhruvam //
1.112.d:
एवं या कुरुते नारी व्रतं सौभाग्यवर्द्धनम् ।
सा तु देवीप्रसादेन सौभाग्यं लभते ध्रुवम् ॥
1.112.m: A woman who thus performs the vow that increases marital felicity, / surely attains marital felicity by the grace of the Goddess.

1.112.s:
yadā tṛtīyā bhādre tu hastarkṣasahitā bhavet /
hastagaurīvrataṃ nāma taduddiṣṭaṃ hi śauriṇā //
1.112.d:
यदा तृतीया भाद्रे तु हस्तर्क्षसहिता भवेत् ।
हस्तगौरीव्रतं नाम तदुद्दिष्टं हि शौरिणा ॥
1.112.m: When the third lunar day in the month of Bhādra is joined with the asterism Hasta, / that vow, named Hastagaurī, has indeed been taught by Śauri.

1.112.s:
tathā koṭīśvarī nāma vrataṃ proktaṃ pinākinā /
lakṣeśvarī caiva tathā tadvidhānamudīryate //
1.112.d:
तथा कोटीश्वरी नाम व्रतं प्रोक्तं पिनाकिना ।
लक्षेश्वरी चैव तथा तद्विधानमुदीर्यते ॥
1.112.m: Likewise, the vow named Koṭīśvarī was declared by the wielder of Pināka (Śiva), / as well as Lakṣeśvarī; its ritual procedure is now proclaimed.

1.112.s:
asyāṃ vrataṃ tu saṃgrāhyaṃ yāvadvarṣacatuṣṭayam /
upavāsena kartavyaṃ varṣe varṣe tu nārada //
1.112.d:
अस्यां व्रतं तु संग्राह्यं यावद्वर्षचतुष्टयम् ।
उपवासेन कर्तव्यं वर्षे वर्षे तु नारद ॥
1.112.m: This vow should be undertaken for a period of four years; / it must be observed by fasting year after year, O Nārada.

1.112.s:
akhaṇḍānāṃ taṇḍulānāṃ tilānāṃ vā munīsvara /
lakṣamekaṃ viśodhyātha kṣipetpayasi saṃsṛte //
1.112.d:
अखण्डानां तण्डुलानां तिलानां वा मुनीस्वर ।
लक्षमेकं विशोध्याथ क्षिपेत्पयसि संसृते ॥
1.112.m: Having purified one hundred thousand unbroken grains of rice, or sesame seeds, O lord of sages, / one should drop them into poured milk.

1.112.s:
tatpakkena tu nirmāya devyā mūrtiṃ suśomanām /
prakare gandhapuṣpāṇāṃ puṣpamālāvibhūṣitām //
1.112.d:
तत्पक्केन तु निर्माय देव्या मूर्तिं सुशोमनाम् ।
प्रकरे गन्धपुष्पाणां पुष्पमालाविभूषिताम् ॥
1.112.m: Fashioning a very beautiful image of the Goddess from that cooked [substance], / decorated with garlands of flowers upon an expanse of perfumes and flowers,

1.112.s:
saṃsthāpya pārvatīṃ tatra pūjayedbhaktibhāvitaḥ /
gandhaiḥ puṣpaistathā dhūpairdīpairnaivedyavistaraiḥ //
1.112.d:
संस्थाप्य पार्वतीं तत्र पूजयेद्भक्तिभावितः ।
गन्धैः पुष्पैस्तथा धूपैर्दीपैर्नैवेद्यविस्तरैः ॥
1.112.m: and having installed Pārvatī there, filled with devotion, one should worship her / with perfumes, flowers, and incense, with lamps and abundant food offerings,

1.112.s:
vividhaiśca phalairvipra namaskṛtya kṣamāpayet /
tato visarjayaddevīṃ jalamadhye 'tha dakṣiṇām //
1.112.d:
विविधैश्च फलैर्विप्र नमस्कृत्य क्षमापयेत् ।
ततो विसर्जयद्देवीं जलमध्ये ऽथ दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.112.m: and with various fruits, O vipra; having bowed, one should ask for forgiveness. / Then one should discharge the Goddess into the middle of the water; then,

1.112.s:
dattvā vidhijñaviprebhyo bhuñjīyācca pare dine /
iti te kathitaṃ vipra koṭilakṣeśvarīvratam //
1.112.d:
दत्त्वा विधिज्ञविप्रेभ्यो भुञ्जीयाच्च परे दिने ।
इति ते कथितं विप्र कोटिलक्षेश्वरीव्रतम् ॥
1.112.m: having given priestly fees to vipras knowledgeable in the rules, one should eat on the next day. / Thus has been declared to you, O vipra, the Koṭilakṣeśvarī vow.

1.112.s:
gaurīlokaṃ prayātyante vratasyāsya prabhāvataḥ /
iṣaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ bṛbadgaurīvrataṃ caret //
1.112.d:
गौरीलोकं प्रयात्यन्ते व्रतस्यास्य प्रभावतः ।
इषशुक्लतृतीयायां बृबद्गौरीव्रतं चरेत् ॥
1.112.m: At the end, by the power of this vow, he goes to the world of Gaurī. / On the third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Āśvina, one should perform the Bṛhadgaurīvrata.

1.112.s:
pañcavarṣaṃ vidhānena pūrvoktenaiva nārada /
ācāryaṃ pūjayedante viprānanyāndhanādibhiḥ //
1.112.d:
पञ्चवर्षं विधानेन पूर्वोक्तेनैव नारद ।
आचार्यं पूजयेदन्ते विप्रानन्यान्धनादिभिः ॥
1.112.m: For five years, O Nārada, according to the procedure stated before, / he should worship the preceptor at the end, and the other twice-born with wealth and other offerings.

1.112.s:
suvāsinīḥ pañca pūjyā vastrālaṅkāracandanaiḥ /
kañcukaiścaiva tāṭaṅkaiḥ kaṇṭhasūtrairharipriyāḥ //
1.112.d:
सुवासिनीः पञ्च पूज्या वस्त्रालङ्कारचन्दनैः ।
कञ्चुकैश्चैव ताटङ्कैः कण्ठसूत्रैर्हरिप्रियाः ॥
1.112.m: Five married women, beloved of Hari, are to be worshipped with garments, ornaments, and sandalwood paste, / with bodices, ear-rings, and necklaces.

1.112.s:
vaṃśapātrāṇi pañcaiva sūtraiḥ saṃveṣṭitāni ca /
siṃdūraṃ jīrakaṃ caiva saubhāgyadravyasaṃyutam //
1.112.d:
वंशपात्राणि पञ्चैव सूत्रैः संवेष्टितानि च ।
सिंदूरं जीरकं चैव सौभाग्यद्रव्यसंयुतम् ॥
1.112.m: Five bamboo vessels wound round with threads, / vermilion, cumin seeds, along with the articles of marital auspiciousness,

1.112.s:
godhīmapiṣṭajātaṃ ca navāpūpaṃ phalā dikam /
vāyanāni ca pañcaiva tābhyo dadyācca bhojayet //
1.112.d:
गोधीमपिष्टजातं च नवापूपं फला दिकम् ।
वायनानि च पञ्चैव ताभ्यो दद्याच्च भोजयेत् ॥
1.112.m: fresh cakes made of wheat flour, fruits, and the rest; / and he should present five ritual presents to them and feed them.

1.112.s:
arghaṃ dattvā vāyanāni paścādbhuñjīta vāgyatā /
tatphalaṃ dhārayetkaṇṭhe sarvakāmasamṛddhaye //
1.112.d:
अर्घं दत्त्वा वायनानि पश्चाद्भुञ्जीत वाग्यता ।
तत्फलं धारयेत्कण्ठे सर्वकामसमृद्धये ॥
1.112.m: Having offered arghya and given the ritual presents, she should afterwards eat, keeping silent. / She should wear that fruit upon her neck for the prosperity of all desires.

1.112.s:
tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya sālaṅkārā sakhījanaiḥ /
gītavādyayutā nadyāṃ gaurīṃ tāṃ tu visarjayet //
1.112.d:
ततः प्रातः समुत्थाय सालङ्कारा सखीजनैः ।
गीतवाद्ययुता नद्यां गौरीं तां तु विसर्जयेत् ॥
1.112.m: Then, rising in the morning, adorned, accompanied by her female companions / and accompanied by singing and instrumental music, she should dismiss that Gaurī in a river:

1.112.s:
āhūtāsi mayābhadre pūjitā ca yathā vidhi /
mama saubhāgyadānāya yatheṣṭaṃ gamyatāṃ tvayā //
1.112.d:
आहूतासि मयाभद्रे पूजिता च यथा विधि ।
मम सौभाग्यदानाय यथेष्टं गम्यतां त्वया ॥
1.112.m: “You were invoked by me, O auspicious one, and worshipped according to rule; / to grant me marital auspiciousness, go as you please!”

1.112.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ bhaktyā dvija devīprasādataḥ /
bhuktvā bhogāṃstu dehānte gaurīlokamavāpnuyāt //
1.112.d:
एवं कृत्वा व्रतं भक्त्या द्विज देवीप्रसादतः ।
भुक्त्वा भोगांस्तु देहान्ते गौरीलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.112.m: Having performed the vow thus with devotion, O twice-born, by the grace of the Goddess, / having enjoyed pleasures, he attains the world of Gaurī at the end of the body.

1.112.s:
ūrjaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ viṣṇugaurīvrataṃ caret /
pūjayitvā jagadvandyāmupacāraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ //
1.112.d:
ऊर्जशुक्लतृतीयायां विष्णुगौरीव्रतं चरेत् ।
पूजयित्वा जगद्वन्द्यामुपचारैः पृथग्विधैः ॥
1.112.m: On the third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika, one should observe the Viṣṇugaurīvrata. / Having worshipped her who is adored by the universe with various kinds of offerings,

1.112.s:
suvāsinīṃ bhojayitvā maṅgaladravyapūjitām /
visarjayetpraṇamyaināṃ viṣṇugaurīpratuṣṭaye //
1.112.d:
सुवासिनीं भोजयित्वा मङ्गलद्रव्यपूजिताम् ।
विसर्जयेत्प्रणम्यैनां विष्णुगौरीप्रतुष्टये ॥
1.112.m: and having fed a married woman honoured with auspicious items, / one should bow to her and dismiss her for the complete satisfaction of Viṣṇugaurī.

1.112.s:
mārgaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ haragaurīvrataṃ śubham /
kṛtvā pūrvavidhānena pūjayejjagadaṃbikām //
1.112.d:
मार्गशुक्लतृतीयायां हरगौरीव्रतं शुभम् ।
कृत्वा पूर्वविधानेन पूजयेज्जगदंबिकाम् ॥
1.112.m: On the third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, having performed the auspicious Haragaurīvrata / according to the previous procedure, one should worship the mother of the universe.

1.112.s:
etadvrataprabhāveṇa bhuktvā bhogānmanoramān /
devīlokaṃ samāsādya modate ca tayā saha //
1.112.d:
एतद्व्रतप्रभावेण भुक्त्वा भोगान्मनोरमान् ।
देवीलोकं समासाद्य मोदते च तया सह ॥
1.112.m: By the power of this vow, having enjoyed delightful pleasures / and reached the world of the Goddess, he rejoices together with her.

1.112.s:
pauṣaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ brahmagaurīvrataṃ caret /
pūrvoktena vidhānena pūjitāpi dvijottama //
1.112.d:
पौषशुक्लतृतीयायां ब्रह्मगौरीव्रतं चरेत् ।
पूर्वोक्तेन विधानेन पूजितापि द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.112.m: On the third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Pauṣa, one should perform the Brahmagaurīvrata. / Worshipped according to the procedure stated earlier, O best of the twice-born,

1.112.s:
brahmagaurīprasādena modate tatra saṃgatā /
māghaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ pūjyā saubhāgyasuṃdarī //
1.112.d:
ब्रह्मगौरीप्रसादेन मोदते तत्र संगता ।
माघशुक्लतृतीयायां पूज्या सौभाग्यसुंदरी ॥
1.112.m: by the grace of Brahmagaurī, one rejoices united with her there. / On the third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Māgha, Saubhāgyasundarī is to be worshipped.

1.112.s:
pūrvoktena vidhānena nālikerārghyadānataḥ /
prasannā diśati svīyaṃ lokaṃ tu vratatoṣitā //
1.112.d:
पूर्वोक्तेन विधानेन नालिकेरार्घ्यदानतः ।
प्रसन्ना दिशति स्वीयं लोकं तु व्रततोषिता ॥
1.112.m: According to the procedure stated earlier, through the offering of an arghya of coconut, / she, pleased and gratified by the vow, bestows her own world.

1.112.s:
phaālgunasya site pakṣe tṛtīyā kulasaukhyadā /
pūjitā gandhapuṣpādyaiḥ sarvamaṅgaladā bhavet //
1.112.d:
फआल्गुनस्य सिते पक्षे तृतीया कुलसौख्यदा ।
पूजिता गन्धपुष्पाद्यैः सर्वमङ्गलदा भवेत् ॥
1.112.m: The third lunar day in the bright fortnight of Phālguna bestows happiness to the family; / worshipped with fragrant perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, she becomes the giver of all blessings.

1.112.s:
sarvāsu ca tṛtīyāsu vidhiḥ sādhāraṇo mune /
devīpūjā viprapūjā dānaṃ homo visarjanam //
1.112.d:
सर्वासु च तृतीयासु विधिः साधारणो मुने ।
देवीपूजा विप्रपूजा दानं होमो विसर्जनम् ॥
1.112.m: On all the third lunar days, O sage, the procedure is common: / worship of the Goddess, worship of the twice-born, gifts, fire oblations, and ritual dismissal.

1.112.s:
ityevaṃ kathitānīha tṛtīyāyā vratāni te /
bhaktyā kṛtāni ceṣṭāṃstu kāmāndardyumanogatān //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde dvādaśamāsatṛtīyāvratakathanaṃ nāma dvādaśādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.112.d:
इत्येवं कथितानीह तृतीयाया व्रतानि ते ।
भक्त्या कृतानि चेष्टांस्तु कामान्दर्द्युमनोगतान् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे द्वादशमासतृतीयाव्रतकथनं नाम द्वादशाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.112.m:
Thus the vows of the third lunar day have been declared to you here; / performed with devotion, they grant the desired objects in the mind.

Thus ends the one hundred and twelfth chapter in the fourth quarter of the Great Narrative in the first section of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa, entitled 'Account of the Vows of the Third Lunar Day in the Twelve Months'.

1.113.s:
sanātana uvāca
śṛṇu vipraṃ pravakṣyāmi caturthyāste vratānyaham /
yāni kṛtvā narā nāryo 'bhīṣṭānkāmānavāpnuyuḥ //
1.113.d:
सनातन उवाच
शृणु विप्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि चतुर्थ्यास्ते व्रतान्यहम् ।
यानि कृत्वा नरा नार्यो ऽभीष्टान्कामानवाप्नुयुः ॥
1.113.m:
Sanātana said:
Listen, O brāhmaṇa, I shall declare to you the observances of the fourth [tithi],
by performing which men and women attain their cherished desires.

1.113.s:
caitramāsacaturthyāṃ tu vāsudevasvarūpiṇam /
gaṇapaṃ samyagabhyarcya dattvā kāñcanadakṣiṇām //
1.113.d:
चैत्रमासचतुर्थ्यां तु वासुदेवस्वरूपिणम् ।
गणपं सम्यगभ्यर्च्य दत्त्वा काञ्चनदक्षिणाम् ॥
1.113.m:
On the fourth tithi of the month of Caitra, having duly worshipped Gaṇapa,
who has the form of Vāsudeva, and having given a gift of gold

1.113.s:
viprāya viṣṇulokaṃ tu gaccheddevanamaskṛtaḥ /
vaiśākhasya caturthyāṃ tu prārthyaṃ saṃkarṣaṇāhvayam //
1.113.d:
विप्राय विष्णुलोकं तु गच्छेद्देवनमस्कृतः ।
वैशाखस्य चतुर्थ्यां तु प्रार्थ्यं संकर्षणाह्वयम् ॥
1.113.m:
to a brāhmaṇa, one goes, revered by the gods, to the world of Viṣṇu.
On the fourth tithi of Vaiśākha, the one called Saṃkarṣaṇa should be prayed to;

1.113.s:
gṛhasthadvijamukhyebhyaḥ śaṅkhaṃ dattvā vidhānavit /
prāpya saṃkarṣaṇaṃ lokaṃ modate bahukalpakam //
1.113.d:
गृहस्थद्विजमुख्येभ्यः शङ्खं दत्त्वा विधानवित् ।
प्राप्य संकर्षणं लोकं मोदते बहुकल्पकम् ॥
1.113.m:
having given a conch shell to foremost householder twice-borns, one knowing the rite,
attaining the world of Saṃkarṣaṇa, rejoices for many kalpas.

1.113.s:
jyeṣṭhamāsacaturthyāṃ tu prārcya pradyumnarūpiṇam /
phalaṃ mūlaṃ ca yuthebhyo dattvā svargaṃ labhennaraḥ //
1.113.d:
ज्येष्ठमासचतुर्थ्यां तु प्रार्च्य प्रद्युम्नरूपिणम् ।
फलं मूलं च युथेभ्यो दत्त्वा स्वर्गं लभेन्नरः ॥
1.113.m:
On the fourth tithi of the month of Jyeṣṭha, having worshipped [him] in the form of Pradyumna,
and having given fruits and roots to mendicant groups, a person attains heaven.

1.113.s:
āṣāḍhasya caturthyāṃ tu saṃprapūjyāniruddhakam /
yatibhyo 'lābupātrāṇi dattvābhīṣṭaṃ labhennaraḥ //
1.113.d:
आषाढस्य चतुर्थ्यां तु संप्रपूज्यानिरुद्धकम् ।
यतिभ्यो ऽलाबुपात्राणि दत्त्वाभीष्टं लभेन्नरः ॥
1.113.m:
On the fourth tithi of Āṣāḍha, having fully worshipped Aniruddha,
and having given gourd-vessels to ascetics, a person attains their desire.

1.113.s:
caturmūrtivratānyevaṃ kṛtvā dvādaśavatsaram /
udyāpanaṃ vidhānena kartavyaṃ phalamicchatā //
1.113.d:
चतुर्मूर्तिव्रतान्येवं कृत्वा द्वादशवत्सरम् ।
उद्यापनं विधानेन कर्तव्यं फलमिच्छता ॥
1.113.m:
Having thus performed the observances of the four forms for twelve years,
the concluding rite should be performed according to the rules by one desiring the fruit.

1.113.s:
anyajjyeṣṭhacaturthyāṃ tu satīvratamanuttamam /
kṛtvā gaṇapatermāturloke modeta tatsamam //
1.113.d:
अन्यज्ज्येष्ठचतुर्थ्यां तु सतीव्रतमनुत्तमम् ।
कृत्वा गणपतेर्मातुर्लोके मोदेत तत्समम् ॥
1.113.m:
On another fourth tithi in Jyeṣṭha is the unsurpassed Satīvrata;
having performed it, one rejoices equally in the world of the mother of Gaṇapati.

1.113.s:
tathā'ṣāḍhacaturthyāṃ tu vratamanyacchubhāvaham /
rathantarāhvakalpasya hyādibhūtaṃ dinaṃ yataḥ //
1.113.d:
तथाऽषाढचतुर्थ्यां तु व्रतमन्यच्छुभावहम् ।
रथन्तराह्वकल्पस्य ह्यादिभूतं दिनं यतः ॥
1.113.m:
Likewise, on the fourth tithi of Āṣāḍha there is another auspicious observance,
since it is the very first day of the kalpa named Rathantara.

1.113.s:
śraddhāpūtena manasā gaṇeśaṃ vidhinā naraḥ /
pūjayitvā labheccāpi phalaṃ devādidurgamam //
1.113.d:
श्रद्धापूतेन मनसा गणेशं विधिना नरः ।
पूजयित्वा लभेच्चापि फलं देवादिदुर्गमम् ॥
1.113.m:
With a mind purified by faith, a person, having worshipped Gaṇeśa
according to the rules, attains even a fruit difficult to obtain for the gods and others.

1.113.s: śrāvaṇasya caturthyāṃ tu jāti candrodaye mune //
1.113.d: श्रावणस्य चतुर्थ्यां तु जाति चन्द्रोदये मुने ॥
1.113.m: On the fourth tithi of Śrāvaṇa, O sage, upon moonrise,

1.113.s:
gaṇeśāya pradadyācca hyarghyaṃ vidhividāṃvaraḥ /
lambodaraṃ caturbāhuṃ trinetraṃ raktavarṇakam //
1.113.d:
गणेशाय प्रदद्याच्च ह्यर्घ्यं विधिविदांवरः ।
लम्बोदरं चतुर्बाहुं त्रिनेत्रं रक्तवर्णकम् ॥
1.113.m:
the best of those knowing the rites should offer water-offering to Gaṇeśa:
one should meditate on him as pot-bellied, four-armed, three-eyed, red-hued,

1.113.s:
nānāratnavibhūṣāḍhyaṃ prasannāsyaṃ vicintayet /
āvāhanādibhiḥ sarvairupacāraiḥ samarcayet //
1.113.d:
नानारत्नविभूषाढ्यं प्रसन्नास्यं विचिन्तयेत् ।
आवाहनादिभिः सर्वैरुपचारैः समर्चयेत् ॥
1.113.m:
richly adorned with various jewels, with a gracious face;
one should worship him with all the offerings, beginning with invocation.

1.113.s:
naivedyaṃ modakaṃ dadyādgaṇeśaprītidāyakam /
evaṃ vrataṃ vidhāyātha bhuktvā modakameva ca //
1.113.d:
नैवेद्यं मोदकं दद्याद्गणेशप्रीतिदायकम् ।
एवं व्रतं विधायाथ भुक्त्वा मोदकमेव च ॥
1.113.m:
One should offer sweet dumplings as food-offering, giving pleasure to Gaṇeśa.
Thus having performed the observance and then eaten sweet dumplings alone,

1.113.s:
sukhaṃ svapyānniśāyāṃ tu bhūmāveva kṛtārcanaḥ /
vratasyāsya prabhāveṇa kāmānmanasi cintitān //
1.113.d:
सुखं स्वप्यान्निशायां तु भूमावेव कृतार्चनः ।
व्रतस्यास्य प्रभावेण कामान्मनसि चिन्तितान् ॥
1.113.m:
one who has performed the worship should sleep comfortably at night upon the ground alone.
By the power of this observance, having obtained the desires thought of in one's mind,

1.113.s:
labdhvā leke paraṃ cāpi gaṇeśapadamāpnuyāt /
nānena sadṛśaṃ cānyadvratamasti jagattraye //
1.113.d:
लब्ध्वा लेके परं चापि गणेशपदमाप्नुयात् ।
नानेन सदृशं चान्यद्व्रतमस्ति जगत्त्रये ॥
1.113.m:
one also attains the supreme world, the abode of Gaṇeśa.
There is no other observance equal to this in the three worlds;

1.113.s:
tasmātkāryaṃ prayatnena sarvānkāmānabhīpsatā /
athāsminneva divase dūrvāgaṇapati vratam //
1.113.d:
तस्मात्कार्यं प्रयत्नेन सर्वान्कामानभीप्सता ।
अथास्मिन्नेव दिवसे दूर्वागणपति व्रतम् ॥
1.113.m:
therefore, it must be performed with effort by one desiring all wishes.
Now, on this very day, the Dūrvāgaṇapati observance

1.113.s:
kecidicchanti devarṣe tadvidhānaṃ vadāmi te /
haimaṃ nirmāya gaṇapaṃ tāmrapātropari sthitam //
1.113.d:
केचिदिच्छन्ति देवर्षे तद्विधानं वदामि ते ।
हैमं निर्माय गणपं ताम्रपात्रोपरि स्थितम् ॥
1.113.m:
is desired by some, O divine sage; I shall tell you its procedure:
having made a golden Gaṇapa placed upon a copper vessel,

1.113.s:
veṣṭitaṃ raktavastreṇa sarvatobhadramaṇḍale /
pūjayedraktakusumaiḥ patrikābhiśca pañcabhiḥ //
1.113.d:
वेष्टितं रक्तवस्त्रेण सर्वतोभद्रमण्डले ।
पूजयेद्रक्तकुसुमैः पत्रिकाभिश्च पञ्चभिः ॥
1.113.m:
wrapped in red cloth, upon a sarvatobhadra diagram,
one should worship him with red flowers and five leaves:

1.113.s:
bilvapatramapāmārgaṃ śamī dūrvā haripriyā /
ābhiranyaśca kusumairabhyarcya phalamodakaiḥ //
1.113.d:
बिल्वपत्रमपामार्गं शमी दूर्वा हरिप्रिया ।
आभिरन्यश्च कुसुमैरभ्यर्च्य फलमोदकैः ॥
1.113.m:
bilva leaf, apāmārga, śamī, dūrvā, [and] Tulasī.
Having worshipped with these and other flowers, fruits, and sweet dumplings,

1.113.s:
ācāryāya vidhijñāya satkṛtya vinivedayet /
upahāraṃ prakalpyātha dadyādarghaṃ samudyate /
tataḥ saṃprārathya vighneśamūrtiṃ sopaskarāṃ mune //
1.113.d:
आचार्याय विधिज्ञाय सत्कृत्य विनिवेदयेत् ।
उपहारं प्रकल्प्याथ दद्यादर्घं समुद्यते ।
ततः संप्रारथ्य विघ्नेशमूर्तिं सोपस्करां मुने ॥
1.113.m:
having arranged the offerings, one should present the water-offering when [the moon] has risen.
Then, having prayed to the image of the Lord of Obstacles along with its paraphernalia, O sage,

1.113.s:
ācāryāya vidhijñāya satkṛtya vinivedayet /
kṛtvaivaṃ pañca varṣāṇi samupāsya yathāvidhi //
1.113.d:
आचार्याय विधिज्ञाय सत्कृत्य विनिवेदयेत् ।
कृत्वैवं पञ्च वर्षाणि समुपास्य यथाविधि ॥
1.113.m:
one should respectfully dedicate it to a preceptor who knows the rites.
Having thus worshipped according to the rules for five years,

1.113.s:
bhuktveha bhogānakhilān lokaṃ gaṇapatervrajet /
atha bhādracaturthyāṃ tu bahulādhenusaṃjñakam //
1.113.d:
भुक्त्वेह भोगानखिलान् लोकं गणपतेर्व्रजेत् ।
अथ भाद्रचतुर्थ्यां तु बहुलाधेनुसंज्ञकम् ॥
1.113.m:
after enjoying all worldly pleasures here, one goes to the world of Gaṇapati.
Now, on the fourth tithi of Bhādra, [the cow] named the Bahulā cow

1.113.s:
pūjanī yo 'tra yatnena sraggandhayavasādibhiḥ /
tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya śaktaśceddānamācaret //
1.113.d:
पूजनी यो ऽत्र यत्नेन स्रग्गन्धयवसादिभिः ।
ततः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य शक्तश्चेद्दानमाचरेत् ॥
1.113.m:
should be worshipped here with effort, with garlands, perfumes, barley, and the like.
Then, having circumambulated it, one should make a gift if capable.

1.113.s:
aśaktaḥ puretāṃ tu namaskṛtya visarjayet /
pañcābdaṃ vādaśābdaṃ vā ṣoḍaśābdamathāpi vā //
1.113.d:
अशक्तः पुरेतां तु नमस्कृत्य विसर्जयेत् ।
पञ्चाब्दं वादशाब्दं वा षोडशाब्दमथापि वा ॥
1.113.m:
If incapable, having bowed to her, one should dismiss her.
Having performed the observance for five years, or twelve years, or even sixteen years,

1.113.s:
vrataṃ kṛtvā samudyāpya dhenuṃ dadyātpayasvinīm /
prabhāveṇa vratasyāsya bhuktvā bhogānmanoramān //
1.113.d:
व्रतं कृत्वा समुद्याप्य धेनुं दद्यात्पयस्विनीम् ।
प्रभावेण व्रतस्यास्य भुक्त्वा भोगान्मनोरमान् ॥
1.113.m:
and having concluded it properly, one should donate a milch cow.
By the power of this observance, having enjoyed delightful pleasures,

1.113.s:
satkṛto devatāvṛndairgolokaṃ samavāpnuyāt /
atha śukla caturthyāṃ tu siddhavaināyakavratam //
1.113.d:
सत्कृतो देवतावृन्दैर्गोलोकं समवाप्नुयात् ।
अथ शुक्ल चतुर्थ्यां तु सिद्धवैनायकव्रतम् ॥
1.113.m:
honoured by the hosts of gods, one attains Goloka.
Now, on the bright fourth tithi is the Siddhavināyaka observance.

1.113.s:
āvāhanādibhiḥ sarvairupacāraiḥ samarcanam /
ekāgramānaso bhūtvā dhyāyetsiddhivināyakam //
1.113.d:
आवाहनादिभिः सर्वैरुपचारैः समर्चनम् ।
एकाग्रमानसो भूत्वा ध्यायेत्सिद्धिविनायकम् ॥
1.113.m: With one-pointed mind, having performed worship through all services beginning with invocation, / one should meditate on Siddhivināyaka:

1.113.s:
ekadantaṃ śūrpakarṇaṃ gajavaktraṃ caturbhujam /
pāśāṅkuśadharaṃ devaṃ taptakāñcanasannibham //
1.113.d:
एकदन्तं शूर्पकर्णं गजवक्त्रं चतुर्भुजम् ।
पाशाङ्कुशधरं देवं तप्तकाञ्चनसन्निभम् ॥
1.113.m: single-tusked, winnowing-basket-eared, elephant-faced, four-armed, / holding a noose and a goad, divine, resembling molten gold.

1.113.s:
ekaviṃśati patrāṇi caikaviṃśatināmabhiḥ /
samarpayedbhaktiyuktastāni nāmāni vai śṛṇu //
1.113.d:
एकविंशति पत्राणि चैकविंशतिनामभिः ।
समर्पयेद्भक्तियुक्तस्तानि नामानि वै शृणु ॥
1.113.m: Endowed with devotion, one should offer twenty-one leaves / with twenty-one names; hear indeed those names:

1.113.s:
sumukhāya śamīpatraṃ gaṇādhīśāya bhṛṅgajam /
umāputrāya bailvaṃ tu dūrvāṃ gajamukhāya ca //
1.113.d:
सुमुखाय शमीपत्रं गणाधीशाय भृङ्गजम् ।
उमापुत्राय बैल्वं तु दूर्वां गजमुखाय च ॥
1.113.m: a śamī-leaf to Sumukha; one born of bhṛṅga to Gaṇādhīśa; / a bilva-leaf to the son of Umā; and dūrvā-grass to Gajamukha;

1.113.s:
laṃbodarāya badarīṃ dhattūraṃ harasūnave /
śūrpakarṇāya tulasīṃ vakratuṇḍāya śiṃbijam //
1.113.d:
लंबोदराय बदरीं धत्तूरं हरसूनवे ।
शूर्पकर्णाय तुलसीं वक्रतुण्डाय शिंबिजम् ॥
1.113.m: a jujube-leaf to Lambodara; dhattūra to the son of Hara; / tulasī to Śūrpakarṇa; pod-born [leaf] to Vakratuṇḍa;

1.113.s:
guhāgrajāyāpāmārgamekadantāya bārhatam /
herambāya tu siṃdūraṃ catirhetre ca patrajam //
1.113.d:
गुहाग्रजायापामार्गमेकदन्ताय बार्हतम् ।
हेरम्बाय तु सिंदूरं चतिर्हेत्रे च पत्रजम् ॥
1.113.m: apāmārga to Guha's elder brother; bṛhatī to Ekadanta; / red lead to Heramba, and a tree-leaf to Caturnetra;

1.113.s:
sarveśvarāyāgastyasya patraṃ prītivivarddhanam /
dūrvāyugmaṃ tato gṛhya gandhapuṣpākṣatairyutam //
1.113.d:
सर्वेश्वरायागस्त्यस्य पत्रं प्रीतिविवर्द्धनम् ।
दूर्वायुग्मं ततो गृह्य गन्धपुष्पाक्षतैर्युतम् ॥
1.113.m: the leaf of agastya, which increases love, to Sarveśvara. / Then, taking a pair of dūrvā-grass blades accompanied by perfume, flowers, and unbroken rice,

1.113.s:
pūjāṃ nivedayedbhaktiyukto modakapañcakam /
ācamayya namaskṛtya saṃprārthya ca visarjjayet //
1.113.d:
पूजां निवेदयेद्भक्तियुक्तो मोदकपञ्चकम् ।
आचमय्य नमस्कृत्य संप्रार्थ्य च विसर्ज्जयेत् ॥
1.113.m: endowed with devotion, one should offer worship, [offering] five sweetmeats. / Having sipped water, bowed down, and prayed, one should dismiss [him].

1.113.s:
vināyakasya pratimāṃ haimīṃ sopaskarāṃ mune /
nivedayecca gurave dvijebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ dadet //
1.113.d:
विनायकस्य प्रतिमां हैमीं सोपस्करां मुने ।
निवेदयेच्च गुरवे द्विजेभ्यो दक्षिणां ददेत् ॥
1.113.m: O sage, one should offer a golden image of Vināyaka, / equipped with all accessories, to the guru, and give a priestly fee to the twice-born.

1.113.s:
evaṃ kṛtārcano bhaktyā pañca varṣāṇi nārada /
upāsya labhate kāmānaihikāmuṣmikān śubhān //
1.113.d:
एवं कृतार्चनो भक्त्या पञ्च वर्षाणि नारद ।
उपास्य लभते कामानैहिकामुष्मिकान् शुभान् ॥
1.113.m: Having thus performed the worship with devotion for five years, O Nārada, / by worshipping he attains auspicious desires pertaining to this world and the next.

1.113.s:
asyāṃ caturthyāṃ śaśinaṃ na paśyecca kadācana /
paśyan mithyābhiśāpa tu labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ /
atha taddoṣanāśāya mantraṃ paurāṇikaṃ paṭhet //
1.113.d:
अस्यां चतुर्थ्यां शशिनं न पश्येच्च कदाचन ।
पश्यन् मिथ्याभिशाप तु लभते नात्र संशयः ।
अथ तद्दोषनाशाय मन्त्रं पौराणिकं पठेत् ॥
1.113.m: On this fourth [tithi], one should never look at the moon; / looking at it, one incurs false accusations, there is no doubt here. / Now, for the destruction of that fault, one should recite the Purāṇic mantra:

1.113.s:
siṃhaḥ prasenamamadhītsiṃho jāṃbavatā hataḥ /
sakumāraka mā rodīstava hyeṣa syamantakaḥ //
1.113.d:
सिंहः प्रसेनममधीत्सिंहो जांबवता हतः ।
सकुमारक मा रोदीस्तव ह्येष स्यमन्तकः ॥
1.113.m: 'The lion killed Prasena; the lion was slain by Jāmbavat. / Do not weep, O sweet child! For this Syamantaka jewel is yours.'

1.113.s: iṣaśuklacaturthyāṃ tu kaparddīśaṃ vināyakam //
1.113.d: इषशुक्लचतुर्थ्यां तु कपर्द्दीशं विनायकम् ॥
1.113.m: On the fourth [tithi] of the bright [fortnight] of Iṣa, however, [one should worship] Vināyaka, the lord of cowries:

1.113.s:
pauruṣiṇa tu sūktena pūjayedupacārakaiḥ /
akāraṇānmuṣṭigatāṃstaṇḍulānsakaparddikān //
1.113.d:
पौरुषिण तु सूक्तेन पूजयेदुपचारकैः ।
अकारणान्मुष्टिगतांस्तण्डुलान्सकपर्द्दिकान् ॥
1.113.m: one should worship with the Puruṣasūkta with the [various] services. / For no reason, rice-grains held in the fist together with cowries

1.113.s:
viprāya baṭave dadyādgandhapuṣpārcitāya ca /
taṇḍulā vaiśvadaivatyā haradaivatyamiśritāḥ //
1.113.d:
विप्राय बटवे दद्याद्गन्धपुष्पार्चिताय च ।
तण्डुला वैश्वदैवत्या हरदैवत्यमिश्रिताः ॥
1.113.m: one should give to a twice-born youth who has been worshipped with perfume and flowers. / The rice-grains are dedicated to the Viśvedevas, mixed with those dedicated to Hara:

1.113.s:
kapardigaṇanātho 'sau prīyatāṃ taiḥ samarpitaiḥ /
caturthyāṃ kārtike kṛṣṇe karakākhyaṃ vrataṃ smṛtam //
1.113.d:
कपर्दिगणनाथो ऽसौ प्रीयतां तैः समर्पितैः ।
चतुर्थ्यां कार्तिके कृष्णे करकाख्यं व्रतं स्मृतम् ॥
1.113.m: 'May that Kapardigaṇanātha be pleased by these offered [items]!' / On the fourth [tithi] in the dark [fortnight] of Kārttika, the observance named Karaka is remembered.

1.113.s:
strīṇāmevādhikāro 'tra tadvidhānamudīryate /
pūjayecca gaṇādhīśaṃ snātā strīsamalaṅkṛtā //
1.113.d:
स्त्रीणामेवाधिकारो ऽत्र तद्विधानमुदीर्यते ।
पूजयेच्च गणाधीशं स्नाता स्त्रीसमलङ्कृता ॥
1.113.m: Women alone are entitled to this; its rule is being declared: / having bathed and being adorned, a woman should worship Gaṇādhīśa.

1.113.s:
tadagre pūrṇapakvānnaṃ vinyasetkarakāndaśa /
samarpya devadevāya bhaktyā prayatamānasā //
1.113.d:
तदग्रे पूर्णपक्वान्नं विन्यसेत्करकान्दश ।
समर्प्य देवदेवाय भक्त्या प्रयतमानसा ॥
1.113.m: Before him, having placed ten vessels filled with cooked food, / having offered them to the god of gods with devotion and a restrained mind,

1.113.s:
devo me prīyatāmevamuccāryyātha samarpayet /
suvāsinībhyo viprebhyo yathākāmaṃ ca sādaram //
1.113.d:
देवो मे प्रीयतामेवमुच्चार्य्याथ समर्पयेत् ।
सुवासिनीभ्यो विप्रेभ्यो यथाकामं च सादरम् ॥
1.113.m: saying 'May the god be pleased with me,' one should then offer them / to married women and to the twice-born as desired, with respect.

1.113.s:
tataścandrodaye rātrau dattvārghaṃ vidhipūrvakam /
bhuñjīta miṣṭamannaṃ ca vratasya paripūrtaye //
1.113.d:
ततश्चन्द्रोदये रात्रौ दत्त्वार्घं विधिपूर्वकम् ।
भुञ्जीत मिष्टमन्नं च व्रतस्य परिपूर्तये ॥
1.113.m: Then, at moonrise at night, having offered an oblation according to rule, / she should eat sweet food for the complete fulfillment of the observance.

1.113.s:
yadvā kṣīreṇa karakaṃ pūrṇaṃ toyena vā mune /
sapūgākṣataratnāḍhyaṃ dvijāya pratipādayet //
1.113.d:
यद्वा क्षीरेण करकं पूर्णं तोयेन वा मुने ।
सपूगाक्षतरत्नाढ्यं द्विजाय प्रतिपादयेत् ॥
1.113.m: Or, O sage, a vessel filled with milk or with water, / rich in betel nuts, unbroken rice, and gems, one should bestow upon a twice-born.

1.113.s:
etatkṛtvā vrataṃ nārī ṣoḍaśadvādaśābdakam /
upāyanaṃ vidhāyātha vratametadvisarjjayet //
1.113.d:
एतत्कृत्वा व्रतं नारी षोडशद्वादशाब्दकम् ।
उपायनं विधायाथ व्रतमेतद्विसर्ज्जयेत् ॥
1.113.m: Having performed this observance for sixteen or twelve years, / a woman should then make an offering and complete this observance.

1.113.s:
yāvajjīvaṃ tu vā nāryā kāryyaṃ saubhāgyavāñchayā /
vratenānena sadṛśaṃ strīṇāṃ saubhāgyadāyakam //
1.113.d:
यावज्जीवं तु वा नार्या कार्य्यं सौभाग्यवाञ्छया ।
व्रतेनानेन सदृशं स्त्रीणां सौभाग्यदायकम् ॥
1.113.m: Or it should be observed by a woman for as long as she lives, through desire for good fortune. / An observance equal to this, bestowing good fortune upon women,

1.113.s:
vidyate bhuvaneṣvanyattasmānnityamiti sthitiḥ /
ūrjjaśuklacaturthyāṃ tu nāgavratamudāhṛtam //
1.113.d:
विद्यते भुवनेष्वन्यत्तस्मान्नित्यमिति स्थितिः ।
ऊर्ज्जशुक्लचतुर्थ्यां तु नागव्रतमुदाहृतम् ॥
1.113.m: is not found anywhere else in the worlds; therefore, it is established as perpetual. / On the fourth [tithi] of the bright [fortnight] of Ūrja, the Serpent Observance is declared.

1.113.s:
prātarvrataṃ tu saṃkalpya dhenuśṛñjagalaṃ śuci /
pītvā snātvātha madhyāhne śaṅkhapālādipannagān //
1.113.d:
प्रातर्व्रतं तु संकल्प्य धेनुशृञ्जगलं शुचि ।
पीत्वा स्नात्वाथ मध्याह्ने शङ्खपालादिपन्नगान् ॥
1.113.m: Having taken the resolve for the observance in the morning, having drunk pure cow's horn-water / and then bathed, at midday [one should worship] Śaṅkhapāla and other serpents,

1.113.s:
śeṣaṃ cāhvāmapūrvaistu pūjayedupacārakaiḥ /
kṣīreṇāpyāyanaṃ kuryādetannāgavrataṃ smṛtam //
1.113.d:
शेषं चाह्वामपूर्वैस्तु पूजयेदुपचारकैः ।
क्षीरेणाप्यायनं कुर्यादेतन्नागव्रतं स्मृतम् ॥
1.113.m: and Śeṣa preceded by his names, with the [various] services. / One should perform satiation with milk; this is remembered as the Serpent Observance.

1.113.s:
evaṅkṛte tu viprendra nṛbhirnāgavrate śubhe /
viṣāṇi naśyantyacirānna daśanti ca pannagāḥ //
1.113.d:
एवङ्कृते तु विप्रेन्द्र नृभिर्नागव्रते शुभे ।
विषाणि नश्यन्त्यचिरान्न दशन्ति च पन्नगाः ॥
1.113.m: When this auspicious Serpent Observance is performed by men, O best of the twice-born, / poisons are swiftly destroyed, and serpents do not bite.

1.113.s:
mārgaśuklacaturthyāṃ tu varṣaṃ yāvanmunīśvarā /
kṣapayedekabhaktena naktenātha dvitīyakam //
1.113.d:
मार्गशुक्लचतुर्थ्यां तु वर्षं यावन्मुनीश्वरा ।
क्षपयेदेकभक्तेन नक्तेनाथ द्वितीयकम् ॥
1.113.m: On the fourth [tithi] of the bright [fortnight] of Mārgaśīrṣa, O lord of sages, for a year / one should pass the time eating once a day; then during the second, with nocturnal eating;

1.113.s:
ayācitopavāsābhyāṃ tṛtīyakacaturthake /
evaṃ krameṇa vidhivaccatvāryabdāni mānavaḥ //
1.113.d:
अयाचितोपवासाभ्यां तृतीयकचतुर्थके ।
एवं क्रमेण विधिवच्चत्वार्यब्दानि मानवः ॥
1.113.m: during the third and fourth [years], with food received unasked and with fasting. / Thus, in succession according to rule, for four years a man

1.113.s:
samāpya ca tato 'syānte vratasnāto mahāvratī /
kārayeddhemaghaṭitaṃ bhūgaṇermūṣakaṃ ratham //
1.113.d:
समाप्य च ततो ऽस्यान्ते व्रतस्नातो महाव्रती ।
कारयेद्धेमघटितं भूगणेर्मूषकं रथम् ॥
1.113.m: completes it, and then at its conclusion, having taken the bath of the observance, the great observer of vows / should have a golden mouse-chariot made by a group of goldsmiths;

1.113.s:
aśakto varṇakaireva śubhraṃ cābjaṃ supatrakam /
tasyopari ghaṭaṃ sthāpya tāmrapātreṇa saṃyutam //
1.113.d:
अशक्तो वर्णकैरेव शुभ्रं चाब्जं सुपत्रकम् ।
तस्योपरि घटं स्थाप्य ताम्रपात्रेण संयुतम् ॥
1.113.m: if unable, [made] only with colors, and a white lotus with fine petals. / Placing a jar upon it along with a copper vessel,

1.113.s:
pūrayettaṇḍalaiḥ śubhraistasyopari gaṇeśvaram /
nyasedvastrayugācchannaṃ gandhādyaiḥ pūjayecca tam //
1.113.d:
पूरयेत्तण्डलैः शुभ्रैस्तस्योपरि गणेश्वरम् ।
न्यसेद्वस्त्रयुगाच्छन्नं गन्धाद्यैः पूजयेच्च तम् ॥
1.113.m: one should fill it with white rice-grains; upon it one should place Gaṇeśvara / covered with a pair of garments, and should worship him with perfumes and other [offerings].

1.113.s:
naivedyaṃ modakaṃ kalpyaṃ gaṇeśaḥ prīyatāmiti /
jāgarairśītavādyādyaiḥ purāṇākhyānakaiścaret //
1.113.d:
नैवेद्यं मोदकं कल्प्यं गणेशः प्रीयतामिति ।
जागरैर्शीतवाद्याद्यैः पुराणाख्यानकैश्चरेत् ॥
1.113.m: A sweetmeat should be prepared as food offering, saying, 'May Gaṇeśa be pleased.' / One should keep vigil with songs, musical instruments, and recitations of Purāṇas.

1.113.s:
prabhāte vimale snātvā homaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ /'
tilavrīhiyavaśvetasurṣapājyaiḥ sakhaṇḍakaiḥ //
1.113.d:
प्रभाते विमले स्नात्वा होमं कृत्वा विधानतः ।'
तिलव्रीहियवश्वेतसुर्षपाज्यैः सखण्डकैः ॥
1.113.m: Having bathed at a clear dawn and performed fire oblations according to rule / with sesame, unhusked rice, barley, white mustard, clarified butter, and sugar pieces,

1.113.s:
gaṇo gaṇādhipaścaiva kūṣmāṇḍastripurāntakaḥ /
laṃbodaraikadantau ca rukmadaṃṣṭraśca vighnapaḥ //
1.113.d:
गणो गणाधिपश्चैव कूष्माण्डस्त्रिपुरान्तकः ।
लंबोदरैकदन्तौ च रुक्मदंष्ट्रश्च विघ्नपः ॥
1.113.m: with these sixteen names: Gaṇa, Gaṇādhipa, Kūṣmāṇḍa, Tripurāntaka, / Lambodara, Ekadanta, Rukmadaṃṣṭra, Vighnapa,

1.113.s:
brahmā yamo 'tha varuṇaḥ somasūryahutāśanāḥ /
gandhamādī parameṣṭhītyevaṃ ṣoḍaśanāmabhiḥ //
1.113.d:
ब्रह्मा यमो ऽथ वरुणः सोमसूर्यहुताशनाः ।
गन्धमादी परमेष्ठीत्येवं षोडशनामभिः ॥
1.113.m: Brahmā, Yama, Varuṇa, Soma, Sūrya, Hutāśana, / Gandhamādin, and Parameṣṭhin,

1.113.s:
praṇavādyairṅeṃnamoṃ'taiḥ pratyekaṃ dahane hunet /
vakratuṇḍeti ṅeṃtena barmāntenāṣṭayukchatam //
1.113.d:
प्रणवाद्यैर्ङेंनमोंऽतैः प्रत्येकं दहने हुनेत् ।
वक्रतुण्डेति ङेंतेन बर्मान्तेनाष्टयुक्छतम् ॥
1.113.m: each preceded by Praṇava and ending in dative 'namaḥ', one should offer into the fire. / With 'Vakratuṇḍa' in the dative ending in 'varman', one should offer one hundred and eight times.

1.113.s:
tato vyāhṛtibhiḥ śaktyā hutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ caret /
dikpālānpūjayitvā ca brāhmaṇānbhojayettataḥ //
1.113.d:
ततो व्याहृतिभिः शक्त्या हुत्वा पूर्णाहुतिं चरेत् ।
दिक्पालान्पूजयित्वा च ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेत्ततः ॥
1.113.m: Then, having offered with the vyāhṛtis according to ability, one should perform the final oblation. / And having worshipped the guardians of the directions, one should feed brāhmaṇas:

1.113.s:
catutviṃśatisaṃkhyākān modakaiḥ pāyasaistathā /
savatsāṃ gāṃ tato dadyādācāryāya sadakṣiṇām //
1.113.d:
चतुत्विंशतिसंख्याकान् मोदकैः पायसैस्तथा ।
सवत्सां गां ततो दद्यादाचार्याय सदक्षिणाम् ॥
1.113.m: twenty-four in number, with sweetmeats and milk pudding. / Then one should give a cow with calf, accompanied by a fee, to the ācārya.

1.113.s:
anyobhyo 'pi yathāśakti bhūyasīṃ ca tato dadet /
praṇamya dakṣiṇīkṛtya pravisṛjya dvijottamām //
1.113.d:
अन्योभ्यो ऽपि यथाशक्ति भूयसीं च ततो ददेत् ।
प्रणम्य दक्षिणीकृत्य प्रविसृज्य द्विजोत्तमाम् ॥
1.113.m: To the others as well, according to one's ability, one should give an abundant [fee]. / Having bowed down, circumambulated, and dismissed those best of the twice-born,

1.113.s:
bandhubhiḥ saha bhuñjīta svayaṃ ca prītamānasaḥ /
etadvrataṃ naraḥ kṛtvā bhuktvā bhogānihottamān //
1.113.d:
बन्धुभिः सह भुञ्जीत स्वयं च प्रीतमानसः ।
एतद्व्रतं नरः कृत्वा भुक्त्वा भोगानिहोत्तमान् ॥
1.113.m: one should oneself eat together with relatives, with a pleased mind. / Having performed this observance and enjoyed excellent pleasures here [on earth], a man

1.113.s:
sāyujyaṃ labhate viṣṇorgaṇeśasya prasādataḥ /
kecidvaravrataṃ nāma prāhuretasya nārada //
1.113.d:
सायुज्यं लभते विष्णोर्गणेशस्य प्रसादतः ।
केचिद्वरव्रतं नाम प्राहुरेतस्य नारद ॥
1.113.m: attains union with Viṣṇu through the grace of Gaṇeśa. / Some, O Nārada, call this the Varavrata.

1.113.s:
vidhānametadevāpi phalaṃ cāpīha tatsamam /
pauṣamāsacaturthyāṃ tu vighneśaṃ prārthya bhaktitaḥ //
1.113.d:
विधानमेतदेवापि फलं चापीह तत्समम् ।
पौषमासचतुर्थ्यां तु विघ्नेशं प्रार्थ्य भक्तितः ॥
1.113.m: Its procedure is this very same, and its fruit here is also equal to that. / On the fourth [tithi] of the month of Pauṣa, having prayed to Vighneśa with devotion,

1.113.s:
vipraikaṃ bhojayeccaivaṃ modakairdakṣiṇāṃ dadet /
evaṃ kṛte mune bhūyādvratī saṃpattibhājanam //
1.113.d:
विप्रैकं भोजयेच्चैवं मोदकैर्दक्षिणां ददेत् ।
एवं कृते मुने भूयाद्व्रती संपत्तिभाजनम् ॥
1.113.m: one should feed one twice-born thus with sweetmeats, and give a fee. / When this is done, O sage, the observer of vows becomes a vessel of prosperity.

1.113.s:
māghakṛṣṇacaturthyāṃ tu saṃkaṣṭavratamucyate /
tatropavāsaṃ saṃkalpya vratī niyamapūrvakam //
1.113.d:
माघकृष्णचतुर्थ्यां तु संकष्टव्रतमुच्यते ।
तत्रोपवासं संकल्प्य व्रती नियमपूर्वकम् ॥
1.113.m: On the fourth [tithi] of the dark [fortnight] of Māgha, the Saṃkaṣṭa Observance is declared. / Having resolved upon fasting there according to rule, the observer of vows,

1.113.s:
candrodayamabhivyāpya tiṣṭhetprayatamānasaḥ /
tataścandrodaye prāpte mṛnmayaṃ gaṇanāyakam //
1.113.d:
चन्द्रोदयमभिव्याप्य तिष्ठेत्प्रयतमानसः ।
ततश्चन्द्रोदये प्राप्ते मृन्मयं गणनायकम् ॥
1.113.m: restrained in mind, should remain [fasting] until moonrise. / Then, when moonrise has arrived, having fashioned an earthen Gaṇanāyaka

1.113.s:
vidhāya vinyasetpīṭhe sāyudhaṃ ca savāhanam /
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ //
1.113.d:
विधाय विन्यसेत्पीठे सायुधं च सवाहनम् ।
उपचारैः षोडशभिः समभ्यर्च्य विधानतः ॥
1.113.m: equipped with weapons and with a mount, one should place him on a ritual seat. / Having worshipped him properly with the sixteen services,

1.113.s:
modakaṃ cāpi naivedyaṃ saguḍaṃ tilakuṭṭakam /
tator'ghyaṃ tāmraje pātre raktacandanamiśritam //
1.113.d:
मोदकं चापि नैवेद्यं सगुडं तिलकुट्टकम् ।
ततोर्ऽघ्यं ताम्रजे पात्रे रक्तचन्दनमिश्रितम् ॥
1.113.m: sweetmeats and pounded sesame with jaggery as food offering, / then an water-offering in a copper vessel mixed with red sandalwood

1.113.s:
sakuśaṃ ca sadūrvaṃ ca puṣpākṣatasamanvitam /
saśamīpatradadhi ca kṛtvā candrāya dāpayet //
1.113.d:
सकुशं च सदूर्वं च पुष्पाक्षतसमन्वितम् ।
सशमीपत्रदधि च कृत्वा चन्द्राय दापयेत् ॥
1.113.m:
Having prepared [water] with kuśa, dūrvā, flowers, and unbroken grains,
along with śamī leaves and curd, one should offer it to the moon:

1.113.s:
gaganārṇavamāṇikya candra dākṣāyaṇīpate /
gṛhāṇārghyaṃ mayā dattaṃ gaṇeśapratirūpaka //
1.113.d:
गगनार्णवमाणिक्य चन्द्र दाक्षायणीपते ।
गृहाणार्घ्यं मया दत्तं गणेशप्रतिरूपक ॥
1.113.m:
"O ruby of the sky-ocean! O moon! O lord of Dakṣa's daughter!
Accept the water-offering given by me, O image of Gaṇeśa!"

1.113.s:
evaṃ dattvā gaṇeśāya divyārghyaṃ pāpanāśanam /
śaktyā saṃbhojya viprāgryānsvayaṃ bhuñjīta cājñayā //
1.113.d:
एवं दत्त्वा गणेशाय दिव्यार्घ्यं पापनाशनम् ।
शक्त्या संभोज्य विप्राग्र्यान्स्वयं भुञ्जीत चाज्ञया ॥
1.113.m:
Having thus offered the divine, sin-destroying water-offering to Gaṇeśa,
and having fed the foremost brāhmaṇas according to one's capacity, one should eat oneself with their permission.

1.113.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra saṃkaṣṭākhyaṃ śūbhāvaham /
samṛddho dhanadhānyaiḥ syānna ca saṃkaṣṭamāpnuyāt //
1.113.d:
एवं कृत्वा व्रतं विप्र संकष्टाख्यं शूभावहम् ।
समृद्धो धनधान्यैः स्यान्न च संकष्टमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.113.m:
Having thus performed this observance called Saṃkaṣṭā, which brings good fortune, O brāhmaṇa,
one will flourish with wealth and grain, and will not encounter distress.

1.113.s:
māghaśuklacaturthyāṃ tu gaurīvratamanuttamam /
tasyāṃ tu gaurī saṃpūjyā saṃyuktā yoginīgaṇaiḥ //
1.113.d:
माघशुक्लचतुर्थ्यां तु गौरीव्रतमनुत्तमम् ।
तस्यां तु गौरी संपूज्या संयुक्ता योगिनीगणैः ॥
1.113.m:
On the bright fourth tithi of Māgha is the unsurpassed Gaurīvrata;
on that [tithi], Gaurī accompanied by the host of yoginīs is to be worshipped

1.113.s:
naraiḥ strībhirviśeṣeṇa kundapuṣpaiḥ sakuṅkumaiḥ /
raktasūtre raktapuṣpaistathaivālaktakena ca //
1.113.d:
नरैः स्त्रीभिर्विशेषेण कुन्दपुष्पैः सकुङ्कुमैः ।
रक्तसूत्रे रक्तपुष्पैस्तथैवालक्तकेन च ॥
1.113.m:
by men, and especially by women, with kunda flowers and saffron,
with red threads, red flowers, and likewise with red lac;

1.113.s:
dhūpairdīpaṃśca balibhiḥ saguḍainārdrakeṇa ca /
payasā pāyasenāpi lavaṇena ca pālakaiḥ //
1.113.d:
धूपैर्दीपंश्च बलिभिः सगुडैनार्द्रकेण च ।
पयसा पायसेनापि लवणेन च पालकैः ॥
1.113.m:
with incenses, lamps, oblations, with jaggery and ginger,
with milk, with rice-milk, with salt, and with spinach.

1.113.s:
pūjyāścāvidhavā nāryastathā viprāḥ suśobhanāḥ /
saubhāgyavṛddhaye deyo bhoktavyaṃ bandhubhiḥ saha //
1.113.d:
पूज्याश्चाविधवा नार्यस्तथा विप्राः सुशोभनाः ।
सौभाग्यवृद्धये देयो भोक्तव्यं बन्धुभिः सह ॥
1.113.m:
Non-widowed women and auspicious brāhmaṇas are to be worshipped;
[gifts] should be given for the increase of good fortune, and one should eat together with relatives.

1.113.s:
idaṃ gaurīvrataṃ vipra saubhāgyārogyavarddhanam /
prativarṣaṃ prakarttavyaṃ nārībhiśca naraistathā //
1.113.d:
इदं गौरीव्रतं विप्र सौभाग्यारोग्यवर्द्धनम् ।
प्रतिवर्षं प्रकर्त्तव्यं नारीभिश्च नरैस्तथा ॥
1.113.m:
This Gaurīvrata, O brāhmaṇa, increases good fortune and health;
it should be performed every year by women and also by men.

1.113.s:
ḍhuṇḍhivrataṃ paraiḥ proktaṃ kaiścitkuṇḍavrataṃ smṛtam /
lalitāvratamityanyaiḥ śāntivratamathāparaiḥ //
1.113.d:
ढुण्ढिव्रतं परैः प्रोक्तं कैश्चित्कुण्डव्रतं स्मृतम् ।
ललिताव्रतमित्यन्यैः शान्तिव्रतमथापरैः ॥
1.113.m:
It is proclaimed by others as Ḍhuṇḍhivrata, remembered by some as Kuṇḍavrata,
by others as Lalitāvrata, and by still others as Śāntivrata.

1.113.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ sarvamasyāṃ kṛtaṃ mune /
bhavetsaha sraguṇitaṃ prasādāddantinaḥ sadā //
1.113.d:
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः सर्वमस्यां कृतं मुने ।
भवेत्सह स्रगुणितं प्रसादाद्दन्तिनः सदा ॥
1.113.m:
Bathing, giving, recitation, fire oblation—all done on this [day], O sage,
becomes multiplied a thousandfold, always through the grace of the Tusker.

1.113.s:
caturthyāṃ phaālgune māsi ḍhuṇḍhirājavrataṃ śubham /
tilaṣiṣṭairdvijān bhojya svayaṃ cāśnīta mānavaḥ //
1.113.d:
चतुर्थ्यां फआल्गुने मासि ढुण्ढिराजव्रतं शुभम् ।
तिलषिष्टैर्द्विजान् भोज्य स्वयं चाश्नीत मानवः ॥
1.113.m:
On the fourth tithi in the month of Phālguna is the auspicious Ḍhuṇḍhirājavrata.
Having fed the twice-born with sesame flour, a person should also eat [it] themselves,

1.113.s:
gaṇeśārādhanaparo dānahomaprapūjanaiḥ /
tilaireva kṛtaiḥ siddhiṃ prāpnuyāttatprasādataḥ //
1.113.d:
गणेशाराधनपरो दानहोमप्रपूजनैः ।
तिलैरेव कृतैः सिद्धिं प्राप्नुयात्तत्प्रसादतः ॥
1.113.m:
devoted to the worship of Gaṇeśa with gifts, fire oblations, and acts of worship
performed with sesame alone; one attains perfection through his grace.

1.113.s:
sauvarṇaṃ gajavaktraṃ ca kṛtvā saṃpūjya yatnataḥ /
dvijāgryāya pradātavyaṃ sarvasaṃpatsamṛddhaye //
1.113.d:
सौवर्णं गजवक्त्रं च कृत्वा संपूज्य यत्नतः ।
द्विजाग्र्याय प्रदातव्यं सर्वसंपत्समृद्धये ॥
1.113.m:
Having made a golden elephant-faced [image] and worshipped it with effort,
it should be given to a foremost twice-born for the abundance of all prosperity.

1.113.s:
yasminkasminbhavenmāsi caturthī ravivārayuk /
sāṃgārakā vā viprendra sā viśeṣaphalapradā //
1.113.d:
यस्मिन्कस्मिन्भवेन्मासि चतुर्थी रविवारयुक् ।
सांगारका वा विप्रेन्द्र सा विशेषफलप्रदा ॥
1.113.m:
In whatever month a fourth tithi falls on a Sunday
or on a Tuesday, O chief of brāhmaṇas, it grants special fruits.

1.113.s:
sarvāsu ca caturthīṣu śuklāsvapyasitāsu ca /
vighneśa eva deveśaḥ saṃpūjyo bhaktitatparaiḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde dvādśanāsa caturthīvratānirūpaṇaṃ nāma trayodaśādhikasatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.113.d:
सर्वासु च चतुर्थीषु शुक्लास्वप्यसितासु च ।
विघ्नेश एव देवेशः संपूज्यो भक्तितत्परैः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे द्वाद्शनास चतुर्थीव्रतानिरूपणं नाम त्रयोदशाधिकसततमो ऽध्यायः
1.113.m:
And on all fourth tithis, whether bright or dark,
the Lord of Obstacles, the Lord of Gods, alone is to be worshipped by those devoted in devotion.

Thus ends the one hundred and thirteenth chapter, named 'Description of the Fourth-Tithi Observances of the Twelve Months', in the fourth quarter of the great narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.114.s:
sanātana uvāca
śṛṇu vipra pravakṣyāmi pañcamyāste vratānyaham /
yāni bhaktyā samāsthāya sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt //
1.114.d:
सनातन उवाच
शृणु विप्र प्रवक्ष्यामि पञ्चम्यास्ते व्रतान्यहम् ।
यानि भक्त्या समास्थाय सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.114.m:
Sanātana said:
Listen, O brāhmaṇa, I shall declare to you the observances of the fifth [tithi],
by undertaking which with devotion one attains all desires.

1.114.s:
proktā matsyajayantī tu pañcamī madhuśuklagā /
asyāṃ matsyāvatārārcā bhaktaiḥ kāryā mahotsavā //
1.114.d:
प्रोक्ता मत्स्यजयन्ती तु पञ्चमी मधुशुक्लगा ।
अस्यां मत्स्यावतारार्चा भक्तैः कार्या महोत्सवा ॥
1.114.m:
The fifth tithi in the bright [fortnight] of Madhu is proclaimed as Matsyajayantī;
on this [day], worship of the Fish incarnation should be performed by devotees as a great festival.

1.114.s:
śrīpañcamīti caiṣoktā tatra kāryaṃ śriyor'canam /
gandhādyairupacāraistu naivedyaiḥ pāyasādibhiḥ //
1.114.d:
श्रीपञ्चमीति चैषोक्ता तत्र कार्यं श्रियोर्ऽचनम् ।
गन्धाद्यैरुपचारैस्तु नैवेद्यैः पायसादिभिः ॥
1.114.m: And this is called Śrīpañcamī. There, worship of Śrī should be performed / with offerings such as fragrant pastes, and food offerings such as milk-rice and the like.

1.114.s:
yo lakṣmīṃ pūjayeccātra taṃ vai lakṣmīrna muñcati /
pṛthvīvrataṃ tathā cāndraṃ hayagarīvavrataṃ tathā //
1.114.d:
यो लक्ष्मीं पूजयेच्चात्र तं वै लक्ष्मीर्न मुञ्चति ।
पृथ्वीव्रतं तथा चान्द्रं हयगरीवव्रतं तथा ॥
1.114.m: Whoever worships Lakṣmī here, him Lakṣmī certainly never abandons. / Likewise the Pṛthvīvrata, the Cāndravrata, and the Hayagrīvavrata,

1.114.s:
kāryaṃ tattadvidhānena tattatsiddhimabhīpsubhiḥ /
atha vaiśākhapañcamyāṃ śeṣaṃ cābhyarcya mānavaḥ //
1.114.d:
कार्यं तत्तद्विधानेन तत्तत्सिद्धिमभीप्सुभिः ।
अथ वैशाखपञ्चम्यां शेषं चाभ्यर्च्य मानवः ॥
1.114.m: should be performed according to their respective rules by those desiring their respective accomplishments. / Then, on the fifth day of Vaiśākha, a man having worshipped Śeṣa,

1.114.s:
sarvairnāgagaṇairyuktamabhīṣṭaṃ labhate phalam /
tathā jyeṣṭhasya pañcamyāṃ pitṝnabhyarcayetsudhīḥ //
1.114.d:
सर्वैर्नागगणैर्युक्तमभीष्टं लभते फलम् ।
तथा ज्येष्ठस्य पञ्चम्यां पितॄनभ्यर्चयेत्सुधीः ॥
1.114.m: together with all the host of serpents, attains his desired fruit. / Likewise, on the fifth day of Jyeṣṭha, a wise man should worship the ancestors.

1.114.s:
sarvakāmaphalāvāptirbhavedvai viprabhojanaiḥ /
athāṣāḍhasya pañcamyāṃ vāyuṃ sarvagataṃ mune //
1.114.d:
सर्वकामफलावाप्तिर्भवेद्वै विप्रभोजनैः ।
अथाषाढस्य पञ्चम्यां वायुं सर्वगतं मुने ॥
1.114.m: Attainment of the fruit of all desires shall indeed come about through feeding brāhmaṇas. / Then, on the fifth day of Āṣāḍha, [to worship] the all-pervading wind, O sage,

1.114.s:
grāmādbahirvinirgatya dharopasthe samāstitaḥ /
dhvajaṃ ca pañcavarṇaṃ tu vaṃśadaṇḍāgrasaṃsthitam //
1.114.d:
ग्रामाद्बहिर्विनिर्गत्य धरोपस्थे समास्तितः ।
ध्वजं च पञ्चवर्णं तु वंशदण्डाग्रसंस्थितम् ॥
1.114.m: having gone outside the village, established on the surface of the earth, / a five-coloured flag situated at the top of a bamboo pole,

1.114.s:
samucchritaṃ nidadhyāttu kalpitābje tu madhyataḥ /
tatastanmūladeśe tu dikṣu sarvāsu nārada //
1.114.d:
समुच्छ्रितं निदध्यात्तु कल्पिताब्जे तु मध्यतः ।
ततस्तन्मूलदेशे तु दिक्षु सर्वासु नारद ॥
1.114.m: raised high, one should place in the middle of a prepared lotus. / Then, at its base, in all the directions, O Nārada,

1.114.s:
lokapālānsamabhyarcya kuryādvāyuparīkṣaṇam /
prathamādiṣu yāmeṣu yo yo vāyuḥ pravartate //
1.114.d:
लोकपालान्समभ्यर्च्य कुर्याद्वायुपरीक्षणम् ।
प्रथमादिषु यामेषु यो यो वायुः प्रवर्तते ॥
1.114.m: having worshipped the world-guardians, one should make examination of the wind: / whichever wind blows in the first and subsequent watches,

1.114.s:
tasmai tasmai digīśāya pūjāṃ samyak prakalpayet /
evaṃ sthitvā nirāhārastatra yāmacatuṣṭayam //
1.114.d:
तस्मै तस्मै दिगीशाय पूजां सम्यक् प्रकल्पयेत् ।
एवं स्थित्वा निराहारस्तत्र यामचतुष्टयम् ॥
1.114.m: to that respective lord of the direction one should properly offer worship. / Having thus remained without food there for four watches,

1.114.s:
sāyamāgatya gehaṃ svaṃ bhuktvā svalpaṃ samāhitaḥ /
lokapālānnamaskṛtya svapyādbhūmitale śucau //
1.114.d:
सायमागत्य गेहं स्वं भुक्त्वा स्वल्पं समाहितः ।
लोकपालान्नमस्कृत्य स्वप्याद्भूमितले शुचौ ॥
1.114.m: having returned home in the evening and eaten a little, composed in mind, / having bowed to the world-guardians, one should sleep on the pure ground.

1.114.s:
yaḥ svapno jāyate tasyāṃ rātrau yāme caturthake /
sa eva bhavitā nūnaṃ svapna ityāha vai śivaḥ //
1.114.d:
यः स्वप्नो जायते तस्यां रात्रौ यामे चतुर्थके ।
स एव भविता नूनं स्वप्न इत्याह वै शिवः ॥
1.114.m: Whatever dream arises on that night during the fourth watch, / that very dream will surely come to pass—so said Śiva.

1.114.s:
aśubhe tu samutpanne śivapūjāparāyaṇaḥ /
sopavāso nayedaṣṭayāmaṃ taddinameva vā //
1.114.d:
अशुभे तु समुत्पन्ने शिवपूजापरायणः ।
सोपवासो नयेदष्टयामं तद्दिनमेव वा ॥
1.114.m: If an inauspicious [dream] should arise, dedicated to the worship of Śiva, / fasting, he should spend eight watches or that whole day.

1.114.s:
bhojayitvā dvijānaṣṭau tataḥ śubhaphalaṃ labhet /
vratametatsamuditaṃ śubhāśubhanidarśanam //
1.114.d:
भोजयित्वा द्विजानष्टौ ततः शुभफलं लभेत् ।
व्रतमेतत्समुदितं शुभाशुभनिदर्शनम् ॥
1.114.m: Having fed eight brāhmaṇas, he shall then attain an auspicious fruit. / This observance has been declared as an indicator of good and bad fortune,

1.114.s:
nṛṇāṃ saubhāgyajanakamiha loke paratra ca /
śrāvaṇe kṛṣṇapañcamyāṃ vrataṃ hyannasamṛddhidam //
1.114.d:
नृणां सौभाग्यजनकमिह लोके परत्र च ।
श्रावणे कृष्णपञ्चम्यां व्रतं ह्यन्नसमृद्धिदम् ॥
1.114.m: generating good fortune for men in this world and in the next. / On the dark fifth of Śrāvaṇa, there is an observance that bestows an abundance of grain.

1.114.s:
caturthyāṃ dinaśeṣe tu sarvāṇyannāni nārada /
pṛthak pātreṣu saṃsthāpya jalairāplāvayetsudhīḥ //
1.114.d:
चतुर्थ्यां दिनशेषे तु सर्वाण्यन्नानि नारद ।
पृथक् पात्रेषु संस्थाप्य जलैराप्लावयेत्सुधीः ॥
1.114.m: On the fourth day at the end of the day, O Nārada, / placing all kinds of grains in separate vessels, the wise man should flood them with water.

1.114.s:
tato pātrāntare tattu niṣkāsyāṃbu nidhāpayet /
prātarbhānau samudite pitṝṃścaiva tathā ṛṣīn //
1.114.d:
ततो पात्रान्तरे तत्तु निष्कास्यांबु निधापयेत् ।
प्रातर्भानौ समुदिते पितॄंश्चैव तथा ऋषीन् ॥
1.114.m: Then, having drained that water into another vessel, he should set [the grain] down. / In the morning, when the sun has risen, having worshipped the ancestors and the ṛṣis,

1.114.s:
devāṃścābhyarcya susnātaṃ kṛtvā naivedyamagrataḥ /
tadannaṃ yācakebhyastu prayacchetprītamānasaḥ //
1.114.d:
देवांश्चाभ्यर्च्य सुस्नातं कृत्वा नैवेद्यमग्रतः ।
तदन्नं याचकेभ्यस्तु प्रयच्छेत्प्रीतमानसः ॥
1.114.m: and the deities, having bathed well, offering food oblations in front, / with a pleased mind he should give that food to beggars.

1.114.s:
sarvaṃ dinaṃ kṣipedevaṃ pradoṣe tu śivālaye /
gatvā saṃpūjayeddevaṃ liṅgarūpiṇamīśvaram //
1.114.d:
सर्वं दिनं क्षिपेदेवं प्रदोषे तु शिवालये ।
गत्वा संपूजयेद्देवं लिङ्गरूपिणमीश्वरम् ॥
1.114.m: He should pass the whole day thus; and at twilight, going to a temple of Śiva, / he should worship the lord, God in the form of the liṅga.

1.114.s:
gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ samyakpūjayitvā maheśvaram /
japetpañcākṣarī vidyāṃ śataṃ cāpi sahasrakam //
1.114.d:
गन्धपुष्पादिभिः सम्यक्पूजयित्वा महेश्वरम् ।
जपेत्पञ्चाक्षरी विद्यां शतं चापि सहस्रकम् ॥
1.114.m: Having properly worshipped Maheśvara with fragrant pastes, flowers, and other offerings, / he should recite the five-syllable vidyā a hundred or a thousand times.

1.114.s:
japaṃ nivedya devāya bhavāya bhavarūpiṇe /
stutvā sarvairvaundikaiśca paurāṇaiścāpyanākulaḥ //
1.114.d:
जपं निवेद्य देवाय भवाय भवरूपिणे ।
स्तुत्वा सर्वैर्वौन्दिकैश्च पौराणैश्चाप्यनाकुलः ॥
1.114.m: Offering the recitation to the God, to Bhava who has the form of worldly existence, / having praised him with all Vedic and purāṇic hymns, untroubled,

1.114.s:
prārthayeddevamīśānaṃ śaśvatsarvānnasiddhaye /
śāradīyāni cānnāni tathā vāsaṃtikānyapi //
1.114.d:
प्रार्थयेद्देवमीशानं शश्वत्सर्वान्नसिद्धये ।
शारदीयानि चान्नानि तथा वासंतिकान्यपि ॥
1.114.m: he should pray to the Lord, God, for constant success in [obtaining] all grains: / 'Whatever autumn grains and whatever spring grains

1.114.s:
yāni syustaiḥ samṛddho 'haṃ bhūyāṃ janmani janmani /
evaṃ saṃprārthya deveśaṃ gṛhamāgatya vai svakam //
1.114.d:
यानि स्युस्तैः समृद्धो ऽहं भूयां जन्मनि जन्मनि ।
एवं संप्रार्थ्य देवेशं गृहमागत्य वै स्वकम् ॥
1.114.m: there may be, may I be enriched by them in birth after birth!' / Having thus prayed to the Lord of gods, having returned to his own home,

1.114.s:
datvānnaṃ brāhmaṇādibhyaḥ pakvaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ /
etadannavrataṃ vipra vidhinā'caritaṃ nṛbhiḥ //
1.114.d:
दत्वान्नं ब्राह्मणादिभ्यः पक्वं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ।
एतदन्नव्रतं विप्र विधिनाऽचरितं नृभिः ॥
1.114.m: having given cooked food to brāhmaṇas and others, he should eat, restraining his speech. / This observance of grain, O brāhmaṇa, performed according to rule by men,

1.114.s:
sarvānnasaṃpajjanakaṃ paraloke gatipradam /
śrāvaṇe śuklapañcajamyāṃ nṛbhirāstikyatatparaiḥ //
1.114.d:
सर्वान्नसंपज्जनकं परलोके गतिप्रदम् ।
श्रावणे शुक्लपञ्चजम्यां नृभिरास्तिक्यतत्परैः ॥
1.114.m: generates prosperity of all grains and bestows a [good] destiny in the other world. / On the bright fifth of Śrāvaṇa, by men intent on faith,

1.114.s:
dvārasyobhayato lekhyā gomayena viṣolbaṇāḥ /
gandhādyaiḥ pūjayettāṃśca tathendrāṇīmanantaram //
1.114.d:
द्वारस्योभयतो लेख्या गोमयेन विषोल्बणाः ।
गन्धाद्यैः पूजयेत्तांश्च तथेन्द्राणीमनन्तरम् ॥
1.114.m: on both sides of the door should be drawn [serpents] fierce with poison, using cow dung; / and one should worship them with fragrant pastes and other [articles], and then Indrāṇī.

1.114.s:
saṃpūjya svarṇarūpyādidadhyakṣatakuśāṃbubhiḥ /
gandhaiḥ puṣpaistathā dhūpairdīpairnaivedyasaṃcayaiḥ //
1.114.d:
संपूज्य स्वर्णरूप्यादिदध्यक्षतकुशांबुभिः ।
गन्धैः पुष्पैस्तथा धूपैर्दीपैर्नैवेद्यसंचयैः ॥
1.114.m: Having worshipped with gold, silver, and other gifts, curd, unhusked rice, kuśa grass, and water, / with fragrant pastes, flowers, and incense, lamps, and heaps of food offerings,

1.114.s:
tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya taddravyaṃ saṃpraṇamya ca /
saṃprārthya bhaktibhāvena viprāgryeṣu samarpayet //
1.114.d:
ततः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य तद्द्रव्यं संप्रणम्य च ।
संप्रार्थ्य भक्तिभावेन विप्राग्र्येषु समर्पयेत् ॥
1.114.m: then, having circumambulated that wealth and bowed down, / having prayed with devotion, he should give it to the foremost of brāhmaṇas:

1.114.s:
yadidaṃ svarṇaraupyādi dravyaṃ vai viprasātkṛtam /
tadanantaphalaṃ bhūyānmama janmani janmani //
1.114.d:
यदिदं स्वर्णरौप्यादि द्रव्यं वै विप्रसात्कृतम् ।
तदनन्तफलं भूयान्मम जन्मनि जन्मनि ॥
1.114.m: 'This wealth, consisting of gold, silver, and the like, which has been given to a brāhmaṇa, / may it yield endless fruit for me in birth after birth.'

1.114.s:
ityevaṃ dadato dravyaṃ bhaktibhāvena nārada /
prasannaḥ syāddhanādhyakṣaḥ svarṇādikasamṛddhidaḥ //
1.114.d:
इत्येवं ददतो द्रव्यं भक्तिभावेन नारद ।
प्रसन्नः स्याद्धनाध्यक्षः स्वर्णादिकसमृद्धिदः ॥
1.114.m: To him who gives wealth in this manner with devotion, O Nārada, / the lord of wealth will be pleased, granting abundance of gold and other riches.

1.114.s:
etadvrataṃ naraḥ kṛtvā viprānsaṃbhojya bhaktitaḥ /
paścātsvayaṃ ca bhuñjīta dārāpatyasuhṛddṛtaḥ //
1.114.d:
एतद्व्रतं नरः कृत्वा विप्रान्संभोज्य भक्तितः ।
पश्चात्स्वयं च भुञ्जीत दारापत्यसुहृद्दृतः ॥
1.114.m: A man having performed this observance and fed brāhmaṇas with devotion, / should afterwards himself eat, surrounded by wife, children, and friends.

1.114.s: bhādre tu kṛṣṇapañcamyāṃ nāgān kṣīreṇa tarpayet //
1.114.d: भाद्रे तु कृष्णपञ्चम्यां नागान् क्षीरेण तर्पयेत् ॥
1.114.m: On the dark fifth of Bhādrapada, he should satisfy the serpents with milk;

1.114.s:
yastasyā'saptamaṃ yāvatkulaṃ sarpātsunirbhayam /
bhādrasya śuklapañcamyāṃ pūjayedṛṣisattamān //
1.114.d:
यस्तस्याऽसप्तमं यावत्कुलं सर्पात्सुनिर्भयम् ।
भाद्रस्य शुक्लपञ्चम्यां पूजयेदृषिसत्तमान् ॥
1.114.m: for him, his family up to the seventh generation is completely free from fear of snakes. / On the bright fifth of Bhādrapada, one should worship the best of ṛṣis.

1.114.s:
prātarnadyādike snātvā kṛtvā nityamatandritaḥ /
gṛhamāgatya yatnena vedikāṃ kārayenmṛdā //
1.114.d:
प्रातर्नद्यादिके स्नात्वा कृत्वा नित्यमतन्द्रितः ।
गृहमागत्य यत्नेन वेदिकां कारयेन्मृदा ॥
1.114.m: Having bathed in the morning in a river or other water, unwearied, having performed the daily rites, / having come home, he should carefully make an altar of earth.

1.114.s:
gomayenopalipyātha kṛtvā puṣpopaśobhitām /
tatrāstīrya kuśānvipraṛṣīnsapta samarcayet //
1.114.d:
गोमयेनोपलिप्याथ कृत्वा पुष्पोपशोभिताम् ।
तत्रास्तीर्य कुशान्विप्रऋषीन्सप्त समर्चयेत् ॥
1.114.m: Having smeared it with cow dung and adorned it with flowers, / having spread kuśa grass there, O brāhmaṇa, he should worship the seven ṛṣis,

1.114.s:
gandhaiśca vividhaiḥ puṣpairdhūpairdīpaiḥ suśobhaneḥ /
kaśyapo 'trirbharadvājau viśvāmitro 'tha gautamaḥ //
1.114.d:
गन्धैश्च विविधैः पुष्पैर्धूपैर्दीपैः सुशोभनेः ।
कश्यपो ऽत्रिर्भरद्वाजौ विश्वामित्रो ऽथ गौतमः ॥
1.114.m: with diverse fragrant pastes, flowers, incense, and exceedingly splendid lamps: / Kaśyapa, Atri, Bharadvāja, Viśvāmitra, then Gautama,

1.114.s:
jamadagnirvasiṣṭhaśca saptaite ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
etaibhyo 'ghya ca vidhivatkalpayitvā pradāya ca //
1.114.d:
जमदग्निर्वसिष्ठश्च सप्तैते ऋषयः स्मृताः ।
एतैभ्यो ऽघ्य च विधिवत्कल्पयित्वा प्रदाय च ॥
1.114.m: Jamadagni, and Vasiṣṭha—these are remembered as the seven ṛṣis. / Having prepared and offered water of guest-reception to these according to rule,

1.114.s:
naivedyaṃ vipacedvīmānśyāmākādyairakṛṣṭakaiḥ /
tannivedya visṛjyemānsvayaṃ cādyāttadeva hi //
1.114.d:
नैवेद्यं विपचेद्वीमान्श्यामाकाद्यैरकृष्टकैः ।
तन्निवेद्य विसृज्येमान्स्वयं चाद्यात्तदेव हि ॥
1.114.m: the wise man should cook an oblation of food from uncultivated wild grains such as śyāmāka; / having offered that, having dismissed them, he himself should eat that very food.

1.114.s:
anena vidhinā sapta varṣāṇi prativatsaram /
kṛtvā vratānte varayedācāryān sapta vaidikān //
1.114.d:
अनेन विधिना सप्त वर्षाणि प्रतिवत्सरम् ।
कृत्वा व्रतान्ते वरयेदाचार्यान् सप्त वैदिकान् ॥
1.114.m: Every year according to this rule for seven years / having performed it, at the end of the observance he should select seven Vedic teachers.

1.114.s:
pratimāḥ saptakurvīnta suvarṇena svaśaktitaḥ /
jaṭilāḥ sākṣasūtrāśca kamaṇḍalusamanvitāḥ //
1.114.d:
प्रतिमाः सप्तकुर्वीन्त सुवर्णेन स्वशक्तितः ।
जटिलाः साक्षसूत्राश्च कमण्डलुसमन्विताः ॥
1.114.m: He should make seven images of gold according to his capacity, / having matted hair, accompanied by rosaries and water pots.

1.114.s:
saṃsthāpya kalaśeṣvetāṃstāmreṣu mṛnmayeṣu vā /
snāpayedvidhi vadbhaktyā pṛthakpañcāmṛtairapi //
1.114.d:
संस्थाप्य कलशेष्वेतांस्ताम्रेषु मृन्मयेषु वा ।
स्नापयेद्विधि वद्भक्त्या पृथक्पञ्चामृतैरपि ॥
1.114.m: Having installed them upon water vessels made of copper or of clay, / he should bathe them according to rule with devotion, also separately with the five nectars.

1.114.s:
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhistataḥ saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ /
arghyaṃ datvā tato homaṃ tilavrīhiyavādibhiḥ //
1.114.d:
उपचारैः षोडशभिस्ततः संपूज्य भक्तितः ।
अर्घ्यं दत्वा ततो होमं तिलव्रीहियवादिभिः ॥
1.114.m: Then, having worshipped them with devotion with sixteen ritual services, / having given water of guest-reception, then making fire oblations with sesame, unhusked rice, barley, and the like,

1.114.s:
ṭhasahastomā'iti ṛkhā nāmanantraistu vā pṛthak /
puṇyairmantraistathaivānyairhutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ caret //
1.114.d:
ठसहस्तोमाऽइति ऋखा नामनन्त्रैस्तु वा पृथक् ।
पुण्यैर्मन्त्रैस्तथैवान्यैर्हुत्वा पूर्णाहुतिं चरेत् ॥
1.114.m: with the verse beginning with 'sahasrastoma' or with their name-mantras separately, / and having offered oblations with other holy mantras, he should perform the final oblation.

1.114.s:
tatastu sapta gā dadyādvastrālaṅkārasaṃyutāḥ /
ācāryaṃ pūjayejjaiva vastrālaṅkārabhūṣaṇaiḥ //
1.114.d:
ततस्तु सप्त गा दद्याद्वस्त्रालङ्कारसंयुताः ।
आचार्यं पूजयेज्जैव वस्त्रालङ्कारभूषणैः ॥
1.114.m: Then he should give seven cows endowed with garments and ornaments; / and he should worship the teacher with garments and ornamental jewellery.

1.114.s:
anujñayā guroḥ paścānmūrtīrvipreṣu cārpayet /
bhojayitvā tu tānbhaktyā praṇipatya visarjayet //
1.114.d:
अनुज्ञया गुरोः पश्चान्मूर्तीर्विप्रेषु चार्पयेत् ।
भोजयित्वा तु तान्भक्त्या प्रणिपत्य विसर्जयेत् ॥
1.114.m: Afterwards, with the permission of the guru, he should give the images to the brāhmaṇas; / having fed them with devotion and bowed down, he should dismiss them.

1.114.s:
tataśceṣṭaiḥ sahāsīnaḥ svayaṃ brāhmaṇaśeṣitam /
bhuṅktvā vai ṣaḍrasopetaṃ pramudyātsaha bandhubhiḥ //
1.114.d:
ततश्चेष्टैः सहासीनः स्वयं ब्राह्मणशेषितम् ।
भुङ्क्त्वा वै षड्रसोपेतं प्रमुद्यात्सह बन्धुभिः ॥
1.114.m: Then, seated together with dear ones, having himself eaten / what was left by the brāhmaṇas, endowed with the six tastes, he should rejoice together with his kinsmen.

1.114.s:
etatkṛtvā vrataṃ gāṅgaṃ bhogānbhuktvātha vāñchitān /
saptarṣīṇāṃ prasādena vimānavarago bhavet //
1.114.d:
एतत्कृत्वा व्रतं गाङ्गं भोगान्भुक्त्वाथ वाञ्छितान् ।
सप्तर्षीणां प्रसादेन विमानवरगो भवेत् ॥
1.114.m: Having performed this observance, O son of Gaṅgā, having enjoyed desired pleasures, / through the grace of the seven ṛṣis he shall go upon an excellent celestial chariot.

1.114.s: āśvine śuklapañcamyāmupāṅgalalitāvratam //
1.114.d: आश्विने शुक्लपञ्चम्यामुपाङ्गललिताव्रतम् ॥
1.114.m: On the bright fifth of Āśvina is the Upāṅgalalitā observance.

1.114.s:
tasyāḥ svarṇamayīṃ mūrtiṃ śaktyā nirmāya nārada /
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ pūjayettāṃ vidhānataḥ //
1.114.d:
तस्याः स्वर्णमयीं मूर्तिं शक्त्या निर्माय नारद ।
उपचारैः षोडशभिः पूजयेत्तां विधानतः ॥
1.114.m: Having fashioned a golden image of her according to one's capacity, O Nārada, / one should worship her according to rule with the sixteen ritual services.

1.114.s:
pakvānnaṃ phalasaṃyuktaṃ saghṛtaṃ dakṣiṇānvitam /
dvijavaryāya dātavyaṃ vratasaṃpūrtihetave //
1.114.d:
पक्वान्नं फलसंयुक्तं सघृतं दक्षिणान्वितम् ।
द्विजवर्याय दातव्यं व्रतसंपूर्तिहेतवे ॥
1.114.m: Cooked food accompanied by fruits, with ghee and a priestly gift, / should be given to an eminent twice-born to complete the observance.

1.114.s:
"savāhanā śaktiyutā varadā pūjitā mayā /
mātarmāmanugṛhyātha gamyatāṃ nijamandiram //
1.114.d:
"सवाहना शक्तियुता वरदा पूजिता मया ।
मातर्मामनुगृह्याथ गम्यतां निजमन्दिरम् ॥
1.114.m: "Accompanied by your mount, endowed with power, the granter of boons, you have been worshipped by me; / O Mother, having favored me, go now to your own abode."

1.114.s:
kārtike śuklapañcamyāṃ jayāvratamanuttamam /
kartavyaṃ pāpanāśāya śraddhayā dvijasattama //
1.114.d:
कार्तिके शुक्लपञ्चम्यां जयाव्रतमनुत्तमम् ।
कर्तव्यं पापनाशाय श्रद्धया द्विजसत्तम ॥
1.114.m: On the bright fifth day of Kārtika, the incomparable Jayā observance / should be performed with faith for the destruction of sins, O best of the twice-born.

1.114.s:
pūjayitvā jayāṃ vipra yathāvidhi samāhitaḥ /
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhistataḥ śuciralaṅkṛtaḥ //
1.114.d:
पूजयित्वा जयां विप्र यथाविधि समाहितः ।
उपचारैः षोडशभिस्ततः शुचिरलङ्कृतः ॥
1.114.m: Having worshipped Jayā according to rule, collected in mind, O brahmin, / with sixteen offerings, then pure and adorned,

1.114.s:
vipraikaṃ bhojayeccāpi tasmai dattvā ca dakṣiṇām /
visarjayettataḥ paścātsvayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ //
1.114.d:
विप्रैकं भोजयेच्चापि तस्मै दत्त्वा च दक्षिणाम् ।
विसर्जयेत्ततः पश्चात्स्वयं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥
1.114.m: he should feed one brahmin, and having given him a priestly gift, / should dismiss him; thereafter he himself should eat, restrained in speech.

1.114.s:
yastu vai bhaktisaṃyuktaḥ snānaṃ kuryāj jayādine /
naśyanti tasya pāpāni siṃhākrāntā mṛgā yathā //
1.114.d:
यस्तु वै भक्तिसंयुक्तः स्नानं कुर्याज् जयादिने ।
नश्यन्ति तस्य पापानि सिंहाक्रान्ता मृगा यथा ॥
1.114.m: Whoever, endowed with devotion, bathes on the day of Jayā, / his sins perish just as deer attacked by a lion.

1.114.s:
yadaśvamedhāvabhṛthe phalaṃ snānena kīrtitam /
tatphalaṃ prāpyate viprasnānenāpi jayādine //
1.114.d:
यदश्वमेधावभृथे फलं स्नानेन कीर्तितम् ।
तत्फलं प्राप्यते विप्रस्नानेनापि जयादिने ॥
1.114.m: Whatever fruit is declared from bathing at the concluding bath of an horse-sacrifice, / that same fruit is attained, O brahmin, even by a bath on the day of Jayā.

1.114.s:
aputro labhate putraṃ vandhyā gabha ca vindati /
rogī rogātpramucyeta baddho mucyeta bandhanāt //
1.114.d:
अपुत्रो लभते पुत्रं वन्ध्या गभ च विन्दति ।
रोगी रोगात्प्रमुच्येत बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात् ॥
1.114.m: The sonless one obtains a son, and a barren woman conceives a child; / the diseased is freed from disease, and the bound is released from bondage.

1.114.s:
mārgaśukle ca pañcamyāṃ nāgāniṣṭvā vidhānataḥ /
nāgebhyo hyabhayaṃ labdhvā modate saha bāndhavaiḥ //
1.114.d:
मार्गशुक्ले च पञ्चम्यां नागानिष्ट्वा विधानतः ।
नागेभ्यो ह्यभयं लब्ध्वा मोदते सह बान्धवैः ॥
1.114.m: And having worshipped the serpents according to rule on the bright fifth day of Mārgaśīrṣa, / having indeed obtained fearlessness from serpents, he rejoices with his kinsmen.

1.114.s:
pauṣe 'pi śuklapañcamyāṃ sampūjya madhusūdanam /
labhate bāñchitānkāmānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
1.114.d:
पौषे ऽपि शुक्लपञ्चम्यां सम्पूज्य मधुसूदनम् ।
लभते बाञ्छितान्कामान्नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
1.114.m: Having worshipped the slayer of Madhu on the bright fifth day of Pauṣa as well, / he attains desired wishes; no doubt should be entertained here.

1.114.s:
pañcamyāṃ pratimāse tu śukle kṛṣṇe ca nārada /
pitṝṇāṃ pūjanaṃ śastaṃ nāgānāṃ cāpi sarvathā //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde dvādaśamāsasthapañcamīvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāma caturdaśādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.114.d:
पञ्चम्यां प्रतिमासे तु शुक्ले कृष्णे च नारद ।
पितॄणां पूजनं शस्तं नागानां चापि सर्वथा ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे द्वादशमासस्थपञ्चमीव्रतनिरूपणं नाम चतुर्दशाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.114.m:
Every month on the fifth day, in both the bright and dark fortnights, O Nārada, / the worship of the ancestors and of the serpents is always praised.

Thus ends the one hundred and fourteenth chapter, entitled 'Determination of the Fifth-Day Observances in the Twelve Months', in the fourth quarter in the Great Narrative of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.115.s:
sanātana uvāca
śṛṇu vipra pravakṣyāmi ṣaṣṭhyāścaiva vratāni te /
yāni samyagvidhāyātra labhaghetsarvānmanorathān //
1.115.d:
सनातन उवाच
शृणु विप्र प्रवक्ष्यामि षष्ठ्याश्चैव व्रतानि ते ।
यानि सम्यग्विधायात्र लभघेत्सर्वान्मनोरथान् ॥
1.115.m: Sanātana said: / Listen, O brahmin, I shall declare to you the observances of the sixth day, / by properly performing which here one attains all desires.

1.115.s:
caitramāse śuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ kumāravratamuttamam /
tatreṣṭvā ṣaṇmukhaṃ devaṃ nānāpūjā vidhānataḥ //
1.115.d:
चैत्रमासे शुक्लषष्ठ्यां कुमारव्रतमुत्तमम् ।
तत्रेष्ट्वा षण्मुखं देवं नानापूजा विधानतः ॥
1.115.m: On the bright sixth day in the month of Caitra is the excellent Kumāra observance; / having worshipped the six-faced god there with various rituals according to rule,

1.115.s:
putraṃ sarvaguṇopetaṃ prāpnuyāccirajīvinam /
vaiśākhaśuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ ca pūjayitvā ca kārtikam //
1.115.d:
पुत्रं सर्वगुणोपेतं प्राप्नुयाच्चिरजीविनम् ।
वैशाखशुक्लषष्ठ्यां च पूजयित्वा च कार्तिकम् ॥
1.115.m: one obtains a long-lived son endowed with all good qualities. / And on the bright sixth day of Vaiśākha, having worshipped Kārttikeya,

1.115.s:
labhate mātṛjaṃ saukhyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
jyeṣṭhamāse śuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ vidhineṣṭvā divākaram //
1.115.d:
लभते मातृजं सौख्यं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
ज्येष्ठमासे शुक्लषष्ठ्यां विधिनेष्ट्वा दिवाकरम् ॥
