1.115.m: he obtains happiness derived from the mother; no doubt should be entertained here. / Having worshipped the sun according to rule on the bright sixth day of Jyeṣṭha,

1.115.s:
labhate vāñchitānkāmāṃstatprasādānna saṃśayaḥ /
āṣāḍhaśuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ vai skandavratamanuttamam //
1.115.d:
लभते वाञ्छितान्कामांस्तत्प्रसादान्न संशयः ।
आषाढशुक्लषष्ठ्यां वै स्कन्दव्रतमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.115.m: he obtains his desired wishes through his grace, there is no doubt. / On the bright sixth day of Āṣāḍha is the incomparable Skanda observance.

1.115.s:
upoṣya pūjayitvainaṃ śivomāpriyamātmajam /
labhate 'bhīpsitānkāmānputrapautrādisaṃtatīḥ //
1.115.d:
उपोष्य पूजयित्वैनं शिवोमाप्रियमात्मजम् ।
लभते ऽभीप्सितान्कामान्पुत्रपौत्रादिसंततीः ॥
1.115.m: Having fasted and worshipped this son dear to Śiva and Umā, / he obtains his longed-for wishes and an unbroken line of sons and grandsons.

1.115.s:
śrāvaṇe śuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu śarajanmānamarcayet /
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirbhaktyā paramayānvitaḥ //
1.115.d:
श्रावणे शुक्लषष्ठ्यां तु शरजन्मानमर्चयेत् ।
उपचारैः षोडशभिर्भक्त्या परमयान्वितः ॥
1.115.m: On the bright sixth day of Śrāvaṇa, he should worship the reed-born one / with sixteen offerings, filled with supreme devotion.

1.115.s:
labhate 'bhīpsitānarthānṣaṇmukhasya prasādataḥ /
bhādramāse kṛṣṇaṣaṣṭyāṃ lalitāvratamucyate //
1.115.d:
लभते ऽभीप्सितानर्थान्षण्मुखस्य प्रसादतः ।
भाद्रमासे कृष्णषष्ट्यां ललिताव्रतमुच्यते ॥
1.115.m: He attains desired aims by the grace of the six-faced one. / On the dark sixth day in the month of Bhādrapada, the Lalitā observance is declared.

1.115.s:
prātaḥ snātvā vidhānena nārī śuklāmbarāvṛtā /
śuktamālyayadharā vāpi nadyāḥ saṃgamavālukām //
1.115.d:
प्रातः स्नात्वा विधानेन नारी शुक्लाम्बरावृता ।
शुक्तमाल्ययधरा वापि नद्याः संगमवालुकाम् ॥
1.115.m: Having bathed in the morning according to rule, a woman, clad in white garments / or wearing white garlands, [taking] sand from a river confluence,

1.115.s:
gṛhītvā vaṃśapātre tu dhṛtvā piṇḍākṛtiṃ ca tām /
pañcadhā lalitāṃ tatra dhyāyedvanavilāsinīm //
1.115.d:
गृहीत्वा वंशपात्रे तु धृत्वा पिण्डाकृतिं च ताम् ।
पञ्चधा ललितां तत्र ध्यायेद्वनविलासिनीम् ॥
1.115.m: taking it and placing it in a bamboo vessel in the shape of a lump, / should meditate there fivefold on Lalitā who sports in the woods.

1.115.s:
paṅkajaṃ karavīraṃ ca nepālīṃ mālatīṃ tathā /
nīlotpalaṃ ketakīṃ ca saṃgṛhya tagaraṃ tathā //
1.115.d:
पङ्कजं करवीरं च नेपालीं मालतीं तथा ।
नीलोत्पलं केतकीं च संगृह्य तगरं तथा ॥
1.115.m: Having gathered lotus, karavīra, nepālī, and mālatī, / blue lotus, ketakī, and tagara,

1.115.s:
ekaikāṣṭaśataṃ grāhyamaṣṭāviṃśatireva ca /
akṣatāḥ kalikā gṛhya tābhirdevīṃ prapūjayet //
1.115.d:
एकैकाष्टशतं ग्राह्यमष्टाविंशतिरेव च ।
अक्षताः कलिका गृह्य ताभिर्देवीं प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.115.m: taking one hundred and eight or twenty-eight of each, / and taking unhusked rice grains and buds, she should worship the goddess with them.

1.115.s:
prārthayedagrataḥ sthitvā devīṃ tāṃ giriśapriyām /
gaṅgādvāre kuśāvartte vilvake nīlaparvate //
1.115.d:
प्रार्थयेदग्रतः स्थित्वा देवीं तां गिरिशप्रियाम् ।
गङ्गाद्वारे कुशावर्त्ते विल्वके नीलपर्वते ॥
1.115.m: Standing before her, she should pray to that goddess dear to the mountain-dweller: / "At Gaṅgādvāra, Kuśāvarta, Bilvaka, and Nīlaparvata,

1.115.s:
snātvā kanakhale devi harariṃ labdhavatī patim /
lalite subhagaṃ devi sukhasaubhāgyadāyini //
1.115.d:
स्नात्वा कनखले देवि हररिं लब्धवती पतिम् ।
ललिते सुभगं देवि सुखसौभाग्यदायिनि ॥
1.115.m: having bathed at Kanakhala, O goddess, you obtained Hari [i.e., Hara] as your husband. / O Lalitā, beautiful goddess, giver of happiness and good fortune!"

1.115.s:
anataṃ dahi saubhāgyemahyaṃ tubhyaṃ namo 'namanaḥ /
mantreṇānena kusumaiśvaṃpakasya suśobhanaiḥ //
1.115.d:
अनतं दहि सौभाग्येमह्यं तुभ्यं नमो ऽनमनः ।
मन्त्रेणानेन कुसुमैश्वंपकस्य सुशोभनैः ॥
1.115.m:
‘Grant me boundless good fortune; homage, homage unto you!’
With this mantra, having duly worshipped [her] with very beautiful campaka flowers,

1.115.s:
abhyarcya vidhivattasyā navaidyaṃ purato nyaset /
trapuṣairapi kūṣmāṇḍairnālikeraiḥ sudāḍimaiḥ //
1.115.d:
अभ्यर्च्य विधिवत्तस्या नवैद्यं पुरतो न्यसेत् ।
त्रपुषैरपि कूष्माण्डैर्नालिकेरैः सुदाडिमैः ॥
1.115.m:
one should place before her an offering of food,
along with cucumbers, ash gourds, coconuts, fine pomegranates,

1.115.s:
bījapūraiḥ sutuḍīraiḥ kāravallaiḥ sacirbhaṭaiḥ /
phalaistatkālasaṃbhūtaiḥ kṛtvā śobhāṃ tadagrataḥ //
1.115.d:
बीजपूरैः सुतुडीरैः कारवल्लैः सचिर्भटैः ।
फलैस्तत्कालसंभूतैः कृत्वा शोभां तदग्रतः ॥
1.115.m:
citrons, fine tuḍīras, bitter gourds, and cirbhaṭas,
having made an attractive display before her with fruits produced at that season,

1.115.s:
virūḍhadhānyāṅkurakaiḥ sudīpāvalibhistathā /
sāddhai sargaṇakaidhūpaḥ sauhālakakarañjakaiḥ //
1.115.d:
विरूढधान्याङ्कुरकैः सुदीपावलिभिस्तथा ।
साद्धै सर्गणकैधूपः सौहालककरञ्जकैः ॥
1.115.m:
with sprouted grains, and likewise with rows of bright lamps,
with incense along with its accessories, and with sauhālakas and karañjakas,

1.115.s:
guḍapuṣpaiḥ karṇaveṣṭaḍairmodakairupamodakaiḥ /
bahuprakārairnaivedyairyathā vibhavasārataḥ //
1.115.d:
गुडपुष्पैः कर्णवेष्टडैर्मोदकैरुपमोदकैः ।
बहुप्रकारैर्नैवेद्यैर्यथा विभवसारतः ॥
1.115.m:
with guḍapuṣpas, karṇaveṣṭas, modakas, and minor sweets,
with many kinds of offerings of food according to the extent of one's wealth.

1.115.s:
evamabhyarcya vidhivadrātrau jāgaraṇotsavam /
gītavādyanaṭairnṛtyaiḥ prokṣaṇīyairanekadhā //
1.115.d:
एवमभ्यर्च्य विधिवद्रात्रौ जागरणोत्सवम् ।
गीतवाद्यनटैर्नृत्यैः प्रोक्षणीयैरनेकधा ॥
1.115.m:
Having thus worshipped according to rule, a festival of night vigil
accompanied by songs, instrumental music, actors, dances, and various rites to be displayed—

1.115.s:
sakhībhiḥ sahitā sādhvī tāṃ rātriṃ prasabhaṃ nayet /
na ca saṃmīlayennetre nārīyāmacatuṣṭayam //
1.115.d:
सखीभिः सहिता साध्वी तां रात्रिं प्रसभं नयेत् ।
न च संमीलयेन्नेत्रे नारीयामचतुष्टयम् ॥
1.115.m:
together with her female companions, the virtuous woman should spend that night with effort,
and the woman should not close her eyes for the four watches of the night.

1.115.s:
durbhagā duṣkṛtā vandhyā netrasaṃmīlanādbhavet /
evaṃ jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā saptamyāṃ saritaṃ nayet //
1.115.d:
दुर्भगा दुष्कृता वन्ध्या नेत्रसंमीलनाद्भवेत् ।
एवं जागरणं कृत्वा सप्तम्यां सरितं नयेत् ॥
1.115.m:
From closing her eyes, she would become ill-fated, wicked, and barren.
Having thus kept vigil, on the seventh day she should take [the image] to the river.

1.115.s:
gandhapuṣpaistathābhyarcya gītavādyapuraḥsaraiḥ /
tacca dadyāddvijendrāya naivedyādi dvijottama //
1.115.d:
गन्धपुष्पैस्तथाभ्यर्च्य गीतवाद्यपुरःसरैः ।
तच्च दद्याद्द्विजेन्द्राय नैवेद्यादि द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.115.m:
Having worshipped with fragrant pastes and flowers preceded by song and instrumental music,
she should give that offering of food and the rest to a noble twice-born, O best of the twice-born.

1.115.s:
snātvā gṛhaṃ samāgatya hutvā vaiśvānaraṃ tataḥ /
devānpitṝnmanuṣyāṃśca pūjayitvā suvāsinīḥ //
1.115.d:
स्नात्वा गृहं समागत्य हुत्वा वैश्वानरं ततः ।
देवान्पितॄन्मनुष्यांश्च पूजयित्वा सुवासिनीः ॥
1.115.m:
Having bathed, returned home, and then made an offering into the fire,
having worshipped the gods, ancestors, men, and married women,

1.115.s:
kanyakāścaiva saṃbhojya brāhmaṇāndaśa pañca ca /
bhakṣyabhojyairbahuvidhairdatvā dānāni bhūriśaḥ //
1.115.d:
कन्यकाश्चैव संभोज्य ब्राह्मणान्दश पञ्च च ।
भक्ष्यभोज्यैर्बहुविधैर्दत्वा दानानि भूरिशः ॥
1.115.m:
and having fed maidens and fifteen brāhmaṇas
with various kinds of edible foods, and given abundant gifts,

1.115.s:
lalitā me 'stu suprītā ityuktvā tānvisarjayet /
yaḥ kaścidācaredetadvrataṃ saubhāgyadaṃ param //
1.115.d:
ललिता मे ऽस्तु सुप्रीता इत्युक्त्वा तान्विसर्जयेत् ।
यः कश्चिदाचरेदेतद्व्रतं सौभाग्यदं परम् ॥
1.115.m:
saying, ‘May Lalitā be well pleased with me,’ she should dismiss them.
Whoever performs this foremost vow that grants good fortune—

1.115.s:
naro vā yadi vā nārī tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu /
yadvrataiśca tapobhiśca dānairvā niyamairapi //
1.115.d:
नरो वा यदि वा नारी तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ।
यद्व्रतैश्च तपोभिश्च दानैर्वा नियमैरपि ॥
1.115.m:
whether a man or a woman—listen to the meritorious fruit thereof.
Whatever is obtained by vows, austerities, gifts, or observances,

1.115.s:
tadeteneha labhyeta kiṃ bahūktena nārada /
mṛteranantaraṃ prāpya śivalokaṃ sanātanam //
1.115.d:
तदेतेनेह लभ्येत किं बहूक्तेन नारद ।
मृतेरनन्तरं प्राप्य शिवलोकं सनातनम् ॥
1.115.m:
all that is obtained in this world by this [vow]; why say more, O Nārada?
After death, having attained the eternal world of Śiva,

1.115.s:
modate lalitādevyā śaive vai sakhivacciram /
nabhasye māsi yā śuklā ṣaṣṭhī sā candanāhvayā //
1.115.d:
मोदते ललितादेव्या शैवे वै सखिवच्चिरम् ।
नभस्ये मासि या शुक्ला षष्ठी सा चन्दनाह्वया ॥
1.115.m:
she rejoices for a long time like a companion of the goddess Lalitā in the realm of Śiva.
The bright sixth day in the month of Bhādrapada is known as Candanā.

1.115.s:
tasyāṃ devīṃ samabhyarcya labhate tatsalokatām /
rohiṇī pātabhaumaistu saṃyutā kapilā bhavet //
1.115.d:
तस्यां देवीं समभ्यर्च्य लभते तत्सलोकताम् ।
रोहिणी पातभौमैस्तु संयुता कपिला भवेत् ॥
1.115.m:
Having worshipped the goddess on it, one attains her world.
Joined with Rohiṇī, Pāta, and Tuesday, [a lunar day] becomes Kapilā.

1.115.s:
tasyāṃ raviṃ samabhyarcya vratī niyamatatparaḥ /
labhate vāñchitānkāmānbhāskarasya prasādataḥ //
1.115.d:
तस्यां रविं समभ्यर्च्य व्रती नियमतत्परः ।
लभते वाञ्छितान्कामान्भास्करस्य प्रसादतः ॥
1.115.m:
Having worshipped the Sun on that day, the observer of the vow, intent upon the rules,
attains his desired wishes through the grace of the Sun.

1.115.s:
annadānaṃ japo homaṃ pitṛdevarṣitarpaṇam /
sarvamevākṣayaṃ jñeyaṃ kṛtaṃ devarṣisattama //
1.115.d:
अन्नदानं जपो होमं पितृदेवर्षितर्पणम् ।
सर्वमेवाक्षयं ज्ञेयं कृतं देवर्षिसत्तम ॥
1.115.m:
Gift of food, recitation, fire oblation, and libations to ancestors and divine seers—
all performed [then] is to be known as imperishable, O best of divine seers.

1.115.s:
kapilāṃ dhenumabhyarcya vastramālyānule panaiḥ /
pradadyādvedaviduṣe dvādaśātmapratuṣṭaye //
1.115.d:
कपिलां धेनुमभ्यर्च्य वस्त्रमाल्यानुले पनैः ।
प्रदद्याद्वेदविदुषे द्वादशात्मप्रतुष्टये ॥
1.115.m:
Having worshipped a brown cow with garments, garlands, and ointments,
one should give it to a knower of the Vedas for the pleasure of the Twelve-formed [Sun].

1.115.s:
atheṣuśuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu pūjyā kātyāyanī dvija /
gandhādyairmaṅgaladravyairnaivedyairvividhaistathā //
1.115.d:
अथेषुशुक्लषष्ठ्यां तु पूज्या कात्यायनी द्विज ।
गन्धाद्यैर्मङ्गलद्रव्यैर्नैवेद्यैर्विविधैस्तथा ॥
1.115.m:
Now, on the bright sixth day of Āśvina, Kātyāyanī is to be worshipped, O twice-born,
with auspicious items such as fragrant pastes, and likewise with various offerings of food.

1.115.s:
tataḥ kṣamāpya deveśīṃ praṇipatya visarjayet /
pūjyātra saikatī mūrtiryadvā dvijasatī mudā //
1.115.d:
ततः क्षमाप्य देवेशीं प्रणिपत्य विसर्जयेत् ।
पूज्यात्र सैकती मूर्तिर्यद्वा द्विजसती मुदा ॥
1.115.m:
Then, asking forgiveness of the queen of gods and bowing down, one should bid farewell to her.
An image made of sand is to be worshipped here, or a twice-born virtuous woman with joy,

1.115.s:
vastrālaṅkaraṇairbhavyaiḥ kātyāyinyāḥ pratuṣṭaye /
kanyā varaṃ prāpnuyācca vāñcitaṃ putramaṅganā //
1.115.d:
वस्त्रालङ्करणैर्भव्यैः कात्यायिन्याः प्रतुष्टये ।
कन्या वरं प्राप्नुयाच्च वाञ्चितं पुत्रमङ्गना ॥
1.115.m:
with splendid garments and ornaments, for the pleasure of Kātyāyanī.
A maiden will obtain a desired husband, and a woman a son,

1.115.s:
kātyāyinīprasādādvai nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
kārtike śuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu ṣaṇmukhena mahātmanā //
1.115.d:
कात्यायिनीप्रसादाद्वै नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
कार्तिके शुक्लषष्ठ्यां तु षण्मुखेन महात्मना ॥
1.115.m:
through the grace of Kātyāyinī; no doubt should be entertained here.
On the bright sixth day of Kārttika, by the great-souled six-faced one (Skanda),

1.115.s:
devasenā mahābhāgā labdhā sarvusurārpitā /
atastasyāṃ suraśreṣṭhāṃ devasenāṃ ca ṣaṇmukham //
1.115.d:
देवसेना महाभागा लब्धा सर्वुसुरार्पिता ।
अतस्तस्यां सुरश्रेष्ठां देवसेनां च षण्मुखम् ॥
1.115.m:
the highly fortunate Devasenā was obtained, given by all the gods.
Therefore, having worshipped the foremost of goddesses, Devasenā, and the six-faced one on that day,

1.115.s:
saṃpūjya nikhilaireva upacārairmanoharaiḥ /
prāpnuyādatulāṃ siddhiṃ manobhīṣṭāṃ dvijottama //
1.115.d:
संपूज्य निखिलैरेव उपचारैर्मनोहरैः ।
प्राप्नुयादतुलां सिद्धिं मनोभीष्टां द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.115.m:
with all delightful services,
one will attain matchless success desired by the mind, O best of the twice-born.

1.115.s:
atraiva vahnipūjoktāṃ tāṃ ca sampaksamācaret /
vividhadravyahomaiśca vahnipūjāpuraḥ saram //
1.115.d:
अत्रैव वह्निपूजोक्तां तां च सम्पक्समाचरेत् ।
विविधद्रव्यहोमैश्च वह्निपूजापुरः सरम् ॥
1.115.m:
Right here, worship of the fire is proclaimed, and one should perform it properly,
preceded by worship of fire with oblations of various substances.

1.115.s:
mārgaśīrṣe śaklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ nihatastārakāsuraḥ /
skandena satkṛtiḥ prāptā brahamādyaiḥ parikalpitā //
1.115.d:
मार्गशीर्षे शक्लषष्ठ्यां निहतस्तारकासुरः ।
स्कन्देन सत्कृतिः प्राप्ता ब्रहमाद्यैः परिकल्पिता ॥
1.115.m:
On the bright sixth day of Mārgaśīrṣa, the demon Tāraka was slain;
honour arranged by Brahmā and the others was received by Skanda.

1.115.s:
tato 'syāṃ pūjayetskandaṃ gandhapuṣpākṣataiḥ phalaiḥ /
vastrairābhūṣaṇaścāpi naivedyairvividhaistathā //
1.115.d:
ततो ऽस्यां पूजयेत्स्कन्दं गन्धपुष्पाक्षतैः फलैः ।
वस्त्रैराभूषणश्चापि नैवेद्यैर्विविधैस्तथा ॥
1.115.m:
Therefore, on this [day] one should worship Skanda with fragrant pastes, flowers, unbroken grains, and fruits,
with garments and ornaments, and likewise with various offerings of food.

1.115.s:
ravivāreṇa saṃyuktā tathā śatabhiṣānvitā /
yadi cetsā samuddiṣṭā caṃpāhvā munisattama //
1.115.d:
रविवारेण संयुक्ता तथा शतभिषान्विता ।
यदि चेत्सा समुद्दिष्टा चंपाह्वा मुनिसत्तम ॥
1.115.m:
If it is combined with a Sunday and likewise associated with the Śatabhiṣaj [nakṣatra],
that [day] is designated as Caṃpā, O best of sages.

1.115.s:
tasyāṃ viśveśvaro devo draṣṭavyaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ /
pūjanīyo vedanīyaḥ smartavyaḥ saukhyamicchatā //
1.115.d:
तस्यां विश्वेश्वरो देवो द्रष्टव्यः पापनाशनः ।
पूजनीयो वेदनीयः स्मर्तव्यः सौख्यमिच्छता ॥
1.115.m:
On that day, Lord Viśveśvara, the destroyer of sins, should be seen;
he should be worshipped, known, and remembered by one who desires happiness.

1.115.s:
snānadānādikaṃ cātra sarvamakṣayyamucyate /
pauṣamāse śuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ devo dinapatirdvija //
1.115.d:
स्नानदानादिकं चात्र सर्वमक्षय्यमुच्यते ।
पौषमासे शुक्लषष्ठ्यां देवो दिनपतिर्द्विज ॥
1.115.m:
Bathing, giving of gifts, and the like done here is all declared to be imperishable.
On the bright sixth day in the month of Pauṣa, O twice-born, the god who is the lord of day,

1.115.s: viṣṇurūpī jagattrātā pradurbhūtāḥ sanātanaḥ //
1.115.d: विष्णुरूपी जगत्त्राता प्रदुर्भूताः सनातनः ॥
1.115.m: having the form of Viṣṇu, the protector of the universe, the eternal one, became manifest.

1.115.s:
sa tasmātpūjanīyo 'syāṃ dravyairgandhapuraskṛtaiḥ /
naivedyairvasttrabhūṣādyaiḥ sarvasaukhyamabhīpsubhiḥ //
1.115.d:
स तस्मात्पूजनीयो ऽस्यां द्रव्यैर्गन्धपुरस्कृतैः ।
नैवेद्यैर्वस्त्त्रभूषाद्यैः सर्वसौख्यमभीप्सुभिः ॥
1.115.m:
Therefore, he should be worshipped on this [day] with substances preceded by fragrant pastes,
with food offerings, garments, ornaments, and the like, by those desiring all happiness.

1.115.s:
māghamāse sitā ṣaṣṭhī varuṇāhvā smṛtā tu sā /
tasyāṃ varuṇamabhyarcyedviṣṇurūpaṃ sanātanam //
1.115.d:
माघमासे सिता षष्ठी वरुणाह्वा स्मृता तु सा ।
तस्यां वरुणमभ्यर्च्येद्विष्णुरूपं सनातनम् ॥
1.115.m:
The bright sixth day in the month of Māgha is remembered as Varuṇā;
on it, one should worship Varuṇa, who has the form of Viṣṇu, the eternal one,

1.115.s:
raktairgandhāṃśukaiḥ puṣpairnaivedyairdhūpadīpakaiḥ /
evamabhyarcya vidhivadyadyaccābhilaṣennaraḥ //
1.115.d:
रक्तैर्गन्धांशुकैः पुष्पैर्नैवेद्यैर्धूपदीपकैः ।
एवमभ्यर्च्य विधिवद्यद्यच्चाभिलषेन्नरः ॥
1.115.m:
with red fragrant pastes, garments, flowers, offerings of food, incense, and lamps.
Having thus worshipped according to rule, whatever a person desires,

1.115.s:
tattacca phalato labdhvā modate tatprasādataḥ /
phaālgune śuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu devaṃ paśupatiṃ dvija //
1.115.d:
तत्तच्च फलतो लब्ध्वा मोदते तत्प्रसादतः ।
फआल्गुने शुक्लषष्ठ्यां तु देवं पशुपतिं द्विज ॥
1.115.m:
all that he obtains as the fruit, and rejoices through his grace.
On the bright sixth day in Phālguna, O twice-born, Lord Paśupati—

1.115.s:
mṛnmayaṃ vidhinā kṛttvā pūjayedupacārakaiḥ /
saṃsnāpya śatarudreṇa pṛthakpañcāmṛtairjalaiḥ //
1.115.d:
मृन्मयं विधिना कृत्त्वा पूजयेदुपचारकैः ।
संस्नाप्य शतरुद्रेण पृथक्पञ्चामृतैर्जलैः ॥
1.115.m:
having fashioned [an image] out of clay according to rule, one should worship [him] with the services,
having bathed [him] with the Śatarudrīya, and separately with the five nectars and water;

1.115.s:
gandhairālipya suśvetairakṣataiḥ śvetapuṣpakaiḥ /
bilvapatraiśca dhattūrakusumaiśca phalaistathā //
1.115.d:
गन्धैरालिप्य सुश्वेतैरक्षतैः श्वेतपुष्पकैः ।
बिल्वपत्रैश्च धत्तूरकुसुमैश्च फलैस्तथा ॥
1.115.m:
having anointed [him] with fragrant pastes, with pure white unbroken grains and white flowers,
with leaves of bilva, flowers of dhattūra, and fruits;

1.115.s:
sampūjya nānānaivedyairnīrājya vidhivattataḥ /
kṣamāpya praṇipatyainaṃ kailāsāya visarjayet //
1.115.d:
सम्पूज्य नानानैवेद्यैर्नीराज्य विधिवत्ततः ।
क्षमाप्य प्रणिपत्यैनं कैलासाय विसर्जयेत् ॥
1.115.m:
having worshipped with various offerings of food, and then waved lamps according to rule,
having asked forgiveness and bowed down to him, one should bid him farewell to Kailāsa.

1.115.s:
evaṃ kṛta śivārcastu naro nāryathavā mune /
iha bhuktvā varānbhogānante śivagatiṃ labhet //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde dvādaśamāsasthitaṣaṣṭhīvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcadaśādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.115.d:
एवं कृत शिवार्चस्तु नरो नार्यथवा मुने ।
इह भुक्त्वा वरान्भोगानन्ते शिवगतिं लभेत् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे द्वादशमासस्थितषष्ठीव्रतनिरूपणं नाम पञ्चदशाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.115.m:
A man or a woman who has thus performed the worship of Śiva, O sage,
having enjoyed excellent pleasures in this world, attains the state of Śiva at the end.

Thus ends the one hundred and fifteenth chapter, named 'Description of the Vows of the Sixth Lunar Day in the Twelve Months', in the fourth quarter of the major narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.116.s:
sanātana uvāca
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi saptamyāste vratānyaham /
yāni kṛtvā naro bhaktyā sūryasāyujyamāpnuyāt //
1.116.d:
सनातन उवाच
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि सप्तम्यास्ते व्रतान्यहम् ।
यानि कृत्वा नरो भक्त्या सूर्यसायुज्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.116.m:
Sanātana said:
Listen, O Nārada, I will tell you the vows of the seventh lunar day,
by performing which with devotion a man attains union with the Sun.

1.116.s:
caitre tu śuklasaptamyāṃ bahiḥ snānaṃ samācaret /
sthaṇḍile gomayālipte gauramṛttikayāstṛte //
1.116.d:
चैत्रे तु शुक्लसप्तम्यां बहिः स्नानं समाचरेत् ।
स्थण्डिले गोमयालिप्ते गौरमृत्तिकयास्तृते ॥
1.116.m:
On the bright seventh day of Caitra, one should take a bath outdoors.
On a raised mound smeared with cow dung and covered with white clay,

1.116.s:
likhitvāṣṭadalaṃ padmaṃ karṇikāyāṃ vibhāvam /
vinyasetpūrvapatre tu devau dvau kṛtadhātukau //
1.116.d:
लिखित्वाष्टदलं पद्मं कर्णिकायां विभावम् ।
विन्यसेत्पूर्वपत्रे तु देवौ द्वौ कृतधातुकौ ॥
1.116.m:
having drawn an eight-petalled lotus, one should place the radiant [Sun] in the pericarp,
and on the eastern petal two gods who are the Dhātṛs;

1.116.s:
āgneyaṃ ca nyasenpatre gandharvauṃ kṛtakārakau /
dakṣiṇe ca nyasetpatre tathaiva rākṣasadvayam //
1.116.d:
आग्नेयं च न्यसेन्पत्रे गन्धर्वौं कृतकारकौ ।
दक्षिणे च न्यसेत्पत्रे तथैव राक्षसद्वयम् ॥
1.116.m:
on the south-eastern petal one should place two gandharvas as attendants;
and on the southern petal likewise two rākṣasas;

1.116.s:
ākṛtau dvau nyasetpatre nairṛte munisattama /
kādraveyau mahānāgau paścime kṛtacārakau //
1.116.d:
आकृतौ द्वौ न्यसेत्पत्रे नैरृते मुनिसत्तम ।
काद्रवेयौ महानागौ पश्चिमे कृतचारकौ ॥
1.116.m:
one should place two forms on the south-western petal, O best of sages;
two great serpents, offspring of Kadrū, as attendants on the western;

1.116.s:
vāyavya yātudhānau dvau uttare ca ṛṣidvayam /
aiśānye vinyasetpatpe grahameko dvijottama //
1.116.d:
वायव्य यातुधानौ द्वौ उत्तरे च ऋषिद्वयम् ।
ऐशान्ये विन्यसेत्पत्पे ग्रहमेको द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.116.m:
on the north-western two yātudhānas, and on the northern two seers;
on the north-eastern petal one should place a single planet, O best of the twice-born.

1.116.s:
teṣāṃ saṃpūjanaṃ kāryaṃ gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ /
dīpairdhūpaiḥ sanaivedyaistāṃbūlakramukādibhiḥ //
1.116.d:
तेषां संपूजनं कार्यं गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः ।
दीपैर्धूपैः सनैवेद्यैस्तांबूलक्रमुकादिभिः ॥
1.116.m:
Their worship should be performed with scents, garlands, and unguents,
with lamps, incenses, food offerings, betel, areca nuts, and so forth.

1.116.s:
evaṃ saṃpūjya homaṃ tu ghṛtenāṣṭaśataṃ caret /
sūryasyāṣṭāṣṭa cānyeṣāṃ pradadyādāhutīḥ kramāt //
1.116.d:
एवं संपूज्य होमं तु घृतेनाष्टशतं चरेत् ।
सूर्यस्याष्टाष्ट चान्येषां प्रदद्यादाहुतीः क्रमात् ॥
1.116.m:
Having thus worshiped, one should perform a fire oblation of one hundred and eight [offerings] with clarified butter;
one should offer eight oblations in sequence to the sun, and eight to each of the others,

1.116.s:
nāmamantreṇa vedyāṃ vā tataḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ dadet /
dakṣiṇā ca tato deyā dvijebhyaḥ śaktito dvija //
1.116.d:
नाममन्त्रेण वेद्यां वा ततः पूर्णाहुतिं ददेत् ।
दक्षिणा च ततो देया द्विजेभ्यः शक्तितो द्विज ॥
1.116.m:
with their name-mantras on the altar, and then offer the final oblation.
Then a sacrificial fee should be given to the twice-born according to one's means, O twice-born.

1.116.s:
etatkṛtvā vidhaānaṃ tu sarvasaukhyamavāpnuyāt /
dehānte maṇḍalaṃ bhānorbhattvā gacchetparaṃ padam //
1.116.d:
एतत्कृत्वा विधआनं तु सर्वसौख्यमवाप्नुयात् ।
देहान्ते मण्डलं भानोर्भत्त्वा गच्छेत्परं पदम् ॥
1.116.m:
Having performed this rite, one attains every happiness;
at the end of the body, piercing the orb of the sun, one goes to the supreme abode.

1.116.s:
vaiśākhaśuklasaptamyāṃ jahnunā jāhnavī svayam /
krodhātpītā punastyaktā karṇarandhrāttu dakṣiṇāt //
1.116.d:
वैशाखशुक्लसप्तम्यां जह्नुना जाह्नवी स्वयम् ।
क्रोधात्पीता पुनस्त्यक्ता कर्णरन्ध्रात्तु दक्षिणात् ॥
1.116.m:
On the bright seventh of Vaiśākha, the river Jāhnavī [Gaṅgā] herself
was drunk in anger by Jahnu, and released again from his right ear cavity.

1.116.s:
tāṃ tatra pūjayetsnātvā pratyūṣe vimale jale /
gandhapuṣpākṣatādyaiśca sarvairevopacārakaiḥ //
1.116.d:
तां तत्र पूजयेत्स्नात्वा प्रत्यूषे विमले जले ।
गन्धपुष्पाक्षताद्यैश्च सर्वैरेवोपचारकैः ॥
1.116.m:
Having bathed at dawn in pure water, one should worship her there
with scents, flowers, unhusked barley, and all the customary services.

1.116.s:
tato ghaṭasahasraṃ tu deyaṃ gaṅgāvrate tvidam /
bhaktyā kṛtaṃ saptakulaṃ nayetsvargamasaṃśayaḥ //
1.116.d:
ततो घटसहस्रं तु देयं गङ्गाव्रते त्विदम् ।
भक्त्या कृतं सप्तकुलं नयेत्स्वर्गमसंशयः ॥
1.116.m:
Then, in this observance of Gaṅgā, a thousand jars should be given;
performed with devotion, it leads seven generations to heaven, without a doubt.

1.116.s:
kamalavratamapyatra proktaṃ tadvidhirucyate /
tilamātraṃ tu sauvarṇaṃ vidhāya kamalaṃ śubham //
1.116.d:
कमलव्रतमप्यत्र प्रोक्तं तद्विधिरुच्यते ।
तिलमात्रं तु सौवर्णं विधाय कमलं शुभम् ॥
1.116.m:
The Lotus Observance is also taught here; its procedure is now told:
making an auspicious lotus of gold, just [the weight of] a sesamum seed,

1.116.s:
vastrayugmāvṛtaṃ kṛtvā gandhadhūpādinārcayet /
namaste padmahastāya namaste viśvadhāriṇe //
1.116.d:
वस्त्रयुग्मावृतं कृत्वा गन्धधूपादिनार्चयेत् ।
नमस्ते पद्महस्ताय नमस्ते विश्वधारिणे ॥
1.116.m:
and covering it with a pair of cloths, one should worship it with scents, incense, and the like:
‘Homage to you who hold a lotus in your hand! Homage to you who uphold the universe!

1.116.s:
divākara namastubhyaṃ prabhākara namo 'stu te /
iti saṃprārthya deveśaṃ sūrye cāstamupāgate //
1.116.d:
दिवाकर नमस्तुभ्यं प्रभाकर नमो ऽस्तु ते ।
इति संप्रार्थ्य देवेशं सूर्ये चास्तमुपागते ॥
1.116.m:
Homage to you, maker of the day! Homage be to you, maker of light!’
Having thus prayed to the lord of gods, when the sun has set,

1.116.s:
sodakuṃbhaṃ tu tatpadmaṃ kapilāṃ ca dvijer'payet /
taddine tūpavastavyaṃ bhoktavyaṃ ca pare 'hani //
1.116.d:
सोदकुंभं तु तत्पद्मं कपिलां च द्विजेर्ऽपयेत् ।
तद्दिने तूपवस्तव्यं भोक्तव्यं च परे ऽहनि ॥
1.116.m:
one should present that lotus along with a water-jar and a brown cow to a twice-born.
One must fast on that day and eat on the next day.

1.116.s:
saṃbhojya brāhmaṇānbhaktyā vratasākalyamāpnuyāt /
nibavrataṃ ca tatreva tadvidhānaṃ śṛṇuṣva me //
1.116.d:
संभोज्य ब्राह्मणान्भक्त्या व्रतसाकल्यमाप्नुयात् ।
निबव्रतं च तत्रेव तद्विधानं शृणुष्व मे ॥
1.116.m:
Having fed the brāhmaṇas with devotion, one attains the complete fruit of the observance.
And right there is the Nimba Observance; hear from me its procedure.

1.116.s:
niṃbapatraiḥ smṛtā pūjā bhāskarasya dvijottama /
khakholkāyeti mantreṇa praṇavādyena nārada //
1.116.d:
निंबपत्रैः स्मृता पूजा भास्करस्य द्विजोत्तम ।
खखोल्कायेति मन्त्रेण प्रणवाद्येन नारद ॥
1.116.m:
Worship of the sun with neem leaves is taught, O best of the twice-born,
with the mantra ‘To Khakholka’, preceded by the praṇava, O Nārada.

1.116.s:
niṃbapatraṃ tato 'śnīyācchayedbhūmau ca vāgyataḥ /
dvijānpare 'hni saṃbhojya svayaṃ bhuñjīta bandhubhiḥ //
1.116.d:
निंबपत्रं ततो ऽश्नीयाच्छयेद्भूमौ च वाग्यतः ।
द्विजान्परे ऽह्नि संभोज्य स्वयं भुञ्जीत बन्धुभिः ॥
1.116.m:
Then one should eat a neem leaf, and sleep on the ground, restrained in speech.
Having fed the twice-born on the next day, one should eat oneself along with relatives.

1.116.s:
niṃbapatravrataṃ caitatkartṛāṇāṃ sarvasaukhyadam /
saptamī śarkarākhyaiṣā proktā taccāpi me śṛṇu //
1.116.d:
निंबपत्रव्रतं चैतत्कर्तृआणां सर्वसौख्यदम् ।
सप्तमी शर्कराख्यैषा प्रोक्ता तच्चापि मे शृणु ॥
1.116.m:
And this Neem-leaf Observance grants all happiness to its performers.
This seventh day named Śarkarā is taught; hear that also from me.

1.116.s:
amṛtaṃ pibato hastātsūryasyāmṛtabindavaḥ /
niṣpeturbhuvi cotpannāḥ śālimudgayavekṣavaḥ //
1.116.d:
अमृतं पिबतो हस्तात्सूर्यस्यामृतबिन्दवः ।
निष्पेतुर्भुवि चोत्पन्नाः शालिमुद्गयवेक्षवः ॥
1.116.m:
As the sun drank the nectar, drops of nectar fell from his hand
upon the earth, and from them arose winter-rice, mung beans, barley, and sugarcane.

1.116.s:
śarkarā ca tatastasmādikṣusārāmṛtopamā /
iṣṭā raverataḥ puṇyā śarkarā havyakavyayoḥ //
1.116.d:
शर्करा च ततस्तस्मादिक्षुसारामृतोपमा ।
इष्टा रवेरतः पुण्या शर्करा हव्यकव्ययोः ॥
1.116.m:
And from that [came] sugar, comparable to the nectar-essence of sugarcane;
therefore, sugar is dear to the sun and auspicious in offerings to gods and ancestors.

1.116.s:
śarkarāsaptamī caiva vājimedhapalapradā /
sarvaduḥkhopaśamanī putrasaṃtativardhinī //
1.116.d:
शर्करासप्तमी चैव वाजिमेधपलप्रदा ।
सर्वदुःखोपशमनी पुत्रसंततिवर्धिनी ॥
1.116.m:
And this Śarkarāsaptamī bestows the fruit of a horse-sacrifice;
it pacifies all sorrows and increases sons and progeny.

1.116.s:
asyāntu śarkarādānaṃ śarkarābhojanaṃ tathā /
kartavyaṃ hi prayatnena vratame tadravipriyam //
1.116.d:
अस्यान्तु शर्करादानं शर्कराभोजनं तथा ।
कर्तव्यं हि प्रयत्नेन व्रतमे तद्रविप्रियम् ॥
1.116.m:
On this [tithi], the gift of sugar as well as the eating of sugar
must be performed with effort; this observance is dear to the sun.

1.116.s:
yaḥ kuryātparāyā bhaktyā sa vai sadgatimāpnuyāt /
jyeṣṭhe tu śuklasaptamyāṃ jāta indro raviḥ svayam //
1.116.d:
यः कुर्यात्पराया भक्त्या स वै सद्गतिमाप्नुयात् ।
ज्येष्ठे तु शुक्लसप्तम्यां जात इन्द्रो रविः स्वयम् ॥
1.116.m:
Whoever performs it with supreme devotion attains the good realm.
On the bright seventh of Jyeṣṭha, Indra was born as the sun himself.

1.116.s:
taṃ saṃpūjya vidhānena sopavāso jitendriyaḥ /
svargatiṃ labhate vipra devendrasya prasādataḥ //
1.116.d:
तं संपूज्य विधानेन सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः ।
स्वर्गतिं लभते विप्र देवेन्द्रस्य प्रसादतः ॥
1.116.m:
Having worshiped him according to rule, fasting and with senses controlled,
one attains a heavenly realm by the grace of the lord of the gods, O brāhmaṇa.

1.116.s:
āṣāḍhaśuklasaptamyāṃ vivasvānnāma bhāskaraḥ /
jātastaṃ tatra saṃprārcya gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ pṛthak //
1.116.d:
आषाढशुक्लसप्तम्यां विवस्वान्नाम भास्करः ।
जातस्तं तत्र संप्रार्च्य गन्धपुष्पादिभिः पृथक् ॥
1.116.m:
On the bright seventh of Āṣāḍha, the sun named Vivasvat
was born; having worshiped him there with scents, flowers, and the like separately,

1.116.s:
labhate sūryasāyujyaṃ viprendrātra na saṃśayaḥ /
śrāvaṇe śuklasaptamyāmavyaṅgākhyaṃ vrataṃ śubham //
kārpāsaṃ tu caturhastaṃ sārddha vastraṃ hi gopateḥ ///
1.116.d:
लभते सूर्यसायुज्यं विप्रेन्द्रात्र न संशयः ।
श्रावणे शुक्लसप्तम्यामव्यङ्गाख्यं व्रतं शुभम् ॥
कार्पासं तु चतुर्हस्तं सार्द्ध वस्त्रं हि गोपतेः ॥।
1.116.m:
one attains union with the sun, O best of the twice-born, of this there is no doubt.
On the bright seventh of Śrāvaṇa is the auspicious observance named Avyaṅga.

A cotton cloth four cubits long, together with a half-cloth, for the lord of rays [the Sun],

1.116.s: pūjānte prītaye deyaṃ vratametacchubhāvaham //
1.116.d: पूजान्ते प्रीतये देयं व्रतमेतच्छुभावहम् ॥
1.116.m: should be given at the end of the worship for his pleasure; this observance brings auspiciousness.

1.116.s:
yadi ceddhastayukteyaṃ tadā syātpāpanāśinī /
asyāṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ sarvaṃ cākṣayyatāṃ vrajet //
1.116.d:
यदि चेद्धस्तयुक्तेयं तदा स्यात्पापनाशिनी ।
अस्यां दानं जपो होमः सर्वं चाक्षय्यतां व्रजेत् ॥
1.116.m:
If this [tithi] is conjoined with the Hasta nakṣatra, then it destroys sins;
giving, recitation, and fire oblation on this day all become imperishable.

1.116.s:
bhādre tu śuklasaptamyāmamuktābharaṇavratam /
somasya tu maheśasya pūjanaṃ cātra kīrtitam //
1.116.d:
भाद्रे तु शुक्लसप्तम्याममुक्ताभरणव्रतम् ।
सोमस्य तु महेशस्य पूजनं चात्र कीर्तितम् ॥
1.116.m:
On the bright seventh of Bhādrapada is the Amuktābharaṇa Observance;
and the worship of Soma and Maheśa is proclaimed on this [tithi].

1.116.s:
gaṅgādibhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirupacāraiḥ samarcanam /
prārthya praṇamya visṛjetsarvakāmasamṛddhaye //
1.116.d:
गङ्गादिभिः षोडशभिरुपचारैः समर्चनम् ।
प्रार्थ्य प्रणम्य विसृजेत्सर्वकामसमृद्धये ॥
1.116.m:
Worshiping with the sixteen services, beginning with Gaṅgā [water],
praying, and bowing down, one should dismiss [the deity] for the attainment of all desires.

1.116.s:
phalasaptamikā ceyaṃ tadvidhānamudīryate /
nālikeraṃ ca vṛntākaṃ nāraṅgaṃ bījapūrakam //
1.116.d:
फलसप्तमिका चेयं तद्विधानमुदीर्यते ।
नालिकेरं च वृन्ताकं नारङ्गं बीजपूरकम् ॥
1.116.m:
And this is the Phalasaptamikā; its procedure is declared:
a coconut, an eggplant, an orange, a citron,

1.116.s:
kūṣmāṇḍaṃ bṛhatīpūgamiti sapta phalāni vai /
mahādevasya purato vinyasyāparadorakam //
1.116.d:
कूष्माण्डं बृहतीपूगमिति सप्त फलानि वै ।
महादेवस्य पुरतो विन्यस्यापरदोरकम् ॥
1.116.m:
a white pumpkin, a nightshade, and an areca nut—these seven fruits indeed
having placed before Mahādeva, and also another cord,

1.116.s:
saptatantukṛtaṃ saptagranthiyuktaṃ dvijottama /
saṃpūjya parayā bhaktyā dhārayedvāmake kare //
1.116.d:
सप्ततन्तुकृतं सप्तग्रन्थियुक्तं द्विजोत्तम ।
संपूज्य परया भक्त्या धारयेद्वामके करे ॥
1.116.m:
made of seven threads and tied with seven knots, O best of the twice-born,
having worshiped it with supreme devotion, a woman should wear it on her left hand,

1.116.s:
strī naro dakṣiṇe caiva yāvadvarṣaṃ samāpyate /
saṃbhojya viprānsaptaiva pāyasena visṛjyasa tān //
1.116.d:
स्त्री नरो दक्षिणे चैव यावद्वर्षं समाप्यते ।
संभोज्य विप्रान्सप्तैव पायसेन विसृज्यस तान् ॥
1.116.m:
and a man on the right, until the year is completed.
Having fed exactly seven brāhmaṇas with milk-rice and dismissed them,

1.116.s:
svayaṃ bhuñjīta matimān vratasaṃpūrtihetave /
phalāni tāni deyāni saptasvapi dvijeṣu ca //
1.116.d:
स्वयं भुञ्जीत मतिमान् व्रतसंपूर्तिहेतवे ।
फलानि तानि देयानि सप्तस्वपि द्विजेषु च ॥
1.116.m:
the wise one should eat oneself for the purpose of completing the observance.
Those fruits should also be given to seven twice-born men.

1.116.s:
evaṃ tu sapta varṣāṇi kṛtvopāsya yathāvidhi /
sāyujyaṃ labhate vipra mahādevasya tadvratī //
1.116.d:
एवं तु सप्त वर्षाणि कृत्वोपास्य यथाविधि ।
सायुज्यं लभते विप्र महादेवस्य तद्व्रती ॥
1.116.m:
Thus, having performed and worshiped according to rule for seven years,
the keeper of that observance attains union with Mahādeva, O brāhmaṇa.

1.116.s:
āśvine śuklapakṣe tu vijñeyā śubhasaptamī /
tasyāṃ kṛtasnānapūjo vācayitvā dvijottamān //
1.116.d:
आश्विने शुक्लपक्षे तु विज्ञेया शुभसप्तमी ।
तस्यां कृतस्नानपूजो वाचयित्वा द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
1.116.m:
The auspicious seventh is to be known in the bright fortnight of Āśvina.
Having performed bathing and worship on it, and having caused the best of the twice-born to recite blessings,

1.116.s:
ārabhya kapilāṅgāṃ ca saṃpūjya prārthayettataḥ /
tvāmahaṃ dadmi kalyāṇi prīyatāmaryamā svayam //
1.116.d:
आरभ्य कपिलाङ्गां च संपूज्य प्रार्थयेत्ततः ।
त्वामहं दद्मि कल्याणि प्रीयतामर्यमा स्वयम् ॥
1.116.m:
and having commenced [the rite] and worshiped the brown cow, one should then pray:
‘I give you, O auspicious one; may Aryaman himself be pleased!

1.116.s:
pālaya tvaṃ jagatkatsnaṃ yato 'si dharmasambhavā /
ityuktvā vedaviduṣe dattvā kṛtvā ca dakṣiṇām //
1.116.d:
पालय त्वं जगत्कत्स्नं यतो ऽसि धर्मसम्भवा ।
इत्युक्त्वा वेदविदुषे दत्त्वा कृत्वा च दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.116.m:
Protect the entire world, since you are born from dharma.’
Having spoken thus, having given it to one learned in the Veda and offered a sacrificial fee,

1.116.s:
namaskṛtya svayaṃ vipra visṛjetprāśayetvaravayam /
pacagavyaṃ vrataṃ cetthaṃ vidhāya śvo dvijottamān //
1.116.d:
नमस्कृत्य स्वयं विप्र विसृजेत्प्राशयेत्वरवयम् ।
पचगव्यं व्रतं चेत्थं विधाय श्वो द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
1.116.m:
and having personally bowed down, O brāhmaṇa, one should let [her] go, and should drink the five products of the cow.
Having thus performed the observance, on the next day, having fed the best of the twice-born,

1.116.s:
bhojayitvā svayaṃ cādyāttadannaṃ dvijaśeṣitam /
kṛtaṃ hyetadgataṃ vipra subhāṣyaṃ śraddhayānvitaḥ //
1.116.d:
भोजयित्वा स्वयं चाद्यात्तदन्नं द्विजशेषितम् ।
कृतं ह्येतद्गतं विप्र सुभाष्यं श्रद्धयान्वितः ॥
1.116.m:
one should oneself eat that food left by the twice-born.
This observance thus performed, O brāhmaṇa, spoken well by one endowed with faith,

1.116.s:
devadevaprasādena bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
atha kārtikaśuklāyāṃ śākākhyaṃ saptamīvratam //
1.116.d:
देवदेवप्रसादेन भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् ।
अथ कार्तिकशुक्लायां शाकाख्यं सप्तमीव्रतम् ॥
1.116.m:
one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation by the grace of the god of gods.
Now, on the bright [seventh] of Kārtika is the seventh-day observance called Śāka.

1.116.s:
tasyāṃ tu saptaśākānisasvarṇakamalāni ca /
pradadyātsaptaviprebhyaḥ śākāhārastataḥ svayam //
1.116.d:
तस्यां तु सप्तशाकानिसस्वर्णकमलानि च ।
प्रदद्यात्सप्तविप्रेभ्यः शाकाहारस्ततः स्वयम् ॥
1.116.m:
On it one should give seven vegetables along with golden lotuses
to seven twice-born men; then one should oneself eat only vegetables.

1.116.s:
dvitīye 'hni dvijānbhojya datvā tebhyo 'nnadakṣiṇām /
visṛjya bandhubhiḥ sārddhaṃ svayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ //
1.116.d:
द्वितीये ऽह्नि द्विजान्भोज्य दत्वा तेभ्यो ऽन्नदक्षिणाम् ।
विसृज्य बन्धुभिः सार्द्धं स्वयं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥
1.116.m:
On the second day, having fed the twice-born and given them food and a sacrificial fee,
and dismissed them, one should eat oneself along with relatives, restrained in speech.

1.116.s:
mārgasya sitasaptamyāṃ mitravratamudāhṛtam /
yadviṣṇordakṣiṇaṃ netraṃ tadeva kṛtavāniha //
1.116.d:
मार्गस्य सितसप्तम्यां मित्रव्रतमुदाहृतम् ।
यद्विष्णोर्दक्षिणं नेत्रं तदेव कृतवानिह ॥
1.116.m:
On the bright seventh of Mārgaśīrṣa, the Mitra Observance is declared,
which is the right eye of Viṣṇu; precisely that he performed here.

1.116.s:
adityāṃ kaśyapājjajñe mitro nāmā divākaraḥ /
ato 'syāṃ pūjanaṃ tasya yathoktavidhinā dvija //
1.116.d:
अदित्यां कश्यपाज्जज्ञे मित्रो नामा दिवाकरः ।
अतो ऽस्यां पूजनं तस्य यथोक्तविधिना द्विज ॥
1.116.m:
From Kaśyapa upon Aditi was born the sun named Mitra;
therefore, on this [tithi], worship of him [is prescribed] according to the stated rule, O twice-born.

1.116.s:
kṛtvā dvijānbhojayitvā saptaiva madhurādinā /
suvarṇadakṣiṇāṃ datvā visṛjyāśnīta ca svayam //
1.116.d:
कृत्वा द्विजान्भोजयित्वा सप्तैव मधुरादिना ।
सुवर्णदक्षिणां दत्वा विसृज्याश्नीत च स्वयम् ॥
1.116.m:
Having performed it, having fed seven twice-born with sweets and the like,
having given a gold fee and dismissed them, one should eat oneself.

1.116.s:
kṛtvaitadvidhinā lokaṃ sṛryyasya vrajati dhruvam /
dvijobrāhmaṃ tathā śūdraḥ satkulejanma cāpnuyāt //
1.116.d:
कृत्वैतद्विधिना लोकं सृर्य्यस्य व्रजति ध्रुवम् ।
द्विजोब्राह्मं तथा शूद्रः सत्कुलेजन्म चाप्नुयात् ॥
1.116.m:
Having performed this according to rule, a twice-born certainly goes to the realm of the sun,
and attains a birth in the world of Brahmā, while a śūdra attains birth in a noble family.

1.116.s:
pauṣasya śuklasaptamyāṃ vrataṃ cābhayasaṃjñitam /
upoṣya bhānuṃ triḥsandhyaṃ samabhyarcya dharāsthitaḥ //
1.116.d:
पौषस्य शुक्लसप्तम्यां व्रतं चाभयसंज्ञितम् ।
उपोष्य भानुं त्रिःसन्ध्यं समभ्यर्च्य धरास्थितः ॥
1.116.m:
On the bright seventh of Pauṣa is the observance named Abhaya.
Having fasted, remaining on the ground, having worshiped the sun at the three junctures of the day,

1.116.s:
kṣīrasiktānnasaṃbaddhaṃ modakaṃ prasthasaṃmitam /
dvijāya datvā bhojyānyānsaptāṣṭabhyaśca dakṣiṇām //
1.116.d:
क्षीरसिक्तान्नसंबद्धं मोदकं प्रस्थसंमितम् ।
द्विजाय दत्वा भोज्यान्यान्सप्ताष्टभ्यश्च दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.116.m:
having given to a twice-born a sweetmeat measuring a prastha, prepared with food soaked in milk,
and having fed other [brāhmaṇas], [one should give] a fee to seven or eight [of them].

1.116.s:
pṛthavī vā suvarṇaṃ vā visṛjyāśnīta ca svayam /
abhayākhyaṃ vrataṃ tvetatsarvasyābhayadaṃ smṛtam //
1.116.d:
पृथवी वा सुवर्णं वा विसृज्याश्नीत च स्वयम् ।
अभयाख्यं व्रतं त्वेतत्सर्वस्याभयदं स्मृतम् ॥
1.116.m: Or having given away land or gold, one should eat oneself. / This observance called Abhaya is traditionally regarded as granting freedom from fear to everyone.

1.116.s:
mārtaṇḍākhyaṃ vrataṃ nāma kathayanti dvijāḥ pare /
ekameveti ca proktamekadaivatayā budhaiḥ //
1.116.d:
मार्तण्डाख्यं व्रतं नाम कथयन्ति द्विजाः परे ।
एकमेवेति च प्रोक्तमेकदैवतया बुधैः ॥
1.116.m: Other twice-born call it the observance named Mārtaṇḍa; / it is declared by the wise to be one and the same because of having the same deity.

1.116.s:
māghe tu kṛṣṇasaptamyāṃ vrataṃ sarvāptisaṃjñakam /
samupoṣya dine tasminsampūjyādityabimbakam //
1.116.d:
माघे तु कृष्णसप्तम्यां व्रतं सर्वाप्तिसंज्ञकम् ।
समुपोष्य दिने तस्मिन्सम्पूज्यादित्यबिम्बकम् ॥
1.116.m: On the dark seventh of Māgha, however, there is the observance named Sarvāpti. / Having fasted on that day and fully worshipped the solar disc,

1.116.s:
sauvarṇaṃ gandhapuṣpādyaiḥ kṛtvā rātrau ca jāgaram /
pare 'hni viprānsambhojya pāyasena tu sapta vai //
1.116.d:
सौवर्णं गन्धपुष्पाद्यैः कृत्वा रात्रौ च जागरम् ।
परे ऽह्नि विप्रान्सम्भोज्य पायसेन तु सप्त वै ॥
1.116.m: made of gold, with fragrant perfumes, flowers, and the like, and having kept vigil at night, / on the next day having fed seven Brahmins with sweet milk-rice,

1.116.s:
dakṣiṇāṃ nālikerāṇi tebhyo datvā guruṃ tataḥ /
sauvarṇaṃ tu raverbimbaṃ yuktaṃ dakṣiṇayā nyayā //
1.116.d:
दक्षिणां नालिकेराणि तेभ्यो दत्वा गुरुं ततः ।
सौवर्णं तु रवेर्बिम्बं युक्तं दक्षिणया न्यया ॥
1.116.m: and having given them a sacrificial gift and coconuts, then to the preceptor / [giving] the golden disc of the sun along with a suitable sacrificial gift,

1.116.s:
samarpya ca bhṛśaṃ prārthya visṛjyādyātsvayaṃ tataḥ /
etatsarvāptidaṃ nāma saṃproktaṃ sārvakāmikam //
1.116.d:
समर्प्य च भृशं प्रार्थ्य विसृज्याद्यात्स्वयं ततः ।
एतत्सर्वाप्तिदं नाम संप्रोक्तं सार्वकामिकम् ॥
1.116.m: and having offered it, pray intensely, bid farewell, and then eat oneself. / This is declared to be the wish-fulfilling one called Sarvāptida [Granting All Attainments].

1.116.s:
vratasyāsya prabhāveṇa dvaitaṃ sidhyeddhi sarvathā /
māghasya śuklasaptamyāmacalākhyaṃ vrataṃ smṛtam //
1.116.d:
व्रतस्यास्य प्रभावेण द्वैतं सिध्येद्धि सर्वथा ।
माघस्य शुक्लसप्तम्यामचलाख्यं व्रतं स्मृतम् ॥
1.116.m: By the power of this observance, duality is surely overcome in every way. / On the bright seventh of Māgha, the observance named Acalā is remembered.

1.116.s:
trilocanajayantīyaṃ sarvapāpaharā smṛtā /
rathākhyā saptamī ceyaṃ cakravartitvadāyinī //
1.116.d:
त्रिलोचनजयन्तीयं सर्वपापहरा स्मृता ।
रथाख्या सप्तमी चेयं चक्रवर्तित्वदायिनी ॥
1.116.m: This birth-anniversary of the Three-Eyed One is remembered as removing all sins; / and this seventh named Rathā grants sovereign emperorhood.

1.116.s:
asyāṃ samarcya savituḥ pratimāṃ tu haimīṃ haimāśvayuktarathagāṃ tu dadetsahebhām /
yo bhāvabhaktisahitaḥ sa gato hi lokaṃ śambhoḥ sa modata ihāpi ca bhuktabhogaḥ //
1.116.d:
अस्यां समर्च्य सवितुः प्रतिमां तु हैमीं हैमाश्वयुक्तरथगां तु ददेत्सहेभाम् ।
यो भावभक्तिसहितः स गतो हि लोकं शम्भोः स मोदत इहापि च भुक्तभोगः ॥
1.116.m: On this [day], whoever, endowed with devotion of feeling, worships the golden image of the Sun / mounted on a chariot with golden horses, and gives it away along with an elephant, / goes indeed to the world of Śambhu and rejoices here as well, having enjoyed pleasures.

1.116.s:
bhāskarī saptamī ceyaṃ koṭibhāsvadgrahopamā /
aruṇodayavelāyāmasyāṃ snānaṃ vidhīyate //
1.116.d:
भास्करी सप्तमी चेयं कोटिभास्वद्ग्रहोपमा ।
अरुणोदयवेलायामस्यां स्नानं विधीयते ॥
1.116.m: And this Bhāskarī Saptamī is equal to ten million solar eclipses; / a bath is prescribed on this [day] at the time of dawn.

1.116.s:
arkasya ca badaryāśca sapta sapta dalāni vai /
nidhāya śirasi snāyātsaptajanmāghaśāntaye //
1.116.d:
अर्कस्य च बदर्याश्च सप्त सप्त दलानि वै ।
निधाय शिरसि स्नायात्सप्तजन्माघशान्तये ॥
1.116.m: Having placed seven leaves of the arka plant and seven of the badarī on one's head, / one should bathe for the pacification of sins from seven births.

1.116.s:
putrapradaṃ vrataṃ cātra prāhādityaḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ /
yo māghasitaptamyāṃ pūjayenmāṃ vidhānataḥ //
1.116.d:
पुत्रप्रदं व्रतं चात्र प्राहादित्यः स्वयं प्रभुः ।
यो माघसितप्तम्यां पूजयेन्मां विधानतः ॥
1.116.m: And here the lord Sun himself proclaimed the son-granting observance: / 'Whoever worships me properly on the bright seventh of Māgha,

1.116.s:
tasyāhaṃ putratāṃ yāsye svāṃśena bhṛśatoṣitaḥ /
tasmājjitendriyo bhūtvā samupoṣya divāniśam //
1.116.d:
तस्याहं पुत्रतां यास्ये स्वांशेन भृशतोषितः ।
तस्माज्जितेन्द्रियो भूत्वा समुपोष्य दिवानिशम् ॥
1.116.m: to him I shall go into sonhood by a portion of myself, being greatly pleased.' / Therefore, having controlled one's senses, having fasted day and night,

1.116.s:
pūjayedapare cāhni homaṃ kṛtvā dvijāṃ stataḥ /
dadhyodanena payasā pāyasena ca bhojayet //
1.116.d:
पूजयेदपरे चाह्नि होमं कृत्वा द्विजां स्ततः ।
दध्योदनेन पयसा पायसेन च भोजयेत् ॥
1.116.m: one should worship on the next day, and having performed a fire oblation, then / one should feed twice-born [Brahmins] with curd-rice, milk, and sweet milk-rice.

1.116.s:
anena vidhinā yamtu kurute putrasaptamīḥ /
labhate sa tu satputraṃ cirāyuṣamanāmayam //
tapasyaśuklasaptamyāṃ vratamarkapuṭaṃ caret //
1.116.d:
अनेन विधिना यम्तु कुरुते पुत्रसप्तमीः ।
लभते स तु सत्पुत्रं चिरायुषमनामयम् ॥
तपस्यशुक्लसप्तम्यां व्रतमर्कपुटं चरेत् ॥
1.116.m:
Whoever performs the Putrasaptamī according to this rule / obtains an excellent son who is long-lived and free from illness.

On the bright seventh of Tapasya [Phālguna], one should observe the Arkapuṭa rite.

1.116.s: arkapatrairyajedarkamarkapatrāṇi cāśnuyāt //
1.116.d: अर्कपत्रैर्यजेदर्कमर्कपत्राणि चाश्नुयात् ॥
1.116.m: One should worship the sun with arka leaves, and one should eat [from] arka leaves.

1.116.s:
arkanāma japecchaśvaditthaṃ cārkapuṭavratam /
dhanadaṃ putradaṃ caitatsarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
1.116.d:
अर्कनाम जपेच्छश्वदित्थं चार्कपुटव्रतम् ।
धनदं पुत्रदं चैतत्सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
1.116.m: One should constantly recite the name of the Sun: such is the Arkapuṭa observance. / This grants wealth, grants sons, and destroys all sins.

1.116.s:
trivargadāmiti prāhuḥ kecidetadvataṃ dvija /
yajñavrataṃ tathāpyanye vidhivaddhomakarmaṇā //
1.116.d:
त्रिवर्गदामिति प्राहुः केचिदेतद्वतं द्विज ।
यज्ञव्रतं तथाप्यन्ये विधिवद्धोमकर्मणा ॥
1.116.m: Some say this observance, O twice-born, grants the three aims of life [trivarga]; / others [say it is] a sacrificial observance according to rule through the act of fire oblation.

1.116.s:
sarvāsu sarvamāseṣu saptamīṣu dvijottamaḥ /
bhāskarārādhanaṃ proktaṃ sarvakāmikamityalam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde dvādaśamāsasthitasappamīvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.116.d:
सर्वासु सर्वमासेषु सप्तमीषु द्विजोत्तमः ।
भास्कराराधनं प्रोक्तं सर्वकामिकमित्यलम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे द्वादशमासस्थितसप्पमीव्रतनिरूपणं नाम षोडशाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.116.m:
On all the sevenths in all the months, O best of the twice-born, / the worship of the Sun is declared to grant all desires. Enough [said].

Thus ends the one hundred and sixteenth chapter, named 'Description of the Seventh-Day Observances in the Twelve Months', in the fourth quarter of the Great Narrative in the Pūrvabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.117.s:
sanātana uvāca
śuklāṣṭamyāṃ caitramāse bhavānyāḥ procyate janiḥ /
pradakṣiṇaśataṃ kṛtvā kāryo yātrāmahotsavaḥ //
1.117.d:
सनातन उवाच
शुक्लाष्टम्यां चैत्रमासे भवान्याः प्रोच्यते जनिः ।
प्रदक्षिणशतं कृत्वा कार्यो यात्रामहोत्सवः ॥
1.117.m: Sanātana said: / On the bright eighth in the month of Caitra, the birth of Bhavānī is proclaimed; / having performed a hundred circumambulations, a great pilgrimage festival should be celebrated.

1.117.s:
darśanaṃ jagadambāyāḥ sarvānandapradaṃ nṛṇām /
atraivāśo kakalikāprāśanaṃ samudāhṛtam //
1.117.d:
दर्शनं जगदम्बायाः सर्वानन्दप्रदं नृणाम् ।
अत्रैवाशो ककलिकाप्राशनं समुदाहृतम् ॥
1.117.m: Beholding the Mother of the Universe grants all joy to men. / Right here, the consumption of aśoka buds is proclaimed.

1.117.s:
aśokakalikāścāṣṭau ye pibanti punarvasau /
caitre māsi sitāṣṭamyāṃ na te śokamavāpnuyuḥ //
1.117.d:
अशोककलिकाश्चाष्टौ ये पिबन्ति पुनर्वसौ ।
चैत्रे मासि सिताष्टम्यां न ते शोकमवाप्नुयुः ॥
1.117.m: Those who drink eight aśoka buds under [the asterism] Punarvasu / on the bright eighth in the month of Caitra shall not encounter grief.

1.117.s:
mahāṣṭamīti ca proktā devyāḥ pūjāvidhānataḥ /
vaiśākhasya sitāṣṭamyāṃ samupoṣyātra vāriṇā //
1.117.d:
महाष्टमीति च प्रोक्ता देव्याः पूजाविधानतः ।
वैशाखस्य सिताष्टम्यां समुपोष्यात्र वारिणा ॥
1.117.m: It is declared to be the Mahāṣṭamī through the prescribed worship of the goddess. / On the bright eighth of Vaiśākha, having fasted on this [day], with water

1.117.s:
snātvāparājitāṃ devīṃ māṃsībālakavāribhiḥ /
snāpayitvārcya gandhādyairnaivedyaṃ śarkarāmayam //
1.117.d:
स्नात्वापराजितां देवीं मांसीबालकवारिभिः ।
स्नापयित्वार्च्य गन्धाद्यैर्नैवेद्यं शर्करामयम् ॥
1.117.m: having bathed, and having bathed the goddess Aparājitā with water containing spikenard and bālaka, / having worshipped her with perfumes and the like, [and offered] food-offering made of sugar,

1.117.s:
kumārīrbhojayeccāpi navamyāṃ pāraṇāgrataḥ /
jyotirmayavimānena bhrājamāno yathā raviḥ //
1.117.d:
कुमारीर्भोजयेच्चापि नवम्यां पारणाग्रतः ।
ज्योतिर्मयविमानेन भ्राजमानो यथा रविः ॥
1.117.m: one should also feed young maidens on the ninth before the breaking of the fast. / Shining like the sun in a luminous aerial chariot,

1.117.s:
lokeṣu vicaredvipra devyāścaiva prasādataḥ /
kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ jyeṣṭhamāse pūjayitvā trilocanam //
1.117.d:
लोकेषु विचरेद्विप्र देव्याश्चैव प्रसादतः ।
कृष्णाष्टम्यां ज्येष्ठमासे पूजयित्वा त्रिलोचनम् ॥
1.117.m: one would wander through the worlds, O twice-born, by the grace of the goddess. / Having worshipped the Three-Eyed One on the dark eighth in the month of Jyeṣṭha,

1.117.s:
śivaloke vasetkalpaṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ /
jyeṣṭhaśukle tathāṣṭamyāṃ yo devīṃ pūjayennaraḥ //
1.117.d:
शिवलोके वसेत्कल्पं सर्वदेवनमस्कृतः ।
ज्येष्ठशुक्ले तथाष्टम्यां यो देवीं पूजयेन्नरः ॥
1.117.m: one dwells in the world of Śiva for an eon, bowed to by all the gods. / Likewise, whatever man worships the goddess on the bright eighth of Jyeṣṭha,

1.117.s:
sa vimānena carati gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ /
śuklāṣṭamyāṃ tathā'ṣāḍhe snātvā caiva niśāṃbunā //
1.117.d:
स विमानेन चरति गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणैः ।
शुक्लाष्टम्यां तथाऽषाढे स्नात्वा चैव निशांबुना ॥
1.117.m: he travels in an aerial chariot with hosts of gandharvas and apsarases. / Likewise, having bathed on the bright eighth in Āṣāḍha with water [kept overnight],

1.117.s:
tenaiva snāpayeddevīṃ pūjayecca vidhānataḥ /
tataḥ śuddhajalaiḥ snāpya viliṃpetseṃducandanaiḥ //
1.117.d:
तेनैव स्नापयेद्देवीं पूजयेच्च विधानतः ।
ततः शुद्धजलैः स्नाप्य विलिंपेत्सेंदुचन्दनैः ॥
1.117.m: with that very [water] one should bathe the goddess and worship her according to rule. / Then, having bathed her with pure waters, one should smear her with sandalwood combined with camphor.

1.117.s:
naivedyaṃ śarkaropetaṃ datvā'camanamarpayet /
bhojayitvā tato viprāndatvā svarṇaṃ ca dakṣiṇām //
1.117.d:
नैवेद्यं शर्करोपेतं दत्वाऽचमनमर्पयेत् ।
भोजयित्वा ततो विप्रान्दत्वा स्वर्णं च दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.117.m: Having presented a food-offering accompanied by sugar, one should offer water for sipping. / Then, having fed the Brahmins and given gold as a sacrificial gift,

1.117.s:
visṛjya ca tataḥ paścātsvayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ /
etadvrataṃ naraḥ kṛtvā devīlokamavāpnuyāt //
1.117.d:
विसृज्य च ततः पश्चात्स्वयं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ।
एतद्व्रतं नरः कृत्वा देवीलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.117.m: and having bidden them farewell, one should afterwards eat oneself, restrained in speech. / Having performed this observance, a man attains the world of the goddess.

1.117.s:
nabhaḥśukletathāṣṭamyāṃ devīmiṣṭvā vidhānataḥ /
kṣīreṇa snāpayitvā ca miṣṭānnaṃ vinivedayet //
1.117.d:
नभःशुक्लेतथाष्टम्यां देवीमिष्ट्वा विधानतः ।
क्षीरेण स्नापयित्वा च मिष्टान्नं विनिवेदयेत् ॥
1.117.m: Likewise, on the bright eighth of Nabhas [Śrāvaṇa], having worshipped the goddess according to rule, / and having bathed her with milk, one should offer sweet food.

1.117.s:
tato dvijān bhojayitvā pare 'hni svayamapyuta /
bhuktvā samāpayedadvrataṃ saṃtativardhanam //
1.117.d:
ततो द्विजान् भोजयित्वा परे ऽह्नि स्वयमप्युत ।
भुक्त्वा समापयेदद्व्रतं संततिवर्धनम् ॥
1.117.m: Then, having fed the twice-born on the next day, and having eaten oneself too, / one should conclude this observance that increases offspring.

1.117.s:
nabhomāse sitāṣṭamyāṃ daśāphalamiti vratam /
upavāsaṃ tu saṃkalpya snātvā kṛtvā ca naityikam //
1.117.d:
नभोमासे सिताष्टम्यां दशाफलमिति व्रतम् ।
उपवासं तु संकल्प्य स्नात्वा कृत्वा च नैत्यिकम् ॥
1.117.m: On the bright eighth in the month of Nabhas, there is the observance called Daśāphala. / Having undertaken a fast, having bathed and performed daily rites,

1.117.s:
tulasyāḥ kṛṣṇāvarṇāyā dalairdaśabhirarcayet /
kṛṣṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ tathānantaṃ govindaṃ garuḍadhvajam //
1.117.d:
तुलस्याः कृष्णावर्णाया दलैर्दशभिरर्चयेत् ।
कृष्णं विष्णुं तथानन्तं गोविन्दं गरुडध्वजम् ॥
1.117.m: with ten leaves of dark tulasī one should worship / Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, and Ananta, Govinda, Garuḍadhvaja,

1.117.s:
dāmodaraṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ padmanābhaṃ hariṃ prabhum /
etaiśca nāmabhirnityaṃ kṛṣṇadevaṃ samarcayet //
1.117.d:
दामोदरं हृषीकेशं पद्मनाभं हरिं प्रभुम् ।
एतैश्च नामभिर्नित्यं कृष्णदेवं समर्चयेत् ॥
1.117.m: Dāmodara, Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha, and Lord Hari; / with these names one should daily worship Lord Kṛṣṇa.

1.117.s:
namaskāraṃ tataḥ kuryātpradakṣiṇasamanvitam /
evaṃ daśadinaṃ kuryādvratānāmuttamaṃ vratam //
1.117.d:
नमस्कारं ततः कुर्यात्प्रदक्षिणसमन्वितम् ।
एवं दशदिनं कुर्याद्व्रतानामुत्तमं व्रतम् ॥
1.117.m: Then one should perform obeisance accompanied by circumambulation. / In this way one should perform this best of observances for ten days.

1.117.s:
ādau madhye tathā cānte homaṃ kuryādvidhānataḥ /
kṛṣṇamantreṇa juhuyāccaruṇāṣṭottaraṃ śatam //
1.117.d:
आदौ मध्ये तथा चान्ते होमं कुर्याद्विधानतः ।
कृष्णमन्त्रेण जुहुयाच्चरुणाष्टोत्तरं शतम् ॥
1.117.m: At the beginning, in the middle, and at the end, one should perform a fire oblation according to rule; / one should offer an oblation of sacrificial boiled rice a hundred and eight times with the Kṛṣṇa-mantra.

1.117.s:
homānte vidhinā samyagācāryyaṃ pūjayetsudhīḥ /
sauvarṇe tāmrapātre vā mṛnmaye veṇupātrake //
1.117.d:
होमान्ते विधिना सम्यगाचार्य्यं पूजयेत्सुधीः ।
सौवर्णे ताम्रपात्रे वा मृन्मये वेणुपात्रके ॥
1.117.m: At the end of the fire oblation, the wise person should properly worship the preceptor according to rule. / In a vessel of gold, or of copper, or of clay, or of bamboo,

1.117.s:
tulasīdalaṃ suvarṇena kārayitvā sulakṣaṇam /
haimīṃ ca pratimāṃ kṛtvā pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ //
1.117.d:
तुलसीदलं सुवर्णेन कारयित्वा सुलक्षणम् ।
हैमीं च प्रतिमां कृत्वा पूजयित्वा विधानतः ॥
1.117.m: having had a tulasī leaf fashioned out of gold with auspicious marks, / and having made a golden image and worshipped it according to rule,

1.117.s:
nidhāya pratimāṃ pātre hyācāryāya nivedayet /
dātavyā gauḥ savatsā ca vastrālaṅkārabhūṣitā //
1.117.d:
निधाय प्रतिमां पात्रे ह्याचार्याय निवेदयेत् ।
दातव्या गौः सवत्सा च वस्त्रालङ्कारभूषिता ॥
1.117.m: having placed the image in the vessel, he should present it to the preceptor. / A cow with her calf should also be given, adorned with garments and ornaments.

1.117.s:
daśāhaṃ kṛṣṇadevāya pūrikā daśa cārpayet /
tāśca dadyādvidhijñāya svayaṃ vā bhakṣayedvratī //
1.117.d:
दशाहं कृष्णदेवाय पूरिका दश चार्पयेत् ।
ताश्च दद्याद्विधिज्ञाय स्वयं वा भक्षयेद्व्रती ॥
1.117.m: For ten days, one should offer ten pūrikā cakes to Lord Kṛṣṇa; / and the observer of the vow should give them to one who knows the ritual, or eat them himself.

1.117.s:
śayanaṃ ca pradātavyaṃ yathāśakti dvijottama /
daśame 'hni tato mūrtiṃ sadravyāṃ guraver'payet //
1.117.d:
शयनं च प्रदातव्यं यथाशक्ति द्विजोत्तम ।
दशमे ऽह्नि ततो मूर्तिं सद्रव्यां गुरवेर्ऽपयेत् ॥
1.117.m: And a bed should be given according to one's ability, O best of the twice-born. / Then on the tenth day, he should present the image with wealth to the guru.

1.117.s:
vratānte daśaviprebhyaḥ pratyekaṃ daśa pūrikāḥ /
dadyādeva daśābdaṃ tu kṛtvā vratamanuttamam //
1.117.d:
व्रतान्ते दशविप्रेभ्यः प्रत्येकं दश पूरिकाः ।
दद्यादेव दशाब्दं तु कृत्वा व्रतमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.117.m: At the end of the observance, he should give ten pūrikās to each of ten Brahmins; / having performed this peerless observance for ten years,

1.117.s:
upoṣya vidhinā bhūyātsarvakā masamanvitaḥ /
ante kṛṣṇasya sāyujyaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.117.d:
उपोष्य विधिना भूयात्सर्वका मसमन्वितः ।
अन्ते कृष्णस्य सायुज्यं लभते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.117.m: having fasted according to rule, he becomes endowed with all desires; / at the end, he attains union with Kṛṣṇa; there is no doubt in this.

1.117.s:
kṛṣṇajanmāṣṭamī ceyaṃ smṛtā pāpaharā nṛṇām /
kevalenopavāsena tasmiñjanmadine hareḥ //
1.117.d:
कृष्णजन्माष्टमी चेयं स्मृता पापहरा नृणाम् ।
केवलेनोपवासेन तस्मिञ्जन्मदिने हरेः ॥
1.117.m: And this Kṛṣṇajanmāṣṭamī is remembered as destroying the sins of men; / by merely fasting on that birthday of Hari,

1.117.s:
saptajanmakṛtātpāpānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ /
upavāsī tilaiḥ snāto nadyādau vimale jale //
1.117.d:
सप्तजन्मकृतात्पापान्मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ।
उपवासी तिलैः स्नातो नद्यादौ विमले जले ॥
1.117.m: one is freed from sins committed in seven births, there is no doubt here. / Fasting, having bathed with sesame seeds in clear water of a river or similar place,

1.117.s:
sudeśe maṇḍape kḷpte maṇḍalaṃ racayetsudhīḥ /
tanmadhye kalaśaṃ sthāpya tāmrajaṃ vāpi mṛnmayam //
1.117.d:
सुदेशे मण्डपे कॢप्ते मण्डलं रचयेत्सुधीः ।
तन्मध्ये कलशं स्थाप्य ताम्रजं वापि मृन्मयम् ॥
1.117.m: the wise one should draw a sacred diagram in a pavilion constructed in an auspicious spot; / placing a pot made of copper or earthenware in its center,

1.117.s:
tasyopari nyasetpātraṃ tāmraṃ tasyopari sthitām /
haimīṃ vastrayugācchannāṃ kṛṣṇasya pratimāṃ śubham //
1.117.d:
तस्योपरि न्यसेत्पात्रं ताम्रं तस्योपरि स्थिताम् ।
हैमीं वस्त्रयुगाच्छन्नां कृष्णस्य प्रतिमां शुभम् ॥
1.117.m: above it he should place a copper vessel; resting upon that, / an auspicious golden image of Kṛṣṇa covered with a pair of garments.

1.117.s:
pādyādyairupacāraistu pūjayetsnigdhamānasaḥ /
devakīṃ vasudevaṃ ca yaśodāṃ nandameva ca //
1.117.d:
पाद्याद्यैरुपचारैस्तु पूजयेत्स्निग्धमानसः ।
देवकीं वसुदेवं च यशोदां नन्दमेव च ॥
1.117.m: He should worship with offerings such as water for the feet, his mind affectionate, / and [he should worship] Devakī, Vasudeva, Yaśodā, and Nanda,

1.117.s:
vrajaṃ gopāṃstathā gopīrgāśca dikṣu samarcayet /
tata ārārtikaṃ kṛtvā kṣamāpyānamya bhaktitaḥ //
1.117.d:
व्रजं गोपांस्तथा गोपीर्गाश्च दिक्षु समर्चयेत् ।
तत आरार्तिकं कृत्वा क्षमाप्यानम्य भक्तितः ॥
1.117.m: and he should worship Vraja, the cowherds, the cowherd women, and the cattle in the directions; / then, having performed the lustration of lights, asking forgiveness and bowing with devotion,

1.117.s:
tiṣṭhettathaivārddharātre punaḥ saṃsnāpayeddharim /
pañcāmṛtaiḥ śuddhajalairgandhādyaiḥ pūjayetpunaḥ //
1.117.d:
तिष्ठेत्तथैवार्द्धरात्रे पुनः संस्नापयेद्धरिम् ।
पञ्चामृतैः शुद्धजलैर्गन्धाद्यैः पूजयेत्पुनः ॥
1.117.m: he should remain thus; at midnight he should bathe Hari again / with the five nectars and pure waters, and worship him again with perfumes and other offerings.

1.117.s:
dhānyākaṃ ca yavānīṃ ca śuṇṭhīṃ khaṇḍaṃ ca nārada /
sājyaṃ raupye dhṛtaṃ pātre naivedyaṃ vinivedayet //
1.117.d:
धान्याकं च यवानीं च शुण्ठीं खण्डं च नारद ।
साज्यं रौप्ये धृतं पात्रे नैवेद्यं विनिवेदयेत् ॥
1.117.m: Coriander, ajwain, dried ginger, and raw sugar, O Nārada, / placed with ghee in a silver vessel, he should present as food offering.

1.117.s:
punarārārtikaṃ kṛtvā daśadhā rūpadhāriṇam /
vicintayanmṛgāṅkāya dadyādarghyaṃ samudyate //
1.117.d:
पुनरारार्तिकं कृत्वा दशधा रूपधारिणम् ।
विचिन्तयन्मृगाङ्काय दद्यादर्घ्यं समुद्यते ॥
1.117.m: Having performed the lustration of lights again, contemplating him / who assumes ten forms, he should offer water of hospitality to the moon as it rises.

1.117.s:
tataḥ kṣamāpya deveśaṃ rātrikhaṇḍaṃ nayedvratī /
paurāṇikaiḥ stotrapāṭhairgītavādyairanekadhā //
1.117.d:
ततः क्षमाप्य देवेशं रात्रिखण्डं नयेद्व्रती ।
पौराणिकैः स्तोत्रपाठैर्गीतवाद्यैरनेकधा ॥
1.117.m: Then, having asked forgiveness of the lord of gods, the observer of the vow should pass the rest of the night / with recitations of Puranic hymns and with diverse songs and musical instruments.

1.117.s:
tataḥ prabhāte vipragryānbhojayenmadhurānnakaiḥ /
datvā ca dakṣiṇāṃ tebhyo visṛjettuṣṭamānasaḥ //
1.117.d:
ततः प्रभाते विप्रग्र्यान्भोजयेन्मधुरान्नकैः ।
दत्वा च दक्षिणां तेभ्यो विसृजेत्तुष्टमानसः ॥
1.117.m: Then, in the morning, he should feed the foremost of brahmins with sweet foods, / and having given them a priestly gift, he should dismiss them, joyful in mind.

1.117.s:
tatastāṃ pratimāṃ viṣṇoḥ svarṇadhenudharānvitām /
gurave dakṣiṇāṃ datvā visṛjyāśrīta ca svayam //
1.117.d:
ततस्तां प्रतिमां विष्णोः स्वर्णधेनुधरान्विताम् ।
गुरवे दक्षिणां दत्वा विसृज्याश्रीत च स्वयम् ॥
1.117.m: Then, having given that image of Viṣṇu, accompanied by a golden cow and land, / and a priestly gift to the teacher, and having dismissed him, he himself should eat.

1.117.s:
dārāpatyasuhṛdbhṛtyarevaṃ kṛtvā vrata naraḥ /
sākṣādgokamāpnoti vimānavaramāsthitaḥ //
1.117.d:
दारापत्यसुहृद्भृत्यरेवं कृत्वा व्रत नरः ।
साक्षाद्गोकमाप्नोति विमानवरमास्थितः ॥
1.117.m: Having performed this observance along with his wife, children, friends, and servants, a man / attains Goloka directly, seated upon an excellent celestial chariot.

1.117.s:
naitena sadṛśaṃ cānyadvratamasti jagattraye /
kṛtena yena labhyeta koṭyaikādaśakaṃ phalam //
1.117.d:
नैतेन सदृशं चान्यद्व्रतमस्ति जगत्त्रये ।
कृतेन येन लभ्येत कोट्यैकादशकं फलम् ॥
1.117.m: There is no other observance equal to this in the three worlds, / through the performance of which one would obtain the fruit of a crore of Ekādaśīs.

1.117.s:
śuklāṣṭamyāṃ nabhasyasya kuryādrādhāvrataṃ naraḥ /
pūrvavadrādhikāṃ haimīṃ kalaśasthāṃ prapūjayet //
1.117.d:
शुक्लाष्टम्यां नभस्यस्य कुर्याद्राधाव्रतं नरः ।
पूर्ववद्राधिकां हैमीं कलशस्थां प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.117.m: On the bright eighth day of the month of Bhādrapada, a man should observe the Rādhā vow; / as before, he should worship golden Rādhikā placed on a water-pot.

1.117.s:
madhyāhne pūjayitvenāmekabhaktaṃ samāpayet /
śakto bhaktaścopavāsaṃ pare 'hni vidhinā tataḥ //
1.117.d:
मध्याह्ने पूजयित्वेनामेकभक्तं समापयेत् ।
शक्तो भक्तश्चोपवासं परे ऽह्नि विधिना ततः ॥
1.117.m: Having worshipped her at midday, he should complete a single meal, / or, if capable and devoted, a fast, and on the next day according to rule,

1.117.s:
suvāsinīrbhojayitvā gurave pratimārpaṇam /
kṛtvā svayaṃ ca bhuñjītaṃ vratamevaṃ samāpayet //
1.117.d:
सुवासिनीर्भोजयित्वा गुरवे प्रतिमार्पणम् ।
कृत्वा स्वयं च भुञ्जीतं व्रतमेवं समापयेत् ॥
1.117.m: having fed married women whose husbands are living, / having offered the image to the teacher, he himself should eat, and thus complete the observance.

1.117.s:
vratenānena viprarṣe kṛtena vidhinā vratī /
rahasyaṃ goṣṭhajaṃ labdhvā rādhāparikare vaset //
1.117.d:
व्रतेनानेन विप्रर्षे कृतेन विधिना व्रती ।
रहस्यं गोष्ठजं लब्ध्वा राधापरिकरे वसेत् ॥
1.117.m: Through this observance performed according to rule, O brahmin-sage, the observer of the vow, / having attained the secret of the cowherd station, dwells among the retinue of Rādhā.

1.117.s:
dūrvāṣṭamīvrataṃ cātra kathitaṃ tacca me śṛṇu /
śucau deśe prajātāyāṃ dvarvāyāṃ dvijasattama //
1.117.d:
दूर्वाष्टमीव्रतं चात्र कथितं तच्च मे शृणु ।
शुचौ देशे प्रजातायां द्वर्वायां द्विजसत्तम ॥
1.117.m: The Dūrvāṣṭamī observance is also declared here; hear that from me: / on dūrvā grass that has grown in a pure spot, O best of the twice-born,

1.117.s:
sthāpya liṅgaṃ tato gandhaiḥ puṣpairdhūpaiśca dīpakaiḥ /
naivedyairarcayedbhaktyā dadhyakṣataphalādibhiḥ //
1.117.d:
स्थाप्य लिङ्गं ततो गन्धैः पुष्पैर्धूपैश्च दीपकैः ।
नैवेद्यैरर्चयेद्भक्त्या दध्यक्षतफलादिभिः ॥
1.117.m: having installed a liṅga, he should then worship it with devotion using perfumes, flowers, incenses, and lamps, / food offerings, curd, unhusked rice grains, fruits, and other items.

1.117.s:
arghyaṃ pradadyātpūjānte mantrābhyāṃ susamāhitaḥ /
tvaṃ dūrve 'mṛtajanmāsi surāsuranamaskṛte //
1.117.d:
अर्घ्यं प्रदद्यात्पूजान्ते मन्त्राभ्यां सुसमाहितः ।
त्वं दूर्वे ऽमृतजन्मासि सुरासुरनमस्कृते ॥
1.117.m: At the conclusion of the worship, he should offer water of honour with very concentrated mind using two mantras: / 'O Dūrvā, you were born from nectar, honoured by gods and asuras;

1.117.s:
saubhāgyaṃ saṃtatiṃ dehi sarvakāryakarī bhava /
yathā śākhā praśākhābhirvistṛtāsi mahītale //
1.117.d:
सौभाग्यं संततिं देहि सर्वकार्यकरी भव ।
यथा शाखा प्रशाखाभिर्विस्तृतासि महीतले ॥
1.117.m: Grant good fortune and offspring; accomplish all undertakings! / Just as you have spread over the surface of the earth with branches and minor branches,

1.117.s:
tathā vistṛtasaṃtānaṃ dehi me 'pyajarāmaram /
tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya viprānsaṃbhojya tatra vai //
1.117.d:
तथा विस्तृतसंतानं देहि मे ऽप्यजरामरम् ।
ततः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य विप्रान्संभोज्य तत्र वै ॥
1.117.m: So grant me an extensive lineage that is ageless and immortal.' / Then, having circumambulated [it] and fed the brāhmaṇas there,

1.117.s:
bhuktvā svayaṃ gṛhaṃ gacchedatvā vipreṣu dakṣiṇām /
phalāni ca praśastāni miṣṭāni surabhīṇi ca //
1.117.d:
भुक्त्वा स्वयं गृहं गच्छेदत्वा विप्रेषु दक्षिणाम् ।
फलानि च प्रशस्तानि मिष्टानि सुरभीणि च ॥
1.117.m: He should eat himself and go home after giving priestly fees to the brāhmaṇas, / As well as auspicious, sweet, and fragrant fruits.

1.117.s:
evaṃ puṇyā pāpaharā nṛṇā dūrvāṣṭamī dvija /
caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ strījanānāṃ viśeṣataḥ //
1.117.d:
एवं पुण्या पापहरा नृणा दूर्वाष्टमी द्विज ।
चतुर्णामपि वर्णानां स्त्रीजनानां विशेषतः ॥
1.117.m: Thus the Dūrvāṣṭamī brings merit and removes sins for men, O twice-born one, / And for all four castes, especially for women.

1.117.s:
yā na pūjayate dūrvā nārī mohādyathāvidhi /
janmāni trīṇi vaidhavyaṃ labhate sā na saṃśayaḥ //
1.117.d:
या न पूजयते दूर्वा नारी मोहाद्यथाविधि ।
जन्मानि त्रीणि वैधव्यं लभते सा न संशयः ॥
1.117.m: The woman who, through delusion, does not worship Dūrvā according to the rules, / Suffers widowhood for three births; there is no doubt about this.

1.117.s:
yadā jyeṣṭharkṣasaṃyuktā bhavecjaivāṣṭabhī dvija /
jyeṣṭhā nāmnī tu sā jñeyā pūjitā pāpanāśinī //
1.117.d:
यदा ज्येष्ठर्क्षसंयुक्ता भवेच्जैवाष्टभी द्विज ।
ज्येष्ठा नाम्नी तु सा ज्ञेया पूजिता पापनाशिनी ॥
1.117.m: When the eighth lunar day is conjoined with the constellation Jyeṣṭhā, O twice-born one, / It is known by the name Jyeṣṭhā; when worshipped, it destroys sins.

1.117.s:
athaināṃ tu samārabhya vrataṃ ṣoḍaśavāsaram /
mahālakṣmyāḥ samuddiṣṭaṃ sarvasaṃpadvivardhanam //
1.117.d:
अथैनां तु समारभ्य व्रतं षोडशवासरम् ।
महालक्ष्म्याः समुद्दिष्टं सर्वसंपद्विवर्धनम् ॥
1.117.m: Beginning on this day, a sixteen-day vow / Of Mahālakṣmī is prescribed, which increases all prosperity:

1.117.s:
kariṣye 'haṃ mahālakṣmīvrataṃ te tvatparāyaṇaḥ /
tadavighnena me yātu samāptiṃ tvatprasādataḥ //
1.117.d:
करिष्ये ऽहं महालक्ष्मीव्रतं ते त्वत्परायणः ।
तदविघ्नेन मे यातु समाप्तिं त्वत्प्रसादतः ॥
1.117.m: 'Devoted to you, I will perform your Mahālakṣmī-vow; / May it reach completion without obstacles through your grace.'

1.117.s:
ityuccārya tato baddhā ḍoraka dakṣiṇe kare /
ṣoḍaśagranthisahitaṃ guṇaiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiryutam //
1.117.d:
इत्युच्चार्य ततो बद्धा डोरक दक्षिणे करे ।
षोडशग्रन्थिसहितं गुणैः षोडशभिर्युतम् ॥
1.117.m: Having recited this, he should tie on his right hand a cord / Having sixteen knots and made of sixteen threads.

1.117.s:
tato 'nvahaṃ mahālakṣmīṃ gandhādyairarccayedvratī /
yāvatkṛṣṇāṣṭamī tatra caredudyāpanaṃ sudhīḥ //
1.117.d:
ततो ऽन्वहं महालक्ष्मीं गन्धाद्यैरर्च्चयेद्व्रती ।
यावत्कृष्णाष्टमी तत्र चरेदुद्यापनं सुधीः ॥
1.117.m: Then, day after day, the observer of the vow should worship Mahālakṣmī with perfumes and the like / Until the dark eighth lunar day; on that day the wise one should perform the concluding rite.

1.117.s:
vastramaṇḍapikāṃ kṛtvā sarvatobhadramaṇḍale /
kalaśaṃ supratiṣṭhāpya dīpamuddyotayettataḥ //
1.117.d:
वस्त्रमण्डपिकां कृत्वा सर्वतोभद्रमण्डले ।
कलशं सुप्रतिष्ठाप्य दीपमुद्द्योतयेत्ततः ॥
1.117.m: Having made a cloth pavilion on a sarvatobhadra diagram / And properly installed a pot, he should then light a lamp.

1.117.s:
uttārya ḍorakaṃ bāhoḥ kuṃbhasyādho nivedayet /
catasraḥ pratimāḥ kṛtvā sauvarṇīstatsvarūpiṇīḥ //
1.117.d:
उत्तार्य डोरकं बाहोः कुंभस्याधो निवेदयेत् ।
चतस्रः प्रतिमाः कृत्वा सौवर्णीस्तत्स्वरूपिणीः ॥
1.117.m: Taking the cord off his arm, he should place it under the pot. / Having made four golden images representing her form,

1.117.s:
snapanaṃ kārayettāsāḥ jalaiḥ pañcāmṛtaistathā /
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ //
1.117.d:
स्नपनं कारयेत्तासाः जलैः पञ्चामृतैस्तथा ।
उपचारैः षोडशभिः पूजयित्वा विधानतः ॥
1.117.m: He should bathe them with waters and with the five nectars, / And having worshipped [them] according to the rules with the sixteen services,

1.117.s:
jāgarastatra kartavyo gītavāditraniḥ svanaiḥ /
tato niśīthe saṃprāpte 'bhyudite 'mṛtadīdhitau //
1.117.d:
जागरस्तत्र कर्तव्यो गीतवादित्रनिः स्वनैः ।
ततो निशीथे संप्राप्ते ऽभ्युदिते ऽमृतदीधितौ ॥
1.117.m: A night-vigil should be kept there with the sounds of songs and musical instruments. / Then, when midnight has arrived and the moon has risen,

1.117.s:
datvārghyaṃ bandhanaṃ dravyaiḥ śrīkhaṇḍādyairvidhānataḥ /
candramaṇḍalasaṃsthāyai mahālakṣyai pradāpayet //
1.117.d:
दत्वार्घ्यं बन्धनं द्रव्यैः श्रीखण्डाद्यैर्विधानतः ।
चन्द्रमण्डलसंस्थायै महालक्ष्यै प्रदापयेत् ॥
1.117.m: Having properly offered water of honour and a fastening with substances such as sandalwood, / He should have it offered to Mahālakṣmī seated in the lunar disc:

1.117.s:
kṣīrodārṇavasaṃbhūta mahālakṣmīsahodara /
pīyūṣadhāma rohiṇyāḥ sahitār'ghyaṃ gṛhāṇa me //
1.117.d:
क्षीरोदार्णवसंभूत महालक्ष्मीसहोदर ।
पीयूषधाम रोहिण्याः सहितार्ऽघ्यं गृहाण मे ॥
1.117.m: 'O one born from the ocean of milk, uterine brother of Mahālakṣmī, / O abode of nectar, united with Rohiṇī, accept my water of honour!

1.117.s:
kṣīrodārṇavasambhūte kamale kamalālaye /
viṣṇuvakṣasthalasthe me sarvakāmapradā bhava //
1.117.d:
क्षीरोदार्णवसम्भूते कमले कमलालये ।
विष्णुवक्षस्थलस्थे मे सर्वकामप्रदा भव ॥
1.117.m: O one born from the ocean of milk, O Kamala, O Kamalālayā! / O you who dwell on the chest of Viṣṇu, grant all my desires!

1.117.s:
ekanāthe jagannāthe jamadagnipriye 'vyaye /
reṇuke trāhi māṃ devi rāmamātaḥ śivaṃ kuru //
1.117.d:
एकनाथे जगन्नाथे जमदग्निप्रिये ऽव्यये ।
रेणुके त्राहि मां देवि राममातः शिवं कुरु ॥
1.117.m: O sole mistress, O mistress of the universe, O beloved of Jamadagni, O imperishable one! / O goddess Reṇukā, protect me! O mother of Rāma, bring about auspiciousness!'

1.117.s:
mantrairetairmahālakṣmīṃ prārthya śrotriyayoṣitaḥ /
samyaksaṃpūjya tāḥ samyaggandhayāvakakajjalaiḥ //
1.117.d:
मन्त्रैरेतैर्महालक्ष्मीं प्रार्थ्य श्रोत्रिययोषितः ।
सम्यक्संपूज्य ताः सम्यग्गन्धयावककज्जलैः ॥
1.117.m: Having prayed to Mahālakṣmī with these mantras, having properly honoured the wives of Vedic scholars / Correctly with perfume, red lac-dye, and collyrium,

1.117.s:
saṃbhojya juhuyādagnau bilvapadmakapāyasaiḥ /
tadalābhe ghṛtairvipra gṛhebhyaḥ samidhastilān //
1.117.d:
संभोज्य जुहुयादग्नौ बिल्वपद्मकपायसैः ।
तदलाभे घृतैर्विप्र गृहेभ्यः समिधस्तिलान् ॥
1.117.m: And having fed them, he should make fire oblations with wood-apple, lotus, and milk-rice, / Or in their absence, O twice-born one, with clarified butter, fuel sticks, and sesame seeds taken from households.

1.117.s:
mṛtyuñjayāya ca paraṃ sarvarogapraśāntaye /
candanaṃ tālapatraṃ ca puṣpamālāṃ tathākṣatān //
1.117.d:
मृत्युञ्जयाय च परं सर्वरोगप्रशान्तये ।
चन्दनं तालपत्रं च पुष्पमालां तथाक्षतान् ॥
1.117.m: And for Mṛtyuñjaya, for the total pacification of all diseases, [he should offer] / Sandalwood, palm leaf, a garland of flowers, and unbroken grains,

1.117.s:
durvāṃ kausumbhasūtraṃ ca yugaṃ śrīphalameva vā /
bhakṣyāṇi ca nave śūrpe pratidravyaṃ tu ṣoḍaśa //
1.117.d:
दुर्वां कौसुम्भसूत्रं च युगं श्रीफलमेव वा ।
भक्ष्याणि च नवे शूर्पे प्रतिद्रव्यं तु षोडश ॥
1.117.m: Dūrvā grass, a safflower-coloured thread, a pair [of garments], or wood-apples, / And sixteen edibles of each substance in a new winnowing basket.

1.117.s:
samācchādyānyaśūrpeṇa vratī dadyātsamantrakam /
kṣīrodārṇavasaṃbhūtā lakṣmīścandrasahodarā //
1.117.d:
समाच्छाद्यान्यशूर्पेण व्रती दद्यात्समन्त्रकम् ।
क्षीरोदार्णवसंभूता लक्ष्मीश्चन्द्रसहोदरा ॥
1.117.m: Covering it with another winnowing basket, the observer of the vow should give it accompanied by the mantra: / 'May Lakṣmī, born from the ocean of milk, sister of the moon,

1.117.s:
vratenānena saṃtuṣṭā bhavatādviṣṇuvallabhā /
cetasraḥ pratimāstāstu śrotriyebhyaḥ samarpayet //
1.117.d:
व्रतेनानेन संतुष्टा भवताद्विष्णुवल्लभा ।
चेतस्रः प्रतिमास्तास्तु श्रोत्रियेभ्यः समर्पयेत् ॥
1.117.m: And beloved of Viṣṇu, be pleased by this vow!' / He should present those four images to Vedic scholars.

1.117.s:
tatastu caturo viprān ṣoḍaśāpi suvāsinīḥ /
miṣṭānnenāśayitvā tu visṛjettāḥ sadakṣiṇāḥ //
1.117.d:
ततस्तु चतुरो विप्रान् षोडशापि सुवासिनीः ।
मिष्टान्नेनाशयित्वा तु विसृजेत्ताः सदक्षिणाः ॥
1.117.m: Then, having fed four brāhmaṇas and also sixteen married women whose husbands are living / With sweet food, he should dismiss them with priestly fees.

1.117.s:
samāptiniyamaḥ paścādbhañjīteṣṭaiḥ samanvitaḥ /
etadvrataṃ mahālakṣmyāḥ kṛtvā vipra vidhānataḥ //
1.117.d:
समाप्तिनियमः पश्चाद्भञ्जीतेष्टैः समन्वितः ।
एतद्व्रतं महालक्ष्म्याः कृत्वा विप्र विधानतः ॥
1.117.m: Having concluded the observances, he should later eat together with his cherished ones. / Having performed this vow of Mahālakṣmī according to rule, O twice-born one,

1.117.s:
bhuktveṣṭānaihikān kāmāṃllakṣmīloke vasecciram /
eṣāṣokāṣṭamī coktā yasyāṃ pūrṇaṃ ramāvratam //
1.117.d:
भुक्त्वेष्टानैहिकान् कामांल्लक्ष्मीलोके वसेच्चिरम् ।
एषाषोकाष्टमी चोक्ता यस्यां पूर्णं रमाव्रतम् ॥
1.117.m: He enjoys his desired worldly wishes and dwells for a long time in the world of Lakṣmī. / This is also called Aśokāṣṭamī, on which Ramā's vow is completed.

1.117.s:
atrāśokasya pūjā syādekabhaktaṃ tathā smṛtam /
kṛtvāśokavrataṃ nārī hyaśokā śokajanmani //
1.117.d:
अत्राशोकस्य पूजा स्यादेकभक्तं तथा स्मृतम् ।
कृत्वाशोकव्रतं नारी ह्यशोका शोकजन्मनि ॥
1.117.m: Worship of the Aśoka tree should take place here, and taking only a single meal is prescribed. / Having performed the Aśoka vow, a woman becomes free from grief in an existence of grief,

1.117.s:
yatra kutrāpi saṃjātā nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
āśvine śuklapakṣe tu proktā vipra mahāṣṭamī //
1.117.d:
यत्र कुत्रापि संजाता नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
आश्विने शुक्लपक्षे तु प्रोक्ता विप्र महाष्टमी ॥
1.117.m: Wherever she may be born; there should be no doubt about this. / The bright eighth lunar day of Āśvina is declared to be Mahāṣṭamī, O twice-born one.

1.117.s:
tatra durgācanaṃ proktaṃ savrairapyupacārakaiḥ /
upavāsaṃ caikabhaktaṃ mahāṣṭamyāṃ vidhāya tu //
1.117.d:
तत्र दुर्गाचनं प्रोक्तं सव्रैरप्युपचारकैः ।
उपवासं चैकभक्तं महाष्टम्यां विधाय तु ॥
1.117.m: Worship of Durgā with all services is prescribed on that day. / Having observed a fast and a single meal on Mahāṣṭamī,

1.117.s:
sarvato vibhavaṃ prāpya modate devavacciram /
ūrjje kṛṣṇādike 'ṣṭamyāṃ karakākhyaṃ vrataṃ smṛtam //
1.117.d:
सर्वतो विभवं प्राप्य मोदते देववच्चिरम् ।
ऊर्ज्जे कृष्णादिके ऽष्टम्यां करकाख्यं व्रतं स्मृतम् ॥
1.117.m: He attains glory in every respect and rejoices for a long time like a god. / In the month of Kārttika, on the dark eighth lunar day, the vow named Karaka is prescribed.

1.117.s:
tatromāsahitaḥ śaṃbhuḥ pūjanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ /
candrodayer'ghadānaṃ ca vidheyaṃ vratibhiḥ sadā //
1.117.d:
तत्रोमासहितः शंभुः पूजनीयः प्रयत्नतः ।
चन्द्रोदयेर्ऽघदानं च विधेयं व्रतिभिः सदा ॥
1.117.m: There Śambhu accompanied by Umā should be worshipped with effort, / And offering water of honour at moonrise must always be performed by those observing the vow

1.117.s:
putraṃ sarvaguṇopetamicchadbhirvividhaṃ sukham /
gopāṣṭamīti saṃproktā kārtike dhavale dale //
1.117.d:
पुत्रं सर्वगुणोपेतमिच्छद्भिर्विविधं सुखम् ।
गोपाष्टमीति संप्रोक्ता कार्तिके धवले दले ॥
1.117.m: Who desire a son endowed with all good qualities and diverse happiness. / It is called Gopāṣṭamī in the bright half of Kārttika.

1.117.s:
tatrakuryādgavāṃ pūjāṃ gogrāsaṃ gopradakṣiṇām /
gavānugamanaṃ dānaṃ vāñchansarvāśca saṃpadaḥ //
1.117.d:
तत्रकुर्याद्गवां पूजां गोग्रासं गोप्रदक्षिणाम् ।
गवानुगमनं दानं वाञ्छन्सर्वाश्च संपदः ॥
1.117.m: There one desiring all prosperity should perform the worship of cows, the feeding of a mouthful of grass to a cow, circumambulation of cows, / Following cows, and the gift [of cows].

1.117.s:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ mārgaśīrṣe mithunaṃ darbhanirmitam /
anaghāṃ cānaghāṃ tatra bahuputrasamanvitam //
1.117.d:
कृष्णाष्टम्यां मार्गशीर्षे मिथुनं दर्भनिर्मितम् ।
अनघां चानघां तत्र बहुपुत्रसमन्वितम् ॥
1.117.m: On the dark eighth lunar day in Mārgaśīrṣa, having set up a couple made of darbha grass, / Anagha and Anaghā accompanied by many sons,

1.117.s:
sthāpayitvā śubhe deśe gomayenopalepite /
pūjayedgandhapuṣpādyairupacāraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ //
1.117.d:
स्थापयित्वा शुभे देशे गोमयेनोपलेपिते ।
पूजयेद्गन्धपुष्पाद्यैरुपचारैः पृथग्विधैः ॥
1.117.m: In an auspicious place smeared with cow dung, / He should worship them with perfumes, flowers, and the like, with various kinds of services.

1.117.s:
saṃbhojya dvijadāṃpatyaṃ visṛjellabdhadakṣiṇam /
vratametannaraḥ kṛtvā nārī vā vidhipūrvakam //
1.117.d:
संभोज्य द्विजदांपत्यं विसृजेल्लब्धदक्षिणम् ।
व्रतमेतन्नरः कृत्वा नारी वा विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
1.117.m: Having fed a brāhmaṇa couple, he should dismiss them after they have received priestly fees. / Having performed this vow according to the rules, a man or a woman

1.117.s: putraṃ sallakṣaṇopetaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.117.d: पुत्रं सल्लक्षणोपेतं लभते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.117.m: Obtains a son endowed with auspicious marks; there is no doubt about this.

1.117.s:
mārgāśīrṣasitāṣṭamyāṃ kālabhairavasannidau /
upoṣya jāgaraṃ kṛtvā mahāpāpaiḥ pramucyate //
1.117.d:
मार्गाशीर्षसिताष्टम्यां कालभैरवसन्निदौ ।
उपोष्य जागरं कृत्वा महापापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
1.117.m: Having fasted and kept a night-vigil in the presence of Kālabhairava on the bright eighth lunar day of Mārgaśīrṣa, / One is freed from great sins.

1.117.s:
yatkiñcidaśubhaṃ karma kṛtaṃ mānuṣajanmani /
tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ yāti kālabhairavadarśanāt //
1.117.d:
यत्किञ्चिदशुभं कर्म कृतं मानुषजन्मनि ।
तत्सर्वं विलयं याति कालभैरवदर्शनात् ॥
1.117.m: Whatever inauspicious deed was done in human birth / All dissolves away from the sight of Kālabhairava.

1.117.s:
atha pauṣasitāṣṭamyāṃ śrāddhamaṣṭakasaṃjñitam /
pitṝṇāṃ tṛptidaṃ varṣaṃ kulasantativarddhanam //
1.117.d:
अथ पौषसिताष्टम्यां श्राद्धमष्टकसंज्ञितम् ।
पितॄणां तृप्तिदं वर्षं कुलसन्ततिवर्द्धनम् ॥
1.117.m: Now, on the bright eighth lunar day of Pauṣa, the ancestral rite named Aṣṭakā [is performed], / Which brings satisfaction to the ancestors for a year and increases family lineage.

1.117.s:
śuklāṣṭamyāṃ tu pauṣasya śivaṃ sampūjya bhaktitaḥ /
bhuktimuktimavāpnoti bhaktimekāṃ samācaran //
1.117.d:
शुक्लाष्टम्यां तु पौषस्य शिवं सम्पूज्य भक्तितः ।
भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नोति भक्तिमेकां समाचरन् ॥
1.117.m: Having worshipped Śiva with devotion on the bright eighth lunar day of Pauṣa, / Practising single-minded devotion, he attains enjoyment and liberation.

1.117.s:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ tu māghasya bhadrakālīṃ samarcayet /
bhaktito vairivṛndaghnīṃ sarvakāmapradāyinīm //
1.117.d:
कृष्णाष्टम्यां तु माघस्य भद्रकालीं समर्चयेत् ।
भक्तितो वैरिवृन्दघ्नीं सर्वकामप्रदायिनीम् ॥
1.117.m: On the dark eighth lunar day of Māgha, he should worship Bhadrakālī with devotion, / The slayer of host of enemies, who bestows all desires.

1.117.s:
māghamāse sitāṣṭamyāṃ bhīṣmaṃ saṃtarpayaddvija /
saṃtatiṃ tvavyavacchinnāmicchaṃścāpyaparājayam //
1.117.d:
माघमासे सिताष्टम्यां भीष्मं संतर्पयद्द्विज ।
संततिं त्वव्यवच्छिन्नामिच्छंश्चाप्यपराजयम् ॥
1.117.m: On the bright eighth lunar day in the month of Māgha, O twice-born one, one desiring unbroken lineage / And invincibility should make a water offering to Bhīṣma.

1.117.s:
phaālgune tvasitāṣṭamyāṃ bhīprāṃ devīṃ samarcayet /
tatra vrataparo vipra sarvakāmasamṛddhaye //
1.117.d:
फआल्गुने त्वसिताष्टम्यां भीप्रां देवीं समर्चयेत् ।
तत्र व्रतपरो विप्र सर्वकामसमृद्धये ॥
1.117.m: On the dark eighth lunar day in Phālguna, intent on the vow on that day, O twice-born one, / He should worship the goddess Bhīmā for the fulfilment of all desires.

1.117.s:
śuklāṣṭamyāṃ phaālgunasya śivaṃ cāpi śivāṃ dvija /
gandhādyaiḥ samyagabhyarcya sarvasiddhīśvaro bhavet //
1.117.d:
शुक्लाष्टम्यां फआल्गुनस्य शिवं चापि शिवां द्विज ।
गन्धाद्यैः सम्यगभ्यर्च्य सर्वसिद्धीश्वरो भवेत् ॥
1.117.m: On the bright eighth lunar day of Phālguna, having properly worshipped Śiva and Śivā / With perfumes and other articles, O twice-born one, he becomes the master of all perfections.

1.117.s:
phaālgunāparapakṣe tu śītalāmaṣṭamīdine /
pūjayetsarvavapakkānaiḥ saptamyāṃ vidhivatkṛtaiḥ //
1.117.d:
फआल्गुनापरपक्षे तु शीतलामष्टमीदिने ।
पूजयेत्सर्ववपक्कानैः सप्तम्यां विधिवत्कृतैः ॥
1.117.m: In the dark fortnight of Phālguna, on the day of the eighth lunar day, / He should worship Śītalā with all cooked foods prepared properly on the seventh lunar day.

1.117.s:
śītale tvaṃ jaganmātā śītale tvaṃ jagatpitā /
śītale tvaṃ jagadvātrī śītalāyai namonamaḥ //
1.117.d:
शीतले त्वं जगन्माता शीतले त्वं जगत्पिता ।
शीतले त्वं जगद्वात्री शीतलायै नमोनमः ॥
1.117.m: "O Śītalā, you are the mother of the universe; O Śītalā, you are the father of the universe. / O Śītalā, you are the sustainer of the universe; salutations, salutations to Śītalā!"

1.117.s:
vande 'haṃ śītalāṃ devīṃ rāsabhasthāṃ digaṃbarām /
mārjanī kalaśopetāṃ visphoṭakavināśinīm //
1.117.d:
वन्दे ऽहं शीतलां देवीं रासभस्थां दिगंबराम् ।
मार्जनी कलशोपेतां विस्फोटकविनाशिनीम् ॥
1.117.m: "I praise the goddess Śītalā, mounted upon a donkey, sky-clad, / equipped with a broom and a water-pot, the destroyer of smallpox."

1.117.s:
