śītale śītale cetthaṃ ye japanti jale lthitāḥ //ṭha
teṣāṃ tu śītalā devī syādvisphoṭakaśāntidā //
1.117.d:
शीतले शीतले चेत्थं ये जपन्ति जले ल्थिताः ॥ठ
तेषां तु शीतला देवी स्याद्विस्फोटकशान्तिदा ॥
1.117.m: Those who, standing in water, thus recite: "O Śītalā, O Śītalā," / to them the goddess Śītalā will grant relief from smallpox.

1.117.s:
ityevaṃ śītalāmantrairyaḥ samarcayate dvija /
tasya varṣaṃ bhavecchāntiḥ śītalāyāḥ prasādataḥ //
1.117.d:
इत्येवं शीतलामन्त्रैर्यः समर्चयते द्विज ।
तस्य वर्षं भवेच्छान्तिः शीतलायाः प्रसादतः ॥
1.117.m: Whoever thus properly worships with Śītalā's mantras, O twice-born one, / to him peace will come for a year by the grace of Śītalā.

1.117.s:
sarvamāsobhaye pakṣe vidhivaccāṣṭamīdine /
śivāṃ vāpiśivaṃ prārcyalabhate vāñchitaṃ phalam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde dvādaśamāsasthitāṣṭamīvratakathanaṃ nāma saptadaśādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.117.d:
सर्वमासोभये पक्षे विधिवच्चाष्टमीदिने ।
शिवां वापिशिवं प्रार्च्यलभते वाञ्छितं फलम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे द्वादशमासस्थिताष्टमीव्रतकथनं नाम सप्तदशाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.117.m:
In every month, in both fortnights, on the eighth day according to rule, / having properly worshipped Śivā or Śiva, one attains the desired fruit.

Thus ends the one hundred and seventeenth chapter, entitled "The Description of the Vrata of the Eighth Day Standing in the Twelve Months," in the Fourth Quarter of the Great Narrative in the First Part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.118.s:
sanātana uvāca
atha vakṣyāmi viprendra navamyāste vratāni vai /
yāni kṛtvā narā loke labhante vāñchitaṃ phalam //
1.118.d:
सनातन उवाच
अथ वक्ष्यामि विप्रेन्द्र नवम्यास्ते व्रतानि वै ।
यानि कृत्वा नरा लोके लभन्ते वाञ्छितं फलम् ॥
1.118.m: Sanātana said: / Now I shall declare to you, O best of sages, the observances of the ninth [tithi], / by performing which men in this world obtain their desired fruit.

1.118.s:
caitrasya śuklapakṣe tu śrīrāmanavamīvratam /
tatropavāsaṃ vidhivacchakto bhaktaḥ samācaret //
1.118.d:
चैत्रस्य शुक्लपक्षे तु श्रीरामनवमीव्रतम् ।
तत्रोपवासं विधिवच्छक्तो भक्तः समाचरेत् ॥
1.118.m: In the bright fortnight of Caitra occurs the Śrīrāmanavamī observance; / there, a capable devotee should properly observe a fast.

1.118.s:
aśaktaścaikabhaktaṃ vai madhyāhnotsavataḥ param /
viprānsaṃbhojya miṣṭānnai rāmaprīti sumācaret //
1.118.d:
अशक्तश्चैकभक्तं वै मध्याह्नोत्सवतः परम् ।
विप्रान्संभोज्य मिष्टान्नै रामप्रीति सुमाचरेत् ॥
1.118.m: One who is incapable should eat only one single meal after the midday festival; / having fed brāhmaṇas with sweet foods, he should generate Rāma's delight.

1.118.s:
gobhūtilahariraṇyādyervastrālaṅkaraṇestathā /
eva yaḥ kurute bhaktyā śrīrāmanavamīvratam //
1.118.d:
गोभूतिलहरिरण्याद्येर्वस्त्रालङ्करणेस्तथा ।
एव यः कुरुते भक्त्या श्रीरामनवमीव्रतम् ॥
1.118.m: With cows, land, sesame, gold, and the like, as well as with garments and ornaments, / he who thus performs the Śrīrāmanavamī observance with devotion,

1.118.s:
vidhūya cehapāpāni vraje dviṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam /
uktaṃ mātṛvrataṃ cātra bhairaveṇa samanvitāḥ //
1.118.d:
विधूय चेहपापानि व्रजे द्विष्णोः परं पदम् ।
उक्तं मातृव्रतं चात्र भैरवेण समन्विताः ॥
1.118.m: having shaken off sins here, goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. / And here the Mātṛvrata accompanied by Bhairava is spoken of.

1.118.s:
sraggandhavasranamanaivedyaiścatuḥṣṭistu yoginīḥ /
atraiva bhadrakālo tu yoginīnāṃ mahābalā //
1.118.d:
स्रग्गन्धवस्रनमनैवेद्यैश्चतुःष्टिस्तु योगिनीः ।
अत्रैव भद्रकालो तु योगिनीनां महाबला ॥
1.118.m: With garlands, scents, garments, obeisances, and food offerings [one worships] the sixty-four Yoginīs; / right here, Bhadrakālī, of great strength among the Yoginīs,

1.118.s:
brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhaḥ sarvāsāmādhipatye 'bhiṣecitā /
tasmāttāṃ pūjayeccātra sopavāso jitendriyaḥ //
1.118.d:
ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठः सर्वासामाधिपत्ये ऽभिषेचिता ।
तस्मात्तां पूजयेच्चात्र सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.118.m: is consecrated into sovereignty over all of them, O best of brāhmaṇas; / therefore, one should worship her here, fasting and with senses controlled.

1.118.s:
rādhe navamyāṃ dalayoścaṇḍikāṃ yastu pūjayet /
vidhinā sa vimānena devataiḥ saha modate //
1.118.d:
राधे नवम्यां दलयोश्चण्डिकां यस्तु पूजयेत् ।
विधिना स विमानेन देवतैः सह मोदते ॥
1.118.m: In Vaiśākha, on the ninth of both fortnights, whoever worships Caṇḍikā / according to rule, rejoices together with the deities in a celestial chariot.

1.118.s:
jyeṣṭhaśuklanavamyāṃ tu sopavāso narottamaḥ /
umāṃ saṃpūjya vidhivatkumārīrbhojayeddvijān //
1.118.d:
ज्येष्ठशुक्लनवम्यां तु सोपवासो नरोत्तमः ।
उमां संपूज्य विधिवत्कुमारीर्भोजयेद्द्विजान् ॥
1.118.m: On the ninth day of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha, an excellent man, fasting, / having worshipped Umā according to rule, should feed maidens and brāhmaṇas.

1.118.s:
svabhaktyā dakṣiṇāṃ datvā śālyannaṃ payasāśnuyāt /
umāvratamidaṃ vipra yaḥ kuryādvidhivannaraḥ //
1.118.d:
स्वभक्त्या दक्षिणां दत्वा शाल्यन्नं पयसाश्नुयात् ।
उमाव्रतमिदं विप्र यः कुर्याद्विधिवन्नरः ॥
1.118.m: Having given a priestly fee according to his devotion, he should eat rice with milk. / The man who performs this observance of Umā according to rule, O brāhmaṇa,

1.118.s:
sa bhuktveha varānbhogānante svargagatiṃ labhet /
āṣāḍhe māsi viprendra yaḥ kuryātpakṣayordvija //
1.118.d:
स भुक्त्वेह वरान्भोगानन्ते स्वर्गगतिं लभेत् ।
आषाढे मासि विप्रेन्द्र यः कुर्यात्पक्षयोर्द्विज ॥
1.118.m: having enjoyed excellent pleasures here, attains heavenly status at the end. / In the month of Āṣāḍha, O best of brāhmaṇas, whoever in both fortnights, O twice-born one,

1.118.s:
naktaṃ caindrīṃ samabhyarcyedairāvatagatāṃ sitām /
sa bhavedvai valoke tu bhogabhāragdevayānagaḥ //
1.118.d:
नक्तं चैन्द्रीं समभ्यर्च्येदैरावतगतां सिताम् ।
स भवेद्वै वलोके तु भोगभारग्देवयानगः ॥
1.118.m: observing a night-fast, worships white Aindrī riding upon Airāvata, / will indeed partake of enjoyments in her world, travelling in a divine vehicle.

1.118.s:
śrāvaṇe māsi viprendra yaḥ kuryānnaktabhojanam /
pakṣayorupavāsaṃ vā kaumārīṃ caṇḍikāṃ yajet //
1.118.d:
श्रावणे मासि विप्रेन्द्र यः कुर्यान्नक्तभोजनम् ।
पक्षयोरुपवासं वा कौमारीं चण्डिकां यजेत् ॥
1.118.m: In the month of Śrāvaṇa, O best of brāhmaṇas, whoever eats only at night / or fasts in both fortnights, should worship Caṇḍikā as Kaumārī.

1.118.s:
evaṃ pāpaharāṃ gandhaiḥ puṣpairdhūpaiśca dīpakaiḥ /
naivedyairvividhaiścaiva kumārībhojanaistathā //
1.118.d:
एवं पापहरां गन्धैः पुष्पैर्धूपैश्च दीपकैः ।
नैवेद्यैर्विविधैश्चैव कुमारीभोजनैस्तथा ॥
1.118.m: Thus, [he worships] the destroyer of sins with scents, flowers, incense, lamps, / various offerings of food, and likewise by feeding maidens.

1.118.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute bhaktyā kaumārīvratamuttamam /
sa vimānena gacchedvai devīlokaṃ sanātanam //
1.118.d:
एवं यः कुरुते भक्त्या कौमारीव्रतमुत्तमम् ।
स विमानेन गच्छेद्वै देवीलोकं सनातनम् ॥
1.118.m: He who thus performs with devotion the excellent Kaumārī observance / goes indeed by celestial chariot to the eternal world of the Goddess.

1.118.s:
bhādre tu navamī śuklā nandāhvā parikīrtitā /
tasyāṃ yaḥ pūjayeddurgāṃ vidhivaccopacārakaiḥ //
1.118.d:
भाद्रे तु नवमी शुक्ला नन्दाह्वा परिकीर्तिता ।
तस्यां यः पूजयेद्दुर्गां विधिवच्चोपचारकैः ॥
1.118.m: In Bhādrapada, the bright ninth is known by the name Nandā; / on it, whoever worships Durgā according to rule with ritual offerings,

1.118.s:
so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labdhvā viṣṇuloke mahīyate /
āśvine śuklanavamī mahāpūrvā prakīrtitā //
1.118.d:
सो ऽश्वमेधफलं लब्ध्वा विष्णुलोके महीयते ।
आश्विने शुक्लनवमी महापूर्वा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
1.118.m: obtaining the fruit of a horse sacrifice, is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. / In Āśvina, the bright ninth is proclaimed as the Mahānavamī.

1.118.s:
aparāhne śamīpūjā kāryāsyāṃ prāgdiśi dvija /
tato niśāyāṃ prāgyāme khaḍgaṃ dhanuriṣūngadām //
1.118.d:
अपराह्ने शमीपूजा कार्यास्यां प्राग्दिशि द्विज ।
ततो निशायां प्राग्यामे खड्गं धनुरिषून्गदाम् ॥
1.118.m: In the afternoon of this day, the worship of the śamī tree is to be performed in the eastern direction, O twice-born one; / then at night, in the first watch, [worshipping] the sword, bow, arrows, mace,

1.118.s:
śūlaṃ śaktiṃ ca paraśuṃ chirikāṃ carma kheṭakam /
chatraṃ dhvajaṃ gajaṃ cāśva govṛṣaṃ pustakaṃ tulām //
1.118.d:
शूलं शक्तिं च परशुं छिरिकां चर्म खेटकम् ।
छत्रं ध्वजं गजं चाश्व गोवृषं पुस्तकं तुलाम् ॥
1.118.m: spear, lance, axe, dagger, hide, shield, / parasol, banner, elephant, horse, cow, bull, book, scales,

1.118.s:
daṇḍaṃ pāśaṃ cakraśaṅkhau gandhādyairupacārakaiḥ /
saṃpūjya mahiṣaṃ tatra bhadrakālyai samālabhet //
1.118.d:
दण्डं पाशं चक्रशङ्खौ गन्धाद्यैरुपचारकैः ।
संपूज्य महिषं तत्र भद्रकाल्यै समालभेत् ॥
1.118.m: staff, noose, discus, and conch with ritual offerings such as perfumes, / having worshipped them, one should then sacrifice a buffalo to Bhadrakālī:

1.118.s:
evaṃ baliṃ vidhāyātha bhuktvā pakkānna meva ca /
dvijebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ datvā vrataṃ tatra samāpayet //
1.118.d:
एवं बलिं विधायाथ भुक्त्वा पक्कान्न मेव च ।
द्विजेभ्यो दक्षिणां दत्वा व्रतं तत्र समापयेत् ॥
1.118.m:
Having thus offered the oblation, eaten cooked food,
and given sacrificial gifts to the twice-born, one should conclude the observance there.

1.118.s:
evaṃ yaḥ pūjayeddurgāṃ nṝṇāṃ durgatināśinīm /
iha bhuktvā varānbhogānante svargatimāpnuyāt //
1.118.d:
एवं यः पूजयेद्दुर्गां नॄणां दुर्गतिनाशिनीम् ।
इह भुक्त्वा वरान्भोगानन्ते स्वर्गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.118.m:
He who thus worships Durgā, who destroys the misfortunes of mortals,
enjoys excellent pleasures in this world and attains heaven in the end.

1.118.s:
kārtike śuklanavamī yākṣayā sā prakīrtatā /
tasyāmaśvatthamūle vai tarppaṇaṃ samyagācaret //
1.118.d:
कार्तिके शुक्लनवमी याक्षया सा प्रकीर्तता ।
तस्यामश्वत्थमूले वै तर्प्पणं सम्यगाचरेत् ॥
1.118.m:
The bright ninth in Kārttika is renowned as Akṣayā;
on it, one should properly perform the water offering at the base of a sacred fig tree.

1.118.s:
devānāṃ ca ṛṣīṇāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ cāpi nārada /
svaśākhoktaistathā mantraiḥ sūryāyārghyaṃ tator'payet //
1.118.d:
देवानां च ऋषीणां च पितॄणां चापि नारद ।
स्वशाखोक्तैस्तथा मन्त्रैः सूर्यायार्घ्यं ततोर्ऽपयेत् ॥
1.118.m:
To the gods, the sages, and the ancestors, O Nārada,
and then one should offer an arghya to the sun with the mantras declared in one's own Vedic branch.

1.118.s:
tato dvijānbhojayitvā miṣṭānnena munūśvara /
svayaṃ bhuktvā ca vihareddvijebhyo dattadakṣiṇaḥ //
1.118.d:
ततो द्विजान्भोजयित्वा मिष्टान्नेन मुनूश्वर ।
स्वयं भुक्त्वा च विहरेद्द्विजेभ्यो दत्तदक्षिणः ॥
1.118.m:
Then, having fed the twice-born with sweet food, O best of sages,
and given sacrificial gifts to the twice-born, one should eat oneself and take one's recreation.

1.118.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute bhaktyā japadānaṃ dvijārcanam /
homaṃ ca sarvamakṣayyaṃ bhavediti vidhervayaḥ //
1.118.d:
एवं यः कुरुते भक्त्या जपदानं द्विजार्चनम् ।
होमं च सर्वमक्षय्यं भवेदिति विधेर्वयः ॥
1.118.m:
He who thus performs recitation, gift-giving, worship of the twice-born,
and fire oblation with devotion—all this becomes imperishable; such is the word of the creator.

1.118.s:
mārge tu śuklanavamī nandinī parikīrtitā /
tasyāmupoṣito yastu jagadaṃbāṃ prapūjayet //
1.118.d:
मार्गे तु शुक्लनवमी नन्दिनी परिकीर्तिता ।
तस्यामुपोषितो यस्तु जगदंबां प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.118.m:
In Mārgaśīrṣa, the bright ninth is celebrated as Nandinī;
he who, having fasted on it, worships the Mother of the Universe

1.118.s:
gandhādyaiḥ so 'śvamedhasya phalabhāṅnātra saṃśayaḥ /
pauṣe śuklanavamyāṃ tu mahāmāyāṃ prapūjayet //
1.118.d:
गन्धाद्यैः सो ऽश्वमेधस्य फलभाङ्नात्र संशयः ।
पौषे शुक्लनवम्यां तु महामायां प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.118.m:
with fragrances and the rest, shares the fruit of a horse sacrifice—there is no doubt about this.
On the bright ninth in Pauṣa, one should worship Mahāmāyā

1.118.s:
ekabhaktaparo vipra vājapeyaphalāptaye /
māghamāse tu vā śuklā navamī lokapūjitā //
1.118.d:
एकभक्तपरो विप्र वाजपेयफलाप्तये ।
माघमासे तु वा शुक्ला नवमी लोकपूजिता ॥
1.118.m:
devoted to a single meal, O twice-born, to obtain the fruit of a Vājapeya sacrifice.
In the month of Māgha, the bright ninth, revered by the worlds,

1.118.s:
mahānandeti sā proktā sadānandakarī nṛṇām /
tasyāṃ snānaṃ tathā dānaṃ japo homa upoṣaṇam //
1.118.d:
महानन्देति सा प्रोक्ता सदानन्दकरी नृणाम् ।
तस्यां स्नानं तथा दानं जपो होम उपोषणम् ॥
1.118.m:
is called Mahānandā; it constantly brings joy to mortals.
On it, bathing, gift-giving, recitation, fire oblation, and fasting—

1.118.s:
sarvamakṣayatāṃ yāti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
phaālgunāmalapakṣasya navamī yā dvijottama //
1.118.d:
सर्वमक्षयतां याति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
फआल्गुनामलपक्षस्य नवमी या द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.118.m:
all attains imperishability; no doubt should be entertained here.
The ninth of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, O best of the twice-born,

1.118.s:
ānandā sā mahāpuṇyā sarvapāpaharā smṛtā /
sopavāsor'cayettatra yastvānandāṃ dvijottama //
1.118.d:
आनन्दा सा महापुण्या सर्वपापहरा स्मृता ।
सोपवासोर्ऽचयेत्तत्र यस्त्वानन्दां द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.118.m:
is remembered as Ānandā, highly meritorious, removing all sins.
He who, fasting, worships Ānandā on that day, O best of the twice-born,

1.118.s:
sa labhedvāñchitānkāmānsatyaṃ satyaṃ mayoditam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde dvādaśamāsasthitanavamīvratakathanaṃ nāmāṣṭādaśādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.118.d:
स लभेद्वाञ्छितान्कामान्सत्यं सत्यं मयोदितम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे द्वादशमासस्थितनवमीव्रतकथनं नामाष्टादशाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.118.m:
attains his desired wishes; this is spoken by me in truth, in absolute truth.

Thus ends the one hundred and eighteenth chapter in the fourth quarter of the Great Narrative in the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa, entitled "The Account of the Observances of the Ninth Days Occurring in the Twelve Months."

1.119.s:
sanātana uvāca
atha te 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi daśamyā vai vratāni ca /
yāni kṛtvā naro bhaktyā dharmarājapriyo bhavet //
1.119.d:
सनातन उवाच
अथ ते ऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि दशम्या वै व्रतानि च ।
यानि कृत्वा नरो भक्त्या धर्मराजप्रियो भवेत् ॥
1.119.m:
Sanātana said:
Now I shall declare to you the observances of the tenth day,
by performing which with devotion a man becomes dear to the King of Dharma.

1.119.s:
caitraśuklada śamyāṃ tu dharmarājaṃ prapūjayet /
tatkālasaṃbhavaiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalairgandhādibhistathā //
1.119.d:
चैत्रशुक्लद शम्यां तु धर्मराजं प्रपूजयेत् ।
तत्कालसंभवैः पुष्पैः फलैर्गन्धादिभिस्तथा ॥
1.119.m:
On the bright tenth of Caitra, one should worship the King of Dharma
with flowers produced in that season, with fruits, and with fragrances and the like.

1.119.s:
sopavāso vaikabhakto bhojayitvā dvijottamān /
caturddaśatatastebhyaḥ śaktyā dadyācca dakṣiṇām //
1.119.d:
सोपवासो वैकभक्तो भोजयित्वा द्विजोत्तमान् ।
चतुर्द्दशततस्तेभ्यः शक्त्या दद्याच्च दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.119.m:
Fasting or taking a single meal, having fed fourteen
foremost twice-born men, one should then bestow sacrificial gifts upon them according to one's capacity.

1.119.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute vipra dharmarājaprapūjanam /
sa dharmasyājñayāgaccheddevaiḥ sādharmyamacyutaḥ //
1.119.d:
एवं यः कुरुते विप्र धर्मराजप्रपूजनम् ।
स धर्मस्याज्ञयागच्छेद्देवैः साधर्म्यमच्युतः ॥
1.119.m:
He who thus performs the worship of the King of Dharma, O twice-born,
goes, infallible, to shared divinity with the gods by the command of Dharma.

1.119.s:
daśamyāṃ mādhave śukle viṣṇumabhyarcya mānavaḥ /
gandhādyairupacāraiśca śvetapuṣpaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ //
1.119.d:
दशम्यां माधवे शुक्ले विष्णुमभ्यर्च्य मानवः ।
गन्धाद्यैरुपचारैश्च श्वेतपुष्पैः सुगन्धिभिः ॥
1.119.m:
On the tenth day of the bright fortnight in Mādhava, having worshipped Viṣṇu
with offerings of fragrances and the like, and with fragrant white flowers,

1.119.s:
śataṃ pradakṣiṇāḥ kṛtvā vipransaṃbhojya yatnataḥ /
labhate vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
1.119.d:
शतं प्रदक्षिणाः कृत्वा विप्रन्संभोज्य यत्नतः ।
लभते वैष्णवं लोकं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
1.119.m:
having performed a hundred circumambulations and diligently fed the twice-born,
a mortal attains the world of Viṣṇu; no doubt should be entertained here.

1.119.s:
jyeṣṭhe śukladaśamyāṃ tu jāhnavī saritāṃ varā /
samāyātā dharāṃ svargāttasmātsā puṇyadā smṛtā //
1.119.d:
ज्येष्ठे शुक्लदशम्यां तु जाह्नवी सरितां वरा ।
समायाता धरां स्वर्गात्तस्मात्सा पुण्यदा स्मृता ॥
1.119.m:
On the bright tenth of Jyeṣṭha, the Jāhnavī, best of rivers,
came to earth from heaven; therefore it is remembered as bestowing merit.

1.119.s:
jyeṣṭhaḥ śukladalaṃ hasto budhaśca daśamīḥ tithiḥ /
garānandavyatīpātāḥ kanyenduvṛṣabhāskarāḥ //
1.119.d:
ज्येष्ठः शुक्लदलं हस्तो बुधश्च दशमीः तिथिः ।
गरानन्दव्यतीपाताः कन्येन्दुवृषभास्कराः ॥
1.119.m:
The month of Jyeṣṭha, the bright half, the Hasta asterism, Wednesday, the tenth lunar day,
the Garā division, Ānanda yoga, Vyatīpāta, the moon in Virgo, and the sun in Taurus:

1.119.s:
daśayogaḥ samākhyāto mahāpuṇyatamo dvija /
harate daśa pāpāni tasmāddaśaharaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.119.d:
दशयोगः समाख्यातो महापुण्यतमो द्विज ।
हरते दश पापानि तस्माद्दशहरः स्मृतः ॥
1.119.m:
this tenfold conjunction is declared to be most exceedingly meritorious, O twice-born;
it removes ten sins, and therefore it is known as Daśaharā.

1.119.s:
asyāṃ yo jāhnavīṃ prāpya snāti saṃprītamānasaḥ /
vidhinā jāhnavītoye sa yāti harimandiram //
1.119.d:
अस्यां यो जाह्नवीं प्राप्य स्नाति संप्रीतमानसः ।
विधिना जाह्नवीतोये स याति हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
1.119.m:
He who reaches the Jāhnavī and bathes with a delighted mind
according to the rules in the waters of the Jāhnavī on this day goes to the abode of Hari.

1.119.s:
āṣāḍhaśukladaśamī puṇyā manvā dikaiḥ smṛtā /
tasyāṃ snānaṃ japo dānaṃ homo vā svargatipradāḥ //
1.119.d:
आषाढशुक्लदशमी पुण्या मन्वा दिकैः स्मृता ।
तस्यां स्नानं जपो दानं होमो वा स्वर्गतिप्रदाः ॥
1.119.m:
The bright tenth of Āṣāḍha is remembered by Manu and others as meritorious;
bathing, recitation, gift-giving, or fire oblation on it bestows the heavenly path.

1.119.s:
śrāvaṇe śukladaśamī sarvāśāparipūrtidā /
asyāṃ śivārcanaṃ śastaṃ gandhādyai rupacārakaiḥ //
1.119.d:
श्रावणे शुक्लदशमी सर्वाशापरिपूर्तिदा ।
अस्यां शिवार्चनं शस्तं गन्धाद्यै रुपचारकैः ॥
1.119.m:
The bright tenth in Śrāvaṇa fulfills all desires;
on it, the worship of Śiva with offerings of fragrances and the like is praised.

1.119.s:
tatropavāso naktaṃ vā dvijānāṃ bhojanaṃ japaḥ /
hemno dāna ca dhenvādeḥ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
1.119.d:
तत्रोपवासो नक्तं वा द्विजानां भोजनं जपः ।
हेम्नो दान च धेन्वादेः सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
1.119.m:
A fast on that day, or an evening meal, feeding twice-born men, recitation,
and the donation of gold, cows, and the like destroy all sins.

1.119.s:
atho nabhasyaśuklāyāṃ daśamyāṃ dvijasattama /
vrataṃ daśāvatārākhyaṃ tatra snānaṃ jalāśaye //
1.119.d:
अथो नभस्यशुक्लायां दशम्यां द्विजसत्तम ।
व्रतं दशावताराख्यं तत्र स्नानं जलाशये ॥
1.119.m:
Now, on the bright tenth of Nabhasya, O best of the twice-born,
there is the observance named Daśāvatāra; having bathed there in a body of water,

1.119.s:
kṛtvā saṃdhyādiniyamaṃ devarṣipitṛtarpaṇam /
tato daśāvatārāṇi samabhyarcetsa māhitaḥ //
1.119.d:
कृत्वा संध्यादिनियमं देवर्षिपितृतर्पणम् ।
ततो दशावताराणि समभ्यर्चेत्स माहितः ॥
1.119.m:
and having performed the twilight observances and water offerings to the gods, sages, and ancestors,
one should then worship the ten incarnations with concentrated mind:

1.119.s:
matsyaṃ kūrmaṃ varāhaṃ ca narasiṃhaṃ trivikramam /
rāmaṃ rāmaṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ ca bauddhaṃ kalkinameva ca //
1.119.d:
मत्स्यं कूर्मं वराहं च नरसिंहं त्रिविक्रमम् ।
रामं रामं च कृष्णं च बौद्धं कल्किनमेव च ॥
1.119.m:
Matsya, Kūrma, Varāha, Narasiṃha, Trivikrama,
Rāma, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Buddha, and Kalkin.

1.119.s:
daśamūrtistu sauvarṇīḥ pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ /
daśabhyo vipravaryebhyo dadyātsatkṛtya nārada //
1.119.d:
दशमूर्तिस्तु सौवर्णीः पूजयित्वा विधानतः ।
दशभ्यो विप्रवर्येभ्यो दद्यात्सत्कृत्य नारद ॥
1.119.m:
Having worshipped the ten golden images according to the prescribed rules,
one should honour and give them to ten excellent twice-born men, O Nārada.

1.119.s:
upavāsaṃ caikabhaktaṃ kṛtvā saṃbhojya vāḍavān /
visṛjya paścādbhuñjīta svayaṃ sveṣṭaiḥ samāhitaḥ //
1.119.d:
उपवासं चैकभक्तं कृत्वा संभोज्य वाडवान् ।
विसृज्य पश्चाद्भुञ्जीत स्वयं स्वेष्टैः समाहितः ॥
1.119.m:
Having observed a fast or taken a single meal, and having fed the Brahmins
and dismissed them, one should eat afterwards oneself with one's dear ones, composed in mind.

1.119.s:
bhaktyā kṛtvā vrataṃ tvetadbhuktvā bhogānihottamān /
vimānena vrajedante viṣṇulokaṃ sanātanam //
1.119.d:
भक्त्या कृत्वा व्रतं त्वेतद्भुक्त्वा भोगानिहोत्तमान् ।
विमानेन व्रजेदन्ते विष्णुलोकं सनातनम् ॥
1.119.m:
Having performed this observance with devotion and enjoyed excellent pleasures here,
one goes in the end by aerial chariot to the eternal world of Viṣṇu.

1.119.s:
āśvine śukladaśamī vijayā sā prakīrtitā /
caturgomayapiṇḍāni prātarnyasya gṛhāṅgaṇe //
1.119.d:
आश्विने शुक्लदशमी विजया सा प्रकीर्तिता ।
चतुर्गोमयपिण्डानि प्रातर्न्यस्य गृहाङ्गणे ॥
1.119.m:
The bright tenth in Āśvina is celebrated as Vijayā.
Having placed four balls of cow-dung in the morning in the courtyard of the house

1.119.s:
cakravālasvarūpeṇa tanmadhye rāmalakṣmaṇau /
tathā bharataśatrughnau pūjayeccaturo 'pi hi //
1.119.d:
चक्रवालस्वरूपेण तन्मध्ये रामलक्ष्मणौ ।
तथा भरतशत्रुघ्नौ पूजयेच्चतुरो ऽपि हि ॥
1.119.m:
in the form of a circle, one should worship in their midst Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa,
as well as Bharata and Śatrughna—all four of them indeed.

1.119.s:
sapidhānāsu pātrīṣu gomayīṣu catasṛṣṭa /
kinnaṃ dhānyaṃ saraupyaṃ tu dhṛtvā dhautāṃśukāvṛtam //
1.119.d:
सपिधानासु पात्रीषु गोमयीषु चतसृष्ट ।
किन्नं धान्यं सरौप्यं तु धृत्वा धौतांशुकावृतम् ॥
1.119.m:
In four cow-dung vessels with lids,
having placed moistened grain along with silver, covered with clean cloth,

1.119.s:
pitṛmātṛbhrātṛputrajāyā bhṛtyasamanvitam /
saṃpūjyaṃ gandhapuṣpādyairnaivedyaiśca vidhānataḥ //
1.119.d:
पितृमातृभ्रातृपुत्रजाया भृत्यसमन्वितम् ।
संपूज्यं गन्धपुष्पाद्यैर्नैवेद्यैश्च विधानतः ॥
1.119.m:
together with father, mother, brothers, sons, wife, and servants,
one should worship them according to rule with fragrances, flowers, and the like, and food offerings.

1.119.s:
namaskṛtyātha bhuñjīta dvijānsaṃbhojya pūjitān /
evaṃ kṛtvā vidhānaṃ tu naro varṣaṃ suravānvitaḥ //
1.119.d:
नमस्कृत्याथ भुञ्जीत द्विजान्संभोज्य पूजितान् ।
एवं कृत्वा विधानं तु नरो वर्षं सुरवान्वितः ॥
1.119.m:
Having bowed and fed the worshipped twice-born, one should eat.
Having performed this procedure, a man, accompanied by good heroes

1.119.s:
dhanadhānyasamṛddhaśca niścitaṃ jāyate dvija /
athāpārāhnasamaye navamyāṃ saṃnimantritām //
1.119.d:
धनधान्यसमृद्धश्च निश्चितं जायते द्विज ।
अथापाराह्नसमये नवम्यां संनिमन्त्रिताम् ॥
1.119.m:
and enriched with wealth and grain, is certainly born, O twice-born.
Then, in the afternoon, having approached the śamī tree that was invited on the ninth

1.119.s:
pūrvadikṣu śamīṃ vipra gatvā tanmūlajāṃ mṛdam /
gṛhītvā svagṛhaṃ prāpya gītavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ //
1.119.d:
पूर्वदिक्षु शमीं विप्र गत्वा तन्मूलजां मृदम् ।
गृहीत्वा स्वगृहं प्राप्य गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः ॥
1.119.m:
in the eastern direction, O twice-born, and taken earth born from its root,
one should reach one's own house to the sounds of songs and musical instruments,

1.119.s:
saṃpūjya tāṃ vidhānena sajjīkṛtya svakaṃ balam /
nirgatya pūrvadvāreṇa grāmādbrahiranākulaḥ //
1.119.d:
संपूज्य तां विधानेन सज्जीकृत्य स्वकं बलम् ।
निर्गत्य पूर्वद्वारेण ग्रामाद्ब्रहिरनाकुलः ॥
1.119.m:
worship it according to the rule, and equip one's own army;
one should leave the village through the eastern gate unperturbed.

1.119.s:
tataḥ śatrupratikṛtiṃ nirmitāṃ patrakādibhiḥ /
manasā kalpitāṃ vāpi svarṇaṃ puṃravaṃśareṇa vai //
1.119.d:
ततः शत्रुप्रतिकृतिं निर्मितां पत्रकादिभिः ।
मनसा कल्पितां वापि स्वर्णं पुंरवंशरेण वै ॥
1.119.m:
Then, an effigy of the enemy fashioned from leaves and the like,
or conceived mentally, with an arrow made of reed tipped with gold,

1.119.s:
vidhyediti bhṛśaṃ prītaḥ prāpnuyātsvagṛhaṃ niśi /
evaṃ kṛtavidhirvāpi gacchedvā śatrunigrahe //
1.119.d:
विध्येदिति भृशं प्रीतः प्राप्नुयात्स्वगृहं निशि ।
एवं कृतविधिर्वापि गच्छेद्वा शत्रुनिग्रहे ॥
1.119.m:
one should pierce; greatly pleased, one should return to one's house at night.
Or having thus performed the rite, one may march forth to subdue enemies.

1.119.s:
eṣaivaṃ daśamī vipra vidhinā'caritā sadā /
dhanaṃ jayaṃ sutān gāśca gajāśvaṃ vāpyajāvikam //
1.119.d:
एषैवं दशमी विप्र विधिनाऽचरिता सदा ।
धनं जयं सुतान् गाश्च गजाश्वं वाप्यजाविकम् ॥
1.119.m:
This tenth day, O twice-born, thus observed constantly according to the rule,
gives wealth, victory, sons, cattle, elephants, horses, or goats and sheep

1.119.s:
dadyādiha śarīrānte svargatiṃ cāpi nārada /
daśamyāṃ kārtike śukle sārvabhaumavrataṃ caret //
1.119.d:
दद्यादिह शरीरान्ते स्वर्गतिं चापि नारद ।
दशम्यां कार्तिके शुक्ले सार्वभौमव्रतं चरेत् ॥
1.119.m:
in this world, and at the end of the body, heavenly realm as well, O Nārada.
On the bright tenth in Kārttika, one should observe the Sārvabhauma rite.

1.119.s:
kṛtopavāso vaikāśī niśīthe 'pūpakādibhiḥ /
daśadikṣu baliṃ dadyād gṛhadvāpi purādbrahiḥ //
1.119.d:
कृतोपवासो वैकाशी निशीथे ऽपूपकादिभिः ।
दशदिक्षु बलिं दद्याद् गृहद्वापि पुराद्ब्रहिः ॥
1.119.m:
Having fasted or eaten once, at midnight one should offer an oblation of cakes and the like
in the ten directions, either at the house door or outside the town,

1.119.s:
maṇḍale 'ṣṭadale kḷpte goviḍliptadharātale /
mantrairebhirdvijaśreṣṭha gaṇeśādikṛtārcanaḥ //
1.119.d:
मण्डले ऽष्टदले कॢप्ते गोविड्लिप्तधरातले ।
मन्त्रैरेभिर्द्विजश्रेष्ठ गणेशादिकृतार्चनः ॥
1.119.m:
upon an eight-petalled maṇḍala fashioned on the ground smeared with cow-dung,
with these mantras, O best of the twice-born, having performed the worship of Gaṇeśa and the others:

1.119.s:
yo me pūrvagataḥ pāpmā pāpakeneha karmaṇā /
tamindro devarā jo 'dya nāśayatvakhileṣṭadaḥ //
1.119.d:
यो मे पूर्वगतः पाप्मा पापकेनेह कर्मणा ।
तमिन्द्रो देवरा जो ऽद्य नाशयत्वखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.119.m: "Whatever evil has approached me from the east by sinful action here, / let Indra, the king of the gods, who grants all desires, destroy that today.

1.119.s:
yo me vahnigataḥ pāpmā pāpakeneha karmaṇā /
tejorājo 'tha vahnistaṃ nāśayatvakhileṣṭadaḥ //
1.119.d:
यो मे वह्निगतः पाप्मा पापकेनेह कर्मणा ।
तेजोराजो ऽथ वह्निस्तं नाशयत्वखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.119.m: Whatever evil has approached me from the south-east by sinful action here, / let Agni, the king of splendor, who grants all desires, destroy that.

1.119.s:
yo me dakṣagataḥ pāpmā pāpakeneha karmaṇā /
taṃ yamaḥ pretarājo vai nāśayatvakhileṣṭadaḥ //
1.119.d:
यो मे दक्षगतः पाप्मा पापकेनेह कर्मणा ।
तं यमः प्रेतराजो वै नाशयत्वखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.119.m: Whatever evil has approached me from the south by sinful action here, / let Yama, the king of spirits, who grants all desires, destroy that.

1.119.s:
yo me nairṛtigaḥ pāpmā pāpakeneha karmaṇā /
rakṣorājo nairṛtistaṃ nāśayatvakhileṣṭadaḥ //
1.119.d:
यो मे नैरृतिगः पाप्मा पापकेनेह कर्मणा ।
रक्षोराजो नैरृतिस्तं नाशयत्वखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.119.m: Whatever evil has approached me from the south-west by sinful action here, / let Nairṛta, the king of rākṣasas, who grants all desires, destroy that.

1.119.s:
yo me paścimagaḥ pāpmā pāpakenehakarmaṇā /
yādaḥ patistaṃ varuṇo nāśayatvakhileṣṭadaḥ //
1.119.d:
यो मे पश्चिमगः पाप्मा पापकेनेहकर्मणा ।
यादः पतिस्तं वरुणो नाशयत्वखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.119.m: Whatever evil has approached me from the west by sinful action here, / let Varuṇa, the lord of aquatic creatures, who grants all desires, destroy that.

1.119.s:
yo me vāyugataḥ pāpmā pāpakeneha karmaṇā /
vāyustaṃ marutāṃ rājo nāśayatvakhileṣṭadaḥ //
1.119.d:
यो मे वायुगतः पाप्मा पापकेनेह कर्मणा ।
वायुस्तं मरुतां राजो नाशयत्वखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.119.m: Whatever evil has approached me from the north-west by sinful action here, / let Vāyu, the king of the Maruts, who grants all desires, destroy that.

1.119.s:
yo me saumyagataḥ pāpmā pāpakeneha karmaṇā /
somastamṛkṣayakṣeśo nāśayatvakhileṣṭadaḥ //
1.119.d:
यो मे सौम्यगतः पाप्मा पापकेनेह कर्मणा ।
सोमस्तमृक्षयक्षेशो नाशयत्वखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.119.m: Whatever evil has approached me from the north by sinful action here, / let Soma, the lord of asterisms and yakṣas, who grants all desires, destroy that.

1.119.s:
yo ma īśagataḥ pāpmā pāpakeneha karmaṇā /
īśāno bhūtanāthastaṃ nāśayatvakhileṣṭadaḥ //
1.119.d:
यो म ईशगतः पाप्मा पापकेनेह कर्मणा ।
ईशानो भूतनाथस्तं नाशयत्वखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.119.m: Whatever evil has approached me from the north-east by sinful action here, / let Īśāna, the lord of spirits, who grants all desires, destroy that.

1.119.s:
yo maṃ ūrddhvagataḥ pāpmā pāpakeneha karmaṇā /
brahmā prajāpatīśastaṃ nāśayatvakhileṣṭadaḥ //
1.119.d:
यो मं ऊर्द्ध्वगतः पाप्मा पापकेनेह कर्मणा ।
ब्रह्मा प्रजापतीशस्तं नाशयत्वखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.119.m: Whatever evil has approached me from above by sinful action here, / let Brahmā, the lord of the Prajāpatis, who grants all desires, destroy that.

1.119.s:
yo me 'dhaḥsaṃsthitaḥ pāpmā pāpakeneha karmaṇā /
ananto nāgarājastaṃ nāśayatvakhileṣṭadaḥ //
1.119.d:
यो मे ऽधःसंस्थितः पाप्मा पापकेनेह कर्मणा ।
अनन्तो नागराजस्तं नाशयत्वखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.119.m: Whatever evil has resided below me by sinful action here, / let Ananta, the king of snakes, who grants all desires, destroy that."

1.119.s:
ityevaṃ dikṣu daśasu baliṃ datvā samāhitaḥ /
kṣetrapālāya tadbāhye kṣipedbalimatandritaḥ //
1.119.d:
इत्येवं दिक्षु दशसु बलिं दत्वा समाहितः ।
क्षेत्रपालाय तद्बाह्ये क्षिपेद्बलिमतन्द्रितः ॥
1.119.m: Having thus offered a sacrifice in the ten directions with focused mind, / one should, unwearied, toss an offering outside of that to the guardian of the field.

1.119.s:
evaṃ kṛtavidhiḥ śeṣaṃ niśāyāṃ ninayetsudhīḥ /
gītaiḥ sumaṅgalaprāyaiḥ stavapāṭhairjapādibhiḥ //
1.119.d:
एवं कृतविधिः शेषं निशायां निनयेत्सुधीः ।
गीतैः सुमङ्गलप्रायैः स्तवपाठैर्जपादिभिः ॥
1.119.m: Having thus performed the rite, the wise one should pass the remainder of the night / with songs predominantly auspicious, with recitations of hymns of praise, recitations of mantras, and the like.

1.119.s:
prātaḥ snātvā samabhyarcya lokapālān dvijottamān /
dvādaśābhyarcya saṃbhojya śaktito dakṣiṇāṃ dadet //
1.119.d:
प्रातः स्नात्वा समभ्यर्च्य लोकपालान् द्विजोत्तमान् ।
द्वादशाभ्यर्च्य संभोज्य शक्तितो दक्षिणां ददेत् ॥
1.119.m: Having bathed in the morning and worshipped the guardians of the worlds, having worshipped twelve / excellent brāhmaṇas and fed them, he should give a priestly fee according to his capacity.

1.119.s:
itthaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra bhogānbhuktaihikāñchubhān /
yugaṃ svargasukhaṃ bhuktvā sārvabhaumo nṛpo bhavet //
1.119.d:
इत्थं कृत्वा व्रतं विप्र भोगान्भुक्तैहिकाञ्छुभान् ।
युगं स्वर्गसुखं भुक्त्वा सार्वभौमो नृपो भवेत् ॥
1.119.m: Having performed this observance thus, O brāhmaṇa, enjoying auspicious earthly pleasures, / and having enjoyed the happiness of heaven for a yuga, he will become an emperor.

1.119.s:
mārgaśukladaśamyāṃ tu caredā rogyakaṃ vratam /
gandhādyairarcayedviprān daśa taccaraṇodakam //
1.119.d:
मार्गशुक्लदशम्यां तु चरेदा रोग्यकं व्रतम् ।
गन्धाद्यैरर्चयेद्विप्रान् दश तच्चरणोदकम् ॥
1.119.m: On the bright tenth of Mārgaśīrṣa, one should perform the observance for health; / he should worship ten brāhmaṇas with perfumes and the like; having drunk the water of their feet,

1.119.s:
pītvātha dakṣiṇāṃ datvā visūjedekabhojanaṃ /
etatkṛtvā vrataṃ vipra hyārogyaṃ prāpya bhūtale //
1.119.d:
पीत्वाथ दक्षिणां दत्वा विसूजेदेकभोजनं ।
एतत्कृत्वा व्रतं विप्र ह्यारोग्यं प्राप्य भूतले ॥
1.119.m: and then having given a priestly fee, eating a single meal, he should dismiss them. / Having performed this observance, O brāhmaṇa, having attained health on the surface of the earth,

1.119.s:
dharmarājaprasādena modate divi devavat /
pauṣe daśamyāṃ śuklāyāṃ viśvedevān samarcayet //
1.119.d:
धर्मराजप्रसादेन मोदते दिवि देववत् ।
पौषे दशम्यां शुक्लायां विश्वेदेवान् समर्चयेत् ॥
1.119.m: he rejoices in heaven like a god by the grace of the King of Justice. / On the bright tenth in Pauṣa, one should worship the Viśvedevas:

1.119.s:
ṛtuṃ dakṣaṃ vasū6nsatyaṃ kālaṃ kāmaṃ muniṃ gurum /
vipraṃ rāmaṃ ca daśadhā keśavastānsamāsthitaḥ //
1.119.d:
ऋतुं दक्षं वसू6न्सत्यं कालं कामं मुनिं गुरुम् ।
विप्रं रामं च दशधा केशवस्तान्समास्थितः ॥
1.119.m: Ṛtu, Dakṣa, Vasu, Satya, Kāla, Kāma, Muni, Guru, / Vipra, and Rāma—Keśava resides in them ten-fold.

1.119.s:
svāpayitvā darbhamayānāsaneṣu ca saṃsthitān /
gandhairdhūpaistathā dīpairnaivedyaiścāpi nārada //
1.119.d:
स्वापयित्वा दर्भमयानासनेषु च संस्थितान् ।
गन्धैर्धूपैस्तथा दीपैर्नैवेद्यैश्चापि नारद ॥
1.119.m: Having installed them made of darbha grass, seated upon seats, / [worshipping them] with perfumes, incenses, and lamps, as well as food offerings, O Nārada,

1.119.s:
pratyekaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ datvā praṇiyatya visarjayet /
dakṣiṇāṃ tāṃ dvijāgryebhyo gurave vā samarpayet //
1.119.d:
प्रत्येकं दक्षिणां दत्वा प्रणियत्य विसर्जयेत् ।
दक्षिणां तां द्विजाग्र्येभ्यो गुरवे वा समर्पयेत् ॥
1.119.m: giving a priestly fee to each and bowing down, he should bid farewell to them; / he should offer that priestly fee to the best of brāhmaṇas or to the guru.

1.119.s:
evaṃ kṛtavidhi ścaikabhakto bhogī vratī bhavet /
lokadvayasya viprarṣe nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
māghaśukladaśamyāṃ tu sopavāso jitendriyaḥ ///
1.119.d:
एवं कृतविधि श्चैकभक्तो भोगी व्रती भवेत् ।
लोकद्वयस्य विप्रर्षे नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
माघशुक्लदशम्यां तु सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः ॥।
1.119.m:
One who has thus performed the rite and eats a single meal becomes a practitioner of the observance who enjoys pleasures / in both worlds, O brāhmaṇa-sage; no doubt should be entertained on this matter.

On the bright tenth day of Māgha, however, fasting and having subdued his senses,

1.119.s: devāṃnagiraso nāma daśa samyaksamarcayet //
1.119.d: देवांनगिरसो नाम दश सम्यक्समर्चयेत् ॥
1.119.m: one should properly worship the ten gods known as the Āṅgirasas,

1.119.s:
kṛtvā svarṇamayānvipra gandhādyairupacārakaiḥ /
ātmā hyāyurmano dakṣo madaḥ prāṇastathaiva ca //
1.119.d:
कृत्वा स्वर्णमयान्विप्र गन्धाद्यैरुपचारकैः ।
आत्मा ह्यायुर्मनो दक्षो मदः प्राणस्तथैव च ॥
1.119.m: having fashioned them out of gold, O brahmin, with services such as perfumes and other offerings: / Ātman, Āyus, Manas, Dakṣa, Mada, and likewise Prāṇa,

1.119.s:
barhiṣmāṃśca gaviṣṭhaśca dattaḥ satyaśca te daśa /
daśa viprānbhojayitvā madhurānnena nārada //
1.119.d:
बर्हिष्मांश्च गविष्ठश्च दत्तः सत्यश्च ते दश ।
दश विप्रान्भोजयित्वा मधुरान्नेन नारद ॥
1.119.m: Barhiṣmat, Gaviṣṭha, Datta, and Satya—these are the ten. / Having fed ten brahmins with sweet food, O Nārada,

1.119.s:
mūrtīstebhyaḥ pradadyāttāḥ svargalokāptaye kramāt /
antyaśukladaśamyāṃ tu caturdaśaṃ yamānyajet //
1.119.d:
मूर्तीस्तेभ्यः प्रदद्यात्ताः स्वर्गलोकाप्तये क्रमात् ।
अन्त्यशुक्लदशम्यां तु चतुर्दशं यमान्यजेत् ॥
1.119.m: one should present those images to them in order to attain the heavenly world. / On the final bright tenth day, however, one should worship the fourteen Yamas:

1.119.s:
yamaśca dharmarājaśca mṛtyuścaivāntakastathā /
vaivasvataśca kālaśca sarvabhūtakṣayastathā //
1.119.d:
यमश्च धर्मराजश्च मृत्युश्चैवान्तकस्तथा ।
वैवस्वतश्च कालश्च सर्वभूतक्षयस्तथा ॥
1.119.m: Yama, Dharmarāja, Mṛtyu, and Antaka, / Vaivasvata, Kāla, and Sarvabhūtakṣaya,

1.119.s:
audumbaraśca daghnaśca dvau nīlaparameṣṭhinau /
vṛkodaraścacitraśca citraguptaścaturdaśa //
1.119.d:
औदुम्बरश्च दघ्नश्च द्वौ नीलपरमेष्ठिनौ ।
वृकोदरश्चचित्रश्च चित्रगुप्तश्चतुर्दश ॥
1.119.m: Audumbara, Daghna, the two Nīla and Parameṣṭhin, / Vṛkodara, Citra, and Citragupta—the fourteen.

1.119.s:
gandhādyairupacāraiśca samabhyarcyāthatarpayet /
tilāṃbumiśrāñjalibhirdarbhaiḥ pratyekaśastribhiḥ //
1.119.d:
गन्धाद्यैरुपचारैश्च समभ्यर्च्याथतर्पयेत् ।
तिलांबुमिश्राञ्जलिभिर्दर्भैः प्रत्येकशस्त्रिभिः ॥
1.119.m: Having worshipped them with offerings such as perfumes and other services, one should then make water libations / with three handfuls of water mixed with sesame seeds and with kuśa grass for each one.

1.119.s:
tataśca dadyātsūryārghaṃ tāmrapātreṇa nārada /
raktacandanasaṃmiśratilākṣatayavāṃbubhiḥ //
1.119.d:
ततश्च दद्यात्सूर्यार्घं ताम्रपात्रेण नारद ।
रक्तचन्दनसंमिश्रतिलाक्षतयवांबुभिः ॥
1.119.m: Then, O Nārada, one should offer water oblation to Sūrya using a copper vessel, / with water mixed with red sandalwood, sesame seeds, unbroken rice, and barley:

1.119.s:
ehi sūryasahasrāṃśo tejorāśe jagatpate /
gṛhāṇārghyaṃ mayā dattaṃ bhaktyā māmanukaṃpaya //
1.119.d:
एहि सूर्यसहस्रांशो तेजोराशे जगत्पते ।
गृहाणार्घ्यं मया दत्तं भक्त्या मामनुकंपय ॥
1.119.m: “Come, O Sūrya of a thousand rays, mass of radiance, Lord of the Universe! / Accept this water oblation offered by me with devotion; have compassion on me.”

1.119.s:
iti mantreṇa datvārghyaṃ viprānbhojya caturddaśa /
raupyāṃ sudakṣiṇāṃ datvā visṛjyāśnīta ca svayam //
1.119.d:
इति मन्त्रेण दत्वार्घ्यं विप्रान्भोज्य चतुर्द्दश ।
रौप्यां सुदक्षिणां दत्वा विसृज्याश्नीत च स्वयम् ॥
1.119.m: Having offered the water oblation with this mantra, fed fourteen brahmins, / given generous sacrificial fees of silver, and dismissed them, one should eat oneself.

1.119.s:
evaṃ kṛtavidhirvipra dharmarājaprasādataḥ /
bhuktvā bhogāṃśca putrārthānaihikāndevadurlabhān //
1.119.d:
एवं कृतविधिर्विप्र धर्मराजप्रसादतः ।
भुक्त्वा भोगांश्च पुत्रार्थानैहिकान्देवदुर्लभान् ॥
1.119.m: One who has thus performed the rite, O brahmin, through the grace of Dharmarāja, / having enjoyed pleasures, sons, and wealth in this world, rare even for gods,

1.119.s:
vimānavaramāsthāya dehānte viṣṇulokabhāk //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde dvādaśamāsasthitadaśamīvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikonaviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.119.d:
विमानवरमास्थाय देहान्ते विष्णुलोकभाक् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे द्वादशमासस्थितदशमीव्रतनिरूपणं नामैकोनविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.119.m:
mounts an excellent aerial chariot and at the end of the body attains the world of Viṣṇu.

Thus ends the one hundred nineteenth chapter in the fourth quarter of the Great Narrative in the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa, entitled “Description of the Tenth-Day Observances in the Twelve Months.”

1.120.s:
sanātana uvāca
ekādaśyāṃ tu dalayornirāhāraḥ samāhitaḥ /
nānāpuṣpairmune kṛtvā vicitraṃ maṇḍapaṃ śubham //
1.120.d:
सनातन उवाच
एकादश्यां तु दलयोर्निराहारः समाहितः ।
नानापुष्पैर्मुने कृत्वा विचित्रं मण्डपं शुभम् ॥
1.120.m: Sanātana said: / On the eleventh day in both fortnights, abstaining from food and concentrated in mind, / having constructed a splendid and beautiful pavilion with various flowers, O sage,

1.120.s:
srātvā samyagvidhānena sopavāso jitendriyaḥ /
saṃpūjya vidhivadviṣṇuṃ śraddhayā susamāhitaḥ //
1.120.d:
स्रात्वा सम्यग्विधानेन सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः ।
संपूज्य विधिवद्विष्णुं श्रद्धया सुसमाहितः ॥
1.120.m: having bathed according to proper rule, fasting, with restrained senses, / having worshipped Viṣṇu according to injunction with faith and deep concentration,

1.120.s:
upacārairbahuvidhairjapairhemaiḥ pradakṣiṇaiḥ /
stotrapāṭhairbahuvidhairgītavādyairmanoharaiḥ //
1.120.d:
उपचारैर्बहुविधैर्जपैर्हेमैः प्रदक्षिणैः ।
स्तोत्रपाठैर्बहुविधैर्गीतवाद्यैर्मनोहरैः ॥
1.120.m: with numerous services, recitations, fire oblations, circumambulations, / readings of various hymns of praise, and charming songs and instrumental music,

1.120.s:
daṇḍavatpraṇipātaiśca jayaśabdairmanoharaiḥ /
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā yāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam //
1.120.d:
दण्डवत्प्रणिपातैश्च जयशब्दैर्मनोहरैः ।
रात्रौ जागरणं कृत्वा याति विष्णोः परं पदम् ॥
1.120.m: with prostrations like a staff and charming cries of “Victory!”, / having kept a night vigil, he goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

1.120.s:
caitrasya śuklaikādaśyāṃ sopavāso narottamaḥ /
kṛtvā ca niyamānsarvānvakṣyamāṇāndinatraye //
1.120.d:
चैत्रस्य शुक्लैकादश्यां सोपवासो नरोत्तमः ।
कृत्वा च नियमान्सर्वान्वक्ष्यमाणान्दिनत्रये ॥
1.120.m: Fasting on the bright eleventh day of Caitra, the best of men, / having observed all the restrictions to be described over three days,

1.120.s:
dvādaśyāmarcayedbhaktayā vāsudevaṃ sanātanam /
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhistataḥ saṃbhojya bāndhavān //
datvā ca dakṣiṇāṃ tebhyo visṛjyāśnīta ca svayam ///
1.120.d:
द्वादश्यामर्चयेद्भक्तया वासुदेवं सनातनम् ।
उपचारैः षोडशभिस्ततः संभोज्य बान्धवान् ॥
दत्वा च दक्षिणां तेभ्यो विसृज्याश्नीत च स्वयम् ॥।
1.120.m:
should worship the eternal Vāsudeva on the twelfth day with devotion / through sixteen forms of service. Then, having fed his relatives,

and given them a sacrificial fee, he should dismiss them and eat himself.

1.120.s: iyaṃ tu kāmadā nāma sarvapātakanāśinī //
1.120.d: इयं तु कामदा नाम सर्वपातकनाशिनी ॥
1.120.m: This [eleventh day] is called Kāmadā, the destroyer of all sins;

1.120.s:
bhuktimuktipradā vipra bhaktyā samyagupoṣitā /
vaiśākhakṛṣṇaikādaśyāṃ samupoṣya vidhānataḥ //
1.120.d:
भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदा विप्र भक्त्या सम्यगुपोषिता ।
वैशाखकृष्णैकादश्यां समुपोष्य विधानतः ॥
1.120.m: it grants worldly enjoyment and liberation, O brahmin, when fasted on properly with devotion. / Having fasted according to rule on the dark eleventh day of Vaiśākha,

1.120.s:
varūthinīṃ paradine pūjayenmṛdhusūdanam /
svarṇānnakanyādhenūnāṃ dānamatra praśasyate //
1.120.d:
वरूथिनीं परदिने पूजयेन्मृधुसूदनम् ।
स्वर्णान्नकन्याधेनूनां दानमत्र प्रशस्यते ॥
1.120.m: [known as] Varūthinī, one should worship Madhusūdana on the next day. / The gift of gold, food, a maiden, and cows is praised here.

1.120.s:
varūthinīvrataṃ kṛtvā naro niyamatatparaḥ /
sarvapāpa vinirmukto vaiṣṇavaṃ labhate padvam //
1.120.d:
वरूथिनीव्रतं कृत्वा नरो नियमतत्परः ।
सर्वपाप विनिर्मुक्तो वैष्णवं लभते पद्वम् ॥
1.120.m: Having performed the Varūthinī observance, a man intent upon religious vows, / freed from all sins, attains the Vaiṣṇava state.

1.120.s:
vaiśākhaśuklaikādaśyāṃ samupoṣya ca mohinīm /
snātvā pare 'hni saṃpūjya gandhādyaiḥ puruṣottamam //
1.120.d:
वैशाखशुक्लैकादश्यां समुपोष्य च मोहिनीम् ।
स्नात्वा परे ऽह्नि संपूज्य गन्धाद्यैः पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
1.120.m: Having fasted on the bright eleventh day of Vaiśākha, [known as] Mohinī, / bathing and worshipping Puruṣottama on the following day with perfumes and other offerings,

1.120.s:
saṃbhojya viprānmucyeta pātakebhyo na saṃśayaḥ /
jeṣṭhasya kṛṣṇakādaśyāṃ samupoṣya parāṃ nṛpa //
1.120.d:
संभोज्य विप्रान्मुच्येत पातकेभ्यो न संशयः ।
जेष्ठस्य कृष्णकादश्यां समुपोष्य परां नृप ॥
1.120.m: and feeding brahmins, he is freed from sins; there is no doubt. / Having fasted on the dark eleventh day of Jyeṣṭha, [known as] Parā, O king,

1.120.s:
dvādaśyāṃ naityikaṃ kṛtvā samabhyarcya trivikramam /
tato dvijāgryānsaṃbhojya datvā tebhyaśca dakṣiṇām //
1.120.d:
द्वादश्यां नैत्यिकं कृत्वा समभ्यर्च्य त्रिविक्रमम् ।
ततो द्विजाग्र्यान्संभोज्य दत्वा तेभ्यश्च दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.120.m: having performed the daily rites on the twelfth day and worshipped Trivikrama, / then feeding excellent brahmins and giving them a sacrificial fee,

1.120.s:
sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ vrajennaraḥ /
jyeṣṭhasya śuklaikādaśyāṃ nirjalāṃ samupoṣya tu //
1.120.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो विष्णुलोकं व्रजेन्नरः ।
ज्येष्ठस्य शुक्लैकादश्यां निर्जलां समुपोष्य तु ॥
1.120.m: A man, completely freed from all sins, goes to the world of Viṣṇu. / Fasting without water on the bright eleventh lunar day of Jyeṣṭha,

1.120.s:
udayādudayaṃ yāvadbhāskarasya dvijottama /
prabhāte kṛtanityastu dvādaśyāmupacārakaiḥ //
1.120.d:
उदयादुदयं यावद्भास्करस्य द्विजोत्तम ।
प्रभाते कृतनित्यस्तु द्वादश्यामुपचारकैः ॥
1.120.m: from sunrise to sunrise [the next day], O best of Brahmins, / and having performed the daily rites in the morning of the twelfth lunar day, with offerings

1.120.s:
hyaṣīkeśaṃ samabhyarcya viprān saṃbhojya bhaktitaḥ /
caturviṃśaikādaśīnāṃ phalaṃ yattatsamāpnuyāt //
1.120.d:
ह्यषीकेशं समभ्यर्च्य विप्रान् संभोज्य भक्तितः ।
चतुर्विंशैकादशीनां फलं यत्तत्समाप्नुयात् ॥
1.120.m: having worshipped Hṛṣīkeśa and fed the Brahmins with devotion, / one obtains whatever fruit belongs to the twenty-four eleventh lunar days.

1.120.s:
āṣāḍhakṛṣṇaikādaśyāṃ yoginīṃ samupoṣya vai /
nārāyaṇaṃ samabhyarcya dvādaśyāṃ kṛtanityakaḥ //
1.120.d:
आषाढकृष्णैकादश्यां योगिनीं समुपोष्य वै ।
नारायणं समभ्यर्च्य द्वादश्यां कृतनित्यकः ॥
1.120.m: Having indeed fasted on the Yoginī [fast] on the dark eleventh lunar day of Āṣāḍha, / having worshipped Nārāyaṇa on the twelfth lunar day, after performing his daily rites,

1.120.s:
tataḥ saṃbhojya viprāgryāndatvā tebhyaśca dakṣiṇām /
sarvadānaphalaṃ prāpya modate viṣṇumandire //
1.120.d:
ततः संभोज्य विप्राग्र्यान्दत्वा तेभ्यश्च दक्षिणाम् ।
सर्वदानफलं प्राप्य मोदते विष्णुमन्दिरे ॥
1.120.m: and then having fed the best of Brahmins and given them a priestly fee, / having attained the fruit of all gifts, he rejoices in the abode of Viṣṇu.

1.120.s:
āṣāḍhaśuklaikādaśyāṃ yadbidhānaṃ śṛṇuṣva tat /
upoṣya tasmin divase vidhivanmaṇḍape śubhe //
1.120.d:
आषाढशुक्लैकादश्यां यद्बिधानं शृणुष्व तत् ।
उपोष्य तस्मिन् दिवसे विधिवन्मण्डपे शुभे ॥
1.120.m: Hear that procedure which is [prescribed] for the bright eleventh lunar day of Āṣāḍha: / having fasted on that day, according to rule, in an auspicious pavilion,

1.120.s:
sthāpayetpratimāṃ viṣṇoḥ śaṅkhacakragadāṃbujaiḥ /
lasaccaturbhujāmagryāṃ kāñcanīṃ vātha rājatīm //
1.120.d:
स्थापयेत्प्रतिमां विष्णोः शङ्खचक्रगदांबुजैः ।
लसच्चतुर्भुजामग्र्यां काञ्चनीं वाथ राजतीम् ॥
1.120.m: one should install an image of Viṣṇu, shining with four arms, / with conch, discus, mace, and lotus, made of gold or silver, the best,

1.120.s:
pītāṃbaradharāṃ śubhre paryyaṅke svāstṛte dvija /
tataḥ pañcāmṛtaiḥ snāpya mantraiḥ śuddhajalena ca //
1.120.d:
पीतांबरधरां शुभ्रे पर्य्यङ्के स्वास्तृते द्विज ।
ततः पञ्चामृतैः स्नाप्य मन्त्रैः शुद्धजलेन च ॥
1.120.m: wearing yellow garments, upon a white, well-spread couch, O Brahmin. / Then, having bathed [it] with the five nectars, with mantras, and with pure water,

1.120.s:
pauruṣeṇaiva sūktena hyupacārān prakalpayet /
nīrājanāntānpādyādīṃstataḥ saṃprārthayeddharim //
1.120.d:
पौरुषेणैव सूक्तेन ह्युपचारान् प्रकल्पयेत् ।
नीराजनान्तान्पाद्यादींस्ततः संप्रार्थयेद्धरिम् ॥
1.120.m: one should offer the services with the Puruṣasūkta alone, / ending with the waving of lights, beginning with water for washing the feet; then one should pray to Hari:

1.120.s:
supte tvayi jagannātha jagatsuptaṃ bhavedidam /
vibuddhe tvayi buddhaṃ ca jagatsarvaṃ carācaram //
1.120.d:
सुप्ते त्वयि जगन्नाथ जगत्सुप्तं भवेदिदम् ।
विबुद्धे त्वयि बुद्धं च जगत्सर्वं चराचरम् ॥
1.120.m: ‘When you are asleep, O Lord of the world, this world is asleep; / when you awaken, the entire world of moving and unmoving things is awake.’

1.120.s:
iti saṃprārthya devāgre cāturmāsyapracoditān /
niyamāṃstu yathāśakti gṛhṇīyādbhaktimānnaraḥ //
1.120.d:
इति संप्रार्थ्य देवाग्रे चातुर्मास्यप्रचोदितान् ।
नियमांस्तु यथाशक्ति गृह्णीयाद्भक्तिमान्नरः ॥
1.120.m: Having prayed thus before the god, a devoted man / should undertake, according to his ability, the observances enjoined for the four-month rainy retreat.

1.120.s:
tataḥ prabhāte dvādaśyāṃ samarceccheṣaśāyinam /
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhistataḥ saṃbhojya vāḍavān //
1.120.d:
ततः प्रभाते द्वादश्यां समर्चेच्छेषशायिनम् ।
उपचारैः षोडशभिस्ततः संभोज्य वाडवान् ॥
1.120.m: Then, in the morning of the twelfth lunar day, he should worship the one who reclines on Śeṣa / with sixteen offerings, and then, having fed the Brahmins,

1.120.s:
pratoṣya dabhiṇābhiśca svayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ /
tataḥ prabhṛti viprendra gandhādyaiḥ pratyahaṃ yajet //
1.120.d:
प्रतोष्य दभिणाभिश्च स्वयं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ।
ततः प्रभृति विप्रेन्द्र गन्धाद्यैः प्रत्यहं यजेत् ॥
1.120.m: and having satisfied them with priestly fees, he himself should eat, restrained in speech. / From then on, O chief of Brahmins, he should worship [him] daily with perfumes and other offerings.

1.120.s:
kṛtvaivaṃ vidhinā vipra devasya śayanīvratam /
bhuktimuktiyuto martyo bhavedviṣṇoḥ prasādataḥ //
1.120.d:
कृत्वैवं विधिना विप्र देवस्य शयनीव्रतम् ।
भुक्तिमुक्तियुतो मर्त्यो भवेद्विष्णोः प्रसादतः ॥
1.120.m: Having performed the god’s sleep-vow according to rule in this manner, O Brahmin, / a mortal, endowed with enjoyment and liberation, becomes [blessed] through the grace of Viṣṇu.

1.120.s:
śrāvaṇe kṛṣṇapakṣe tu ekādaśyāṃ dvijottama /
kāmikāṃ samupoṣyaiva niyamena narottama //
1.120.d:
श्रावणे कृष्णपक्षे तु एकादश्यां द्विजोत्तम ।
कामिकां समुपोष्यैव नियमेन नरोत्तम ॥
1.120.m: On the dark fortnight of Śrāvaṇa, on the eleventh lunar day, O best of Brahmins, / having fasted on the Kāmikā [fast] strictly, O best of men,

1.120.s:
dvādaśyāṃ kṛtanityastu śrīdharaṃ pūjayeddharim /
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśa bhistataḥ saṃbhojya vai dvijān //
1.120.d:
द्वादश्यां कृतनित्यस्तु श्रीधरं पूजयेद्धरिम् ।
उपचारैः षोडश भिस्ततः संभोज्य वै द्विजान् ॥
1.120.m: having performed his daily rites on the twelfth lunar day, he should worship Hari, the bearer of Śrī, / with sixteen offerings, and then, having fed the Brahmins,

1.120.s:
datvā ca dakṣiṇāṃ tebhyo visṛjyāśnīta bāndhavaiḥ /
evaṃ yaḥ kurute viprakāmikāvratamuttamam //
1.120.d:
दत्वा च दक्षिणां तेभ्यो विसृज्याश्नीत बान्धवैः ।
एवं यः कुरुते विप्रकामिकाव्रतमुत्तमम् ॥
1.120.m: and having given them a priestly fee, and dismissed them, he should eat with his relatives. / The person who thus performs the excellent Kāmikā vow, O Brahmin,

1.120.s:
sa sarvakāmāṃllabdhveha yāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam /
ekādaśyāṃ nabhaḥśukle pavitrāṃ samupoṣya vai //
1.120.d:
स सर्वकामांल्लब्ध्वेह याति विष्णोः परं पदम् ।
एकादश्यां नभःशुक्ले पवित्रां समुपोष्य वै ॥
1.120.m: having obtained all desires in this world, goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. / Having fasted on the Pavitrā [fast] on the bright eleventh lunar day of Nabhas (Śrāvaṇa),

1.120.s:
dvādaśyāṃ niyato bhūtvā pūjayecca janārdanam /
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhistataḥ saṃbhojya vāḍavān //
1.120.d:
द्वादश्यां नियतो भूत्वा पूजयेच्च जनार्दनम् ।
उपचारैः षोडशभिस्ततः संभोज्य वाडवान् ॥
1.120.m: and having become restrained, he should worship Janārdana on the twelfth lunar day / with sixteen offerings, and then, having fed the Brahmins,

1.120.s:
/.
datvā ca dakṣiṇāṃ tebhyaḥ putraṃ prāpyeha sadguṇam /
yāti viṣṇoḥ padaṃ sākṣātsarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ //
1.120.d:
॥
दत्वा च दक्षिणां तेभ्यः पुत्रं प्राप्येह सद्गुणम् ।
याति विष्णोः पदं साक्षात्सर्वदेवनमस्कृतः ॥
1.120.m: and having given them a priestly fee, having obtained a virtuous son in this world, / he goes directly to the abode of Viṣṇu, bowed to by all the gods.

1.120.s:
nabhasyakṛṣṇaikā daśyāmajākhyāṃ samupoṣya vai /
arcedurpendraṃ dvādaśyāmupacāraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ //
1.120.d:
नभस्यकृष्णैका दश्यामजाख्यां समुपोष्य वै ।
अर्चेदुर्पेन्द्रं द्वादश्यामुपचारैः पृथग्विधैः ॥
1.120.m: Having fasted on the one called Ajā on the dark eleventh lunar day of Nabhasya (Bhādrapada), / he should worship Upendra on the twelfth lunar day with various kinds of offerings.

1.120.s:
viprānsaṃbhojya miṣṭānnairvisṛjetprāptadakṣiṇān /
evaṃ kṛtavrato viprabhaktyājāyāḥ samāhitaḥ //
1.120.d:
विप्रान्संभोज्य मिष्टान्नैर्विसृजेत्प्राप्तदक्षिणान् ।
एवं कृतव्रतो विप्रभक्त्याजायाः समाहितः ॥
1.120.m: Having fed the Brahmins with sweet foods, he should dismiss them after they have received their priestly fees. / Having thus performed the vow of Ajā with devotion and concentration, O Brahmin,

1.120.s:
bhuktveha bhogānakhilānyātyante vaiṣṇavaṃ kṣayam /
nabhasyaśuklaikādaśyāṃ padmākhyāṃ samupoṣya vai //
1.120.d:
भुक्त्वेह भोगानखिलान्यात्यन्ते वैष्णवं क्षयम् ।
नभस्यशुक्लैकादश्यां पद्माख्यां समुपोष्य वै ॥
1.120.m: having enjoyed all pleasures in this world, he goes at the end to the realm of Viṣṇu. / Having fasted on the one called Padmā on the bright eleventh lunar day of Nabhasya,

1.120.s:
kṛtvā nityārcanaṃ tatra kaṭidānamathācaret /
pūrvaṃ saṃsthāpitāyāstu pratimāyā dvijottama //
1.120.d:
कृत्वा नित्यार्चनं तत्र कटिदानमथाचरेत् ।
पूर्वं संस्थापितायास्तु प्रतिमाया द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.120.m: and having performed the daily worship there, he should then perform the turning of the side. / Of the image previously installed, O best of Brahmins,

1.120.s:
samutsavavidhānena nītvā tāṃ salilāśaye /
kṛtāṃbusparśanāṃ tatra saṃprapūjya vidhānataḥ //
1.120.d:
समुत्सवविधानेन नीत्वा तां सलिलाशये ।
कृतांबुस्पर्शनां तत्र संप्रपूज्य विधानतः ॥
1.120.m: having taken it to a reservoir of water with festive celebration, / having had it touch the water there and worshipped it properly,

1.120.s:
ānīya maṇḍape tasmin vāmapārśvena śāyayet /
tataḥ prabhāpte dvādaśyāṃ gandhādyairarcya vāmanam //
1.120.d:
आनीय मण्डपे तस्मिन् वामपार्श्वेन शाययेत् ।
ततः प्रभाप्ते द्वादश्यां गन्धाद्यैरर्च्य वामनम् ॥
1.120.m: and having brought it back to that pavilion, he should lay it down on its left side. / Then, in the morning of the twelfth lunar day, having worshipped Vāmana with perfumes and other offerings,

1.120.s:
saṃbhojya vāḍavāndatvā dakṣiṇāṃ ca visarjayet /
evaṃ yaḥ kurute vipra padmāvratamanuttamam //
1.120.d:
संभोज्य वाडवान्दत्वा दक्षिणां च विसर्जयेत् ।
एवं यः कुरुते विप्र पद्माव्रतमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.120.m: having fed the Brahmins and given a priestly fee, he should dismiss them. / The person who thus performs the unsurpassed Padmā vow, O Brahmin,

1.120.s:
bhuktiṃ prāpyeha muktiṃ tu labhateṃ'te prapañcataḥ /
iṣasya kṛṣṇaikā daśyāmindirāṃ samupoṣya vai //
1.120.d:
भुक्तिं प्राप्येह मुक्तिं तु लभतेंऽते प्रपञ्चतः ।
इषस्य कृष्णैका दश्यामिन्दिरां समुपोष्य वै ॥
1.120.m: having attained enjoyment in this world, obtains liberation from the manifest world at the end. / Having fasted on the Indirā [fast] on the dark eleventh lunar day of Iṣa (Āśvina),

1.120.s:
śālagrāmaśilāgre tu madhyāhne śrāddhamācaret /
viṣṇoḥ prītikaraṃ vipra tataḥ prātarharerdine //
1.120.d:
शालग्रामशिलाग्रे तु मध्याह्ने श्राद्धमाचरेत् ।
विष्णोः प्रीतिकरं विप्र ततः प्रातर्हरेर्दिने ॥
1.120.m: one should perform an ancestral rite at midday in front of a śālagrāma stone, / pleasing to Viṣṇu, O Brahmin; then, in the morning on the day of Hari,

1.120.s:
padnanābhaṃ samabhyarcya bhūdevānbhojayetsudhīḥ /
visṛjya dakṣiṇāṃ datvā tāṃstato 'śnīta ca svayam //
1.120.d:
पद्ननाभं समभ्यर्च्य भूदेवान्भोजयेत्सुधीः ।
विसृज्य दक्षिणां दत्वा तांस्ततो ऽश्नीत च स्वयम् ॥
1.120.m: the wise man, having worshipped Padmanābha, should feed the gods of the earth (Brahmins); / having dismissed them after giving a priestly fee, he himself should then eat.

1.120.s:
evaṃ kṛtavrato martyo bhuktvā bhogānihepsitān /
pitṝṇāṃ koṭimuddhṛtya yātyante vaiṣṇavaṃ gṛham //
1.120.d:
एवं कृतव्रतो मर्त्यो भुक्त्वा भोगानिहेप्सितान् ।
पितॄणां कोटिमुद्धृत्य यात्यन्ते वैष्णवं गृहम् ॥
1.120.m: A mortal who has performed this vow, having enjoyed desired pleasures in this world / and lifted up ten million ancestors, goes at the end to the home of Viṣṇu.

1.120.s:
ekādaśyāmiṣe śukle vipra pāśāṅkuśāhvayām /
upoṣya vidhivadviṣṇordine viṣṇuṃ samarcayet //
1.120.d:
एकादश्यामिषे शुक्ले विप्र पाशाङ्कुशाह्वयाम् ।
उपोष्य विधिवद्विष्णोर्दिने विष्णुं समर्चयेत् ॥
1.120.m: On the bright eleventh lunar day of Iṣa, O Brahmin, having fasted according to rule / on the one named Pāśāṅkuśā, he should worship Viṣṇu on the day of Viṣṇu.

1.120.s:
tataḥ saṃbhojya viprāgryāndatvā tebhyaśca dakṣiṇām /
bhaktyā praṇamya visṛjedaśnīyācca svayaṃ tataḥ //
1.120.d:
ततः संभोज्य विप्राग्र्यान्दत्वा तेभ्यश्च दक्षिणाम् ।
भक्त्या प्रणम्य विसृजेदश्नीयाच्च स्वयं ततः ॥
1.120.m: Then, having fed the best of Brahmins and given them a priestly fee, / having bowed with devotion, he should dismiss them, and then eat himself.

1.120.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute bhaktyā naraḥ pāśāṅkuśāvratam /
sa bhuktveha varānbhogānyāti viṣṇoḥ salokatām //
1.120.d:
एवं यः कुरुते भक्त्या नरः पाशाङ्कुशाव्रतम् ।
स भुक्त्वेह वरान्भोगान्याति विष्णोः सलोकताम् ॥
1.120.m: The man who thus performs the Pāśāṅkuśā vow with devotion, / having enjoyed excellent pleasures in this world, goes to dwell in the same realm as Viṣṇu.

1.120.s:
kārtike kṛṣṇapakṣe tu ekādaśyāṃ dvijottama /
ramāmupoṣya vidhivaddvādaśyāṃ prātararcayet //
1.120.d:
कार्तिके कृष्णपक्षे तु एकादश्यां द्विजोत्तम ।
रमामुपोष्य विधिवद्द्वादश्यां प्रातरर्चयेत् ॥
1.120.m: In the dark fortnight of Kārtika, on the eleventh lunar day, O best of Brahmins, / having fasted on Ramā according to rule, he should worship in the morning on the twelfth lunar day

1.120.s:
keśavaṃ keśihṝntāraṃ devadevaṃ sanātanam /
bhojayecca tato viprānvisṛjellabdhadakṣiṇān //
1.120.d:
केशवं केशिहॄन्तारं देवदेवं सनातनम् ।
भोजयेच्च ततो विप्रान्विसृजेल्लब्धदक्षिणान् ॥
1.120.m: Keśava, the destroyer of Keśin, the eternal God of gods; / and then he should feed the Brahmins and dismiss them once they have received their priestly fees.

1.120.s:
evaṃ kṛtavrato vipra bhogānbhuktveha vāñchitān /
vyomayānena sāṃnidhyaṃ labhate ca ramāpateḥ //
1.120.d:
एवं कृतव्रतो विप्र भोगान्भुक्त्वेह वाञ्छितान् ।
व्योमयानेन सांनिध्यं लभते च रमापतेः ॥
1.120.m: Having thus performed the vow, O Brahmin, having enjoyed desired pleasures in this world, / he attains closeness to the husband of Ramā (Viṣṇu) by means of an aerial chariot.

1.120.s:
ūrjasya śuklaikādaśyāṃ samupoṣya prabodhinīm /
keśavaṃ bodhayedrātrau suptaṃ gītādimaṅgalaiḥ //
1.120.d:
ऊर्जस्य शुक्लैकादश्यां समुपोष्य प्रबोधिनीम् ।
केशवं बोधयेद्रात्रौ सुप्तं गीतादिमङ्गलैः ॥
1.120.m: Having fasted on the Prabodhinī on the bright eleventh lunar day of Ūrja (Kārtika), / he should awaken Keśava who is asleep at night with auspicious songs and other performances,

1.120.s:
ṛgyajuḥsāmamantraiśca vādyairnānāvidhairapi /
drākṣekṣudāḍimaiścānyai raṃbhāśṛṅgāṭakādibhiḥ //
1.120.d:
ऋग्यजुःसाममन्त्रैश्च वाद्यैर्नानाविधैरपि ।
द्राक्षेक्षुदाडिमैश्चान्यै रंभाशृङ्गाटकादिभिः ॥
1.120.m: and with Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman mantras, and also with various musical instruments, / with offerings of grapes, sugarcane, pomegranates, and other [fruits], such as plantains and water chestnuts.

1.120.s:
samarpaṇaistato rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ pare 'hani /
snātvā nityakriyāṃ kṛtvā gadādāmodaraṃ yajet //
1.120.d:
समर्पणैस्ततो रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां परे ऽहनि ।
स्नात्वा नित्यक्रियां कृत्वा गदादामोदरं यजेत् ॥
1.120.m: Then, the night having passed, on the next day, / having bathed and performed the daily rites, he should worship Damodara with the mace,

1.120.s:
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ pauruṣeṇāpi sūktataḥ /
saṃbhojya viprānvisṛjeddakṣiṇābhiḥ pratoṣitān //
1.120.d:
उपचारैः षोडशभिः पौरुषेणापि सूक्ततः ।
संभोज्य विप्रान्विसृजेद्दक्षिणाभिः प्रतोषितान् ॥
1.120.m: with sixteen offerings and also with the Puruṣasūkta; / having fed the Brahmins, he should dismiss them when they are pleased with priestly fees.

1.120.s:
tatastāṃ pratimāṃ haimīṃ sadhenuṃ guraver'payet /
evaṃ yaḥ kurute bhaktyā bodhinīvratamādṛtaḥ //
1.120.d:
ततस्तां प्रतिमां हैमीं सधेनुं गुरवेर्ऽपयेत् ।
एवं यः कुरुते भक्त्या बोधिनीव्रतमादृतः ॥
1.120.m: Then he should give that golden image, along with a cow, to the teacher. / The person who, full of reverence, thus performs the Bodhinī vow with devotion,

1.120.s:
sa bhuktveha varānbhogānvaiṣṇavaṃ labhate padam /
mārgasya kṛṣṇaikādaśyāmutpannāṃ samupoṣya vai //
1.120.d:
स भुक्त्वेह वरान्भोगान्वैष्णवं लभते पदम् ।
मार्गस्य कृष्णैकादश्यामुत्पन्नां समुपोष्य वै ॥
1.120.m: having enjoyed excellent pleasures in this world, obtains the abode of Viṣṇu. / Having fasted on the Utpannā on the dark eleventh lunar day of Mārga (Mārgaśīrṣa),

1.120.s:
dvādaśyāṃ kṛṣṇamabhyarcedgandhādyairupacārakaiḥ /
tataḥ saṃbhojya viprāgryāndatvā tebhyaśca dakṣiṇām //
1.120.d:
द्वादश्यां कृष्णमभ्यर्चेद्गन्धाद्यैरुपचारकैः ।
ततः संभोज्य विप्राग्र्यान्दत्वा तेभ्यश्च दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.120.m: he should worship Kṛṣṇa on the twelfth lunar day with perfumes and other offerings; / then, having fed the best of Brahmins and given them a priestly fee,

1.120.s:
visṛjya paścādbhuñjīta svayamiṣṭaiḥ samāhitaḥ /
evaṃ yo bhaktibhāvena utpannāvratamācaret //
1.120.d:
विसृज्य पश्चाद्भुञ्जीत स्वयमिष्टैः समाहितः ।
एवं यो भक्तिभावेन उत्पन्नाव्रतमाचरेत् ॥
1.120.m: and having dismissed them, he himself, composed in mind, should afterwards eat with his loved ones. / He who thus observes the Utpannā vow with an attitude of devotion,

1.120.s:
sa vimānaṃ samāruhya yātyante vaiṣṇavaṃ padam /
mārgasya śuklaikādaśyāṃ mokṣākhyāṃ samupoṣya vai //
1.120.d:
स विमानं समारुह्य यात्यन्ते वैष्णवं पदम् ।
मार्गस्य शुक्लैकादश्यां मोक्षाख्यां समुपोष्य वै ॥
1.120.m: having mounted an aerial chariot, goes at the end to the abode of Viṣṇu. / Having fasted on the one called Mokṣā on the bright eleventh lunar day of Mārga,

1.120.s:
dvādaśyāṃ prātarabhyarcya hyanantaṃ viśvarūpakam /
sarvairevopacāraistu viprānsaṃbhojayeddvijaḥ //
1.120.d:
द्वादश्यां प्रातरभ्यर्च्य ह्यनन्तं विश्वरूपकम् ।
सर्वैरेवोपचारैस्तु विप्रान्संभोजयेद्द्विजः ॥
1.120.m: having worshipped Ananta, whose form is the universe, in the morning of the twelfth day / with all services, the twice-born should feed brahmins.

1.120.s:
visṛjya dakṣiṇāṃ datvā svayaṃ bhuñjīta bāndhavaiḥ /
evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra bhuktvā bhogānihepsitān //
1.120.d:
विसृज्य दक्षिणां दत्वा स्वयं भुञ्जीत बान्धवैः ।
एवं कृत्वा व्रतं विप्र भुक्त्वा भोगानिहेप्सितान् ॥
1.120.m: Having dismissed them after giving a sacrificial fee, he should eat himself with his relatives. / Having thus performed the observance, O brahmin, and enjoyed desired pleasures in this world,

1.120.s:
daśa pūrvāndaśa parānsamuddhṛtya vrajeddharim /
paupasya kṛṣṇaikādaśyāṃ saphalāṃ samupoṣya vai /
dvādaśyāmacyutaṃ prārcya sarvairevopacārakaiḥ //
1.120.d:
दश पूर्वान्दश परान्समुद्धृत्य व्रजेद्धरिम् ।
पौपस्य कृष्णैकादश्यां सफलां समुपोष्य वै ।
द्वादश्यामच्युतं प्रार्च्य सर्वैरेवोपचारकैः ॥
1.120.m: having rescued ten ancestors and ten descendants, he goes to Hari. / Having fasted on the dark eleventh day of Pauṣa, [known as] Saphalā, / and worshipped Acyuta on the twelfth day with all services,

1.120.s:
saṃbhojya viprānmadhurairvisṛjellabdhadakṣiṇān /
evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra saphalāyā vidhānataḥ //
1.120.d:
संभोज्य विप्रान्मधुरैर्विसृजेल्लब्धदक्षिणान् ।
एवं कृत्वा व्रतं विप्र सफलाया विधानतः ॥
1.120.m: having fed the brahmins with sweets, one should dismiss them once they have received their sacrificial fees. / Having thus performed the observance of Saphalā according to rule, O brahmin,

1.120.s:
bhuktveha bhogānakhilānyātyante vaiṣṇavaṃ padam /
pauṣasya śuklaikādaśyāṃ putradāṃ samupoṣya vai //
1.120.d:
भुक्त्वेह भोगानखिलान्यात्यन्ते वैष्णवं पदम् ।
पौषस्य शुक्लैकादश्यां पुत्रदां समुपोष्य वै ॥
1.120.m: having enjoyed all pleasures in this world, he goes to the Vaiṣṇava abode at the end. / Having fasted on the bright eleventh day of Pauṣa, [known as] Putradā,

1.120.s:
dvādaśyāṃ cakriṇaṃ prāryedarghādyairupacārakaiḥ /
tataḥ saṃbhojya viprāgryāndatvā tebhyastu dakṣiṇām //
1.120.d:
द्वादश्यां चक्रिणं प्रार्येदर्घाद्यैरुपचारकैः ।
ततः संभोज्य विप्राग्र्यान्दत्वा तेभ्यस्तु दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.120.m: on the twelfth day one should worship the Bearer of the Discus with services such as water offering. / Then, having fed excellent brahmins and given them a sacrificial fee,

1.120.s:
visṛjya svayamaśnīyāccheṣānnaṃ sveṣṭabāndhavaiḥ /
evaṃ kṛtavrato vipra bhukvā bhogānihepsitān //
1.120.d:
विसृज्य स्वयमश्नीयाच्छेषान्नं स्वेष्टबान्धवैः ।
एवं कृतव्रतो विप्र भुक्वा भोगानिहेप्सितान् ॥
1.120.m: and dismissed them, he should eat the remaining food himself with his dear relatives. / Having observed this vow, O brahmin, and enjoyed desired pleasures in this world,

1.120.s:
vimānavaramāruhya yātyante harimandiram /
māghamya kṛṣṇaikādaśyāṃ ṣaṭtilāṃ samupoṣya vai //
1.120.d:
विमानवरमारुह्य यात्यन्ते हरिमन्दिरम् ।
माघम्य कृष्णैकादश्यां षट्तिलां समुपोष्य वै ॥
1.120.m: he ascends an excellent aerial chariot and goes at the end to the abode of Hari. / Having fasted on the dark eleventh day of Māgha, [known as] Ṣaṭtilā,

1.120.s:
snātvā datvā tarpayitvā hutvā bhuktvā samarcya ca /
tilaireva dvijaśreṣṭha dvādaśyāṃ prātareva hi //
1.120.d:
स्नात्वा दत्वा तर्पयित्वा हुत्वा भुक्त्वा समर्च्य च ।
तिलैरेव द्विजश्रेष्ठ द्वादश्यां प्रातरेव हि ॥
1.120.m: bathing, giving, offering libations, performing fire sacrifice, eating, and worshipping / with sesame seeds alone, O best of brahmins, early in the morning of the twelfth day,

1.120.s:
vaikuṇṭhaṃ samyagabhyarvya sarvairevopacārakaiḥ /
dvijānsaṃbhojya visṛjeddatvā tebhyaśca dakṣiṇām //
1.120.d:
वैकुण्ठं सम्यगभ्यर्व्य सर्वैरेवोपचारकैः ।
द्विजान्संभोज्य विसृजेद्दत्वा तेभ्यश्च दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.120.m: having fully worshipped Vaikuṇṭha with all services, / one should feed brahmins and dismiss them after giving them a sacrificial fee.

1.120.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra vidhinā susamāhitaḥ /
bhuktveha vāñchitānbhogānante viṣṇupadaṃ labhet //
1.120.d:
एवं कृत्वा व्रतं विप्र विधिना सुसमाहितः ।
भुक्त्वेह वाञ्छितान्भोगानन्ते विष्णुपदं लभेत् ॥
1.120.m: Having thus performed the observance according to rule, concentrated in mind, O brahmin, / and enjoyed desired pleasures in this world, he attains the abode of Viṣṇu at the end.

1.120.s:
māghasya śuklaikādaśyāṃ samupoṣya jayāhvayām /
prātarhari dine 'bhyarccecchrīpatiṃ puruṣaṃ dvija //
1.120.d:
माघस्य शुक्लैकादश्यां समुपोष्य जयाह्वयाम् ।
प्रातर्हरि दिने ऽभ्यर्च्चेच्छ्रीपतिं पुरुषं द्विज ॥
1.120.m: Having fasted on the bright eleventh day of Māgha, named Jayā, / one should worship the Puruṣa, the Lord of Śrī, on the morning of Hari’s day, O brahmin.

1.120.s:
bhojayitvā dakṣiṇāṃ ca datvā viprānvisṛjya ca /
svayaṃ bhuñjīta taccheṣaṃ prayato nijabāndhavaiḥ //
1.120.d:
भोजयित्वा दक्षिणां च दत्वा विप्रान्विसृज्य च ।
स्वयं भुञ्जीत तच्छेषं प्रयतो निजबान्धवैः ॥
1.120.m: Having fed and given a sacrificial fee to the brahmins and dismissed them, / he should eat the remainder himself, restrained, together with his own relatives.

1.120.s:
ya evaṃ kurute vipra vrataṃ keśavatoṣaṇam /
sa bhuktveha varānbhogānante viṣṇoḥ padaṃ vrajet //
1.120.d:
य एवं कुरुते विप्र व्रतं केशवतोषणम् ।
स भुक्त्वेह वरान्भोगानन्ते विष्णोः पदं व्रजेत् ॥
1.120.m: Whoever performs this observance that pleases Keśava, O brahmin, / he, having enjoyed excellent pleasures here, goes to the abode of Viṣṇu at the end.

1.120.s:
tapasyakṛṣṇaikādaśyāṃ vijayāṃ samupoṣya vai /
dvādaśyāṃ prātarabhyarcya yogīśaṃ gandhapūrvakaiḥ //
1.120.d:
तपस्यकृष्णैकादश्यां विजयां समुपोष्य वै ।
द्वादश्यां प्रातरभ्यर्च्य योगीशं गन्धपूर्वकैः ॥
1.120.m: Having fasted on the dark eleventh day of Tapasya, [known as] Vijayā, / and worshipped the Lord of Yogins in the morning of the twelfth day with perfumes and other offerings,

1.120.s:
tataḥ saṃbhojya bhūdevāndakṣiṇābhiḥ pratoṣya tān /
visṛjya bāndhavaiḥ sārddhaṃ svayamaśnīta vāgyataḥ //
1.120.d:
ततः संभोज्य भूदेवान्दक्षिणाभिः प्रतोष्य तान् ।
विसृज्य बान्धवैः सार्द्धं स्वयमश्नीत वाग्यतः ॥
1.120.m: then feeding the earthly gods and pleasing them with sacrificial fees, / and dismissing them, he should eat himself in silence together with his relatives.

1.120.s:
evaṃ kṛtavrato martyo bhuktvā bhogānihepsitān /
dehānte vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ yāti devaiḥ susatkṛtaḥ //
1.120.d:
एवं कृतव्रतो मर्त्यो भुक्त्वा भोगानिहेप्सितान् ।
देहान्ते वैष्णवं लोकं याति देवैः सुसत्कृतः ॥
1.120.m: A mortal who has thus performed the observance, having enjoyed desired pleasures in this world, / goes to the Vaiṣṇava world at the end of the body, highly honored by the gods.

1.120.s:
phaālgunasya site pakṣe ekādaśyāṃ dvijottama /
upoṣyāmalakīṃ bhaktyā dvādaśyāṃ prātararcayet //
1.120.d:
फआल्गुनस्य सिते पक्षे एकादश्यां द्विजोत्तम ।
उपोष्यामलकीं भक्त्या द्वादश्यां प्रातरर्चयेत् ॥
1.120.m: In the bright fortnight of Phālguna, on the eleventh day, O best of brahmins, / having fasted on Āmalakī with devotion, one should worship in the morning of the twelfth day

1.120.s:
puṇḍarīkākṣamakhilairupacāraistato dvijān /
bhojayitvā varānnena dadyāttebhyastu dakṣiṇām //
1.120.d:
पुण्डरीकाक्षमखिलैरुपचारैस्ततो द्विजान् ।
भोजयित्वा वरान्नेन दद्यात्तेभ्यस्तु दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.120.m: the Lotus-eyed One with all services; then, having fed the brahmins / with excellent food, one should give them a sacrificial fee.

1.120.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā vidhānenāmalakyāṃ pūjanādikam /
sitaikādaśyāṃ tapasye vrajedviṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam //
1.120.d:
एवं कृत्वा विधानेनामलक्यां पूजनादिकम् ।
सितैकादश्यां तपस्ये व्रजेद्विष्णोः परं पदम् ॥
1.120.m: Having thus performed the worship and other rites according to rule on the Āmalakī / bright eleventh day in Tapasya, one goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

1.120.s:
caitrasya kṛṣṇaikādaśīṃ pāpamocanikāṃ dvija /
upāṣya dvādaśyāṃprātargovindaṃ pūjayettathā //
1.120.d:
चैत्रस्य कृष्णैकादशीं पापमोचनिकां द्विज ।
उपाष्य द्वादश्यांप्रातर्गोविन्दं पूजयेत्तथा ॥
1.120.m: Fasting on the dark eleventh [day] of Caitra, [called] Pāpamocanikā, O twice-born one, / one should then worship Govinda in the morning on the twelfth [day],

1.120.s:
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirdvijānsaṃbhojya dakṣiṇām /
datvā tebhyo visṛjyātha svayaṃ bhuñjīta bāndhavaiḥ //
1.120.d:
उपचारैः षोडशभिर्द्विजान्संभोज्य दक्षिणाम् ।
दत्वा तेभ्यो विसृज्याथ स्वयं भुञ्जीत बान्धवैः ॥
1.120.m: with sixteen offerings. Having fed twice-born ones, giving a priestly gift / to them, and dismissing [them], one should then eat oneself with relatives.

1.120.s:
eva yaḥ kurute vipra pāpamocanikāvratām /
sa yāti vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ vimānena tu bhāsvatā //
1.120.d:
एव यः कुरुते विप्र पापमोचनिकाव्रताम् ।
स याति वैष्णवं लोकं विमानेन तु भास्वता ॥
1.120.m: He who observes the vow of Pāpamocanikā in this way, O Brahmin, / goes to the realm of Viṣṇu in a shining aerial chariot.

1.120.s:
itthaṃ kṛṣṇo tathā śukle vrataṃ caikādaśībhavam /
mokṣadaṃ kīrtitaṃ vipra nāstyasminsaṃśayaḥ kvacit //
1.120.d:
इत्थं कृष्णो तथा शुक्ले व्रतं चैकादशीभवम् ।
मोक्षदं कीर्तितं विप्र नास्त्यस्मिन्संशयः क्वचित् ॥
1.120.m: Thus the vow observed on the eleventh [day], both in the dark and bright [fortnights], / has been proclaimed to grant liberation, O Brahmin; there is no doubt about this anywhere.

1.120.s:
yatastridinasaṃsādhyaṃ kīrtinaṃ pāpanāśanam /
sarvavratottamaṃ vipra tato jñeyaṃ mahāphalam //
1.120.d:
यतस्त्रिदिनसंसाध्यं कीर्तिनं पापनाशनम् ।
सर्वव्रतोत्तमं विप्र ततो ज्ञेयं महाफलम् ॥
1.120.m: Because it is accomplished over three days and is proclaimed to destroy sin, / O Brahmin, it is known to be the best of all vows, possessing great fruit.

1.120.s:
tyajeccatvāri bhuktāni nāradai taddinatraye /
ādyantayorekamekaṃ madhyame dvayameva hi //
1.120.d:
त्यजेच्चत्वारि भुक्तानि नारदै तद्दिनत्रये ।
आद्यन्तयोरेकमेकं मध्यमे द्वयमेव हि ॥
1.120.m: On these three days, O Nārada, one must abandon four meals: / one each on the first and last [days], and indeed two on the middle [day].

1.120.s:
atha te niyamānvacmi vrate hyasmindinatraye /
kāṃsyaṃ māṃsaṃ masūrānnaṃ caṇakānkodravāṃstathā //
1.120.d:
अथ ते नियमान्वच्मि व्रते ह्यस्मिन्दिनत्रये ।
कांस्यं मांसं मसूरान्नं चणकान्कोद्रवांस्तथा ॥
1.120.m: Now I shall tell you the restrictions during these three days in the vow: / bell-metal, meat, lentils, chickpeas, and kodrava grains,

1.120.s:
śākaṃ madhu parānnaṃ ca punarbhojanamaithune /
daśamyāṃ daśa vastūni varjayedvaiṣṇavaṛ sadā //
1.120.d:
शाकं मधु परान्नं च पुनर्भोजनमैथुने ।
दशम्यां दश वस्तूनि वर्जयेद्वैष्णवऋ सदा ॥
1.120.m: vegetables, honey, another's food, eating a second time, and sexual intercourse; / on the tenth [day], a Vaiṣṇava must always avoid [these] ten things.

1.120.s:
dyūtakrīḍāṃ ca nidrāṃ ca tāṃbūlaṃ dantadhāvanam /
parāpavādaṃ paiśunyaṃ steyaṃ hiṃsāṃ tathā ratim //
1.120.d:
द्यूतक्रीडां च निद्रां च तांबूलं दन्तधावनम् ।
परापवादं पैशुन्यं स्तेयं हिंसां तथा रतिम् ॥
1.120.m: Gambling, sleep, betel, brushing the teeth, / speaking ill of others, slander, theft, injury, and sexual enjoyment,

1.120.s:
kopaṃ hyanṛtavākyaṃ ca ekādaśyāṃ vivarjjayet /
kāṃsyaṃ māṃsaṃ surāṃ kṣaudraṃ tailaṃ viṇmlecchabhāṣaṇam //
1.120.d:
कोपं ह्यनृतवाक्यं च एकादश्यां विवर्ज्जयेत् ।
कांस्यं मांसं सुरां क्षौद्रं तैलं विण्म्लेच्छभाषणम् ॥
1.120.m: anger, and speaking falsehood—these one must avoid on the eleventh [day]. / Bell-metal, meat, wine, honey, oil, speaking while defecating, speaking with barbarians,

1.120.s:
vyāyāmaṃ ca pravāsaṃ ca punarbhojanamaithune /
aspṛśyasparśamāśūre dvādaśyāṃ dvādaśa tyajet //
1.120.d:
व्यायामं च प्रवासं च पुनर्भोजनमैथुने ।
अस्पृश्यस्पर्शमाशूरे द्वादश्यां द्वादश त्यजेत् ॥
1.120.m: exercise, travel, eating a second time, sexual intercourse, / and touching what is untouchable—on the twelfth [day], a brave man must abandon [these] twelve.

1.120.s:
evaṃ niyamakṛdvipra upavāsaṃ samācaret /
śakto 'śaktustu matimānekabhuktaṃ na naktakam //
1.120.d:
एवं नियमकृद्विप्र उपवासं समाचरेत् ।
शक्तो ऽशक्तुस्तु मतिमानेकभुक्तं न नक्तकम् ॥
1.120.m: Observing these rules in this way, O Brahmin, one who is capable should fast; / but one who is incapable, if wise, [should eat] a single meal, not an evening meal;

1.120.s:
ayācitaṃ vāpi carenna tyajedvratamīdṛśam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīya purāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthabhāge dvādaśamāsastitaikādaśīvratakathanaṃ nāma viṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.120.d:
अयाचितं वापि चरेन्न त्यजेद्व्रतमीदृशम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीय पुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थभागे द्वादशमासस्तितैकादशीव्रतकथनं नाम विंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.120.m:
or he may observe [the vow by eating] unasked food; he must not abandon such a vow.

Thus ends the one hundred and twentieth chapter, named "Account of the Vows of the Eleventh Day in the Twelve Months," in the Fourth Part of the Major Narrative in the First Section of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.
